author.name: Liyan Tan, Yequan Zhao, Ziyue Liu, Yupeng Su, Ruijie Zhang, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: MobileSpec trains lightweight LLM specialists directly on user devices using only forward passes, avoiding the memory cost of backpropagation, and learns from automatically verified task outcomes in an RLVR-like fashion. Its key insight is shaping random perturbations to resemble weight changes induced by RLVR, enabling efficient forward-only updates. This targets the practical goal of personalizing on-device models without sending user data to the cloud.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction at Performative Equilibrium: The Price of Performativity

author.name: Ahmed Mahrous, Roberto Di Pietro

entry.summary: Studies conformal prediction when the deployed predictor itself shifts the data distribution, seeking prediction sets valid at performative equilibrium. It proves a phase transition at distribution-map sensitivity L=1: below it, minimax excess miscoverage is characterized, while above it no finite-sample procedure can guarantee both valid coverage and nontrivial sets.

entry.title: ReListen: Training-Free Evidence Localization in Hour-Long Audio with Frozen Audio Language Models

author.name: Ming-Hao Hsu, Shujie Liu, Yuxuan Hu, Yuxiang Wang, Yingda Shen, Jinyu Li, Zhizheng Wu

entry.summary: ReListen is a training-free method where a frozen audio language model scans hour-long recordings in 20-second windows, scoring each by its probability of answering the question, then answers from the highest-scoring minute. It localizes annotated evidence far better than transcript retrieval (88.5% overlap on VoiceGiraffe questions) without any additional training.

entry.title: LiSA: Linear Stochastic Attention for Long-Range Visual Modeling

author.name: Sahar Dastani, Fereshteh Shakeri, Samuel Barbeau, Kunal Mahatha, Ismail Ben Ayed, Herve Lombaert, Christian Desrosiers

entry.summary: LiSA is a plug-in linear attention module that captures higher-order token interactions via a stochastic diffusion process based on truncated random walks, addressing the expressivity limits of first-order kernel-approximation linear attention while retaining linear cost. It targets long-range visual modeling.

entry.title: Physical Diffusion Policy via MPM-Guided 3D Gaussian Simulation

author.name: Can Wang, Qiyuan Qiao, Lei Liu, Ge Yuan, Xinhui Liu, Dong Xu

entry.summary: The paper augments diffusion policies with object physical understanding by recovering material properties from visual demonstrations via 3D Gaussian Splatting coupled with differentiable Material Point Method simulation, using video guidance and particle-level constraints. This lets the policy reason about heterogeneous deformation and contact dynamics of everyday objects rather than producing averaged actions.

entry.title: WayTrace: A Map-to-Language-to-Trace Hierarchy for Embodied Urban Navigation

author.name: Manthan Patel, Jonas Frey, Pascal Roth, Marco Hutter, Cesar Cadena

entry.summary: WayTrace is a hierarchical urban navigation system where a vision-language model orchestrator reads web-map turn-by-turn directions, a satellite map, and camera images to issue atomic language commands, while an onboard trace predictor trained on over a million automatically labeled street-level images executes them. This bridges reliable web walking directions and robust robot motion without heavy dependence on GNSS.

entry.title: EMBERS: Empirically Motivated Robustness Testing of Deep Research Systems via Defect-Guided Fuzzing

author.name: Shuochuan Li, Zan Wang, Dong Wang, Yuhang Jiang, Huajin Cui, Chen Zhang, Gang Wang, Junjie Chen

entry.summary: EMBERS empirically studies 1,932 execution trajectories from three representative deep research systems, identifies nine recurring defect categories, and uses them to guide fuzzing for robustness testing. It addresses underexplored intrinsic weaknesses in multi-stage research pipelines, where input variations propagate across stages into wrong answers.

entry.title: The Evolution Strategies Paradox: Better Models from Worse Perturbations

author.name: Roberto Dailey, Kajetan Schweighofer, Jamieson Warner, Conor F. Hayes, Elliot Meyerson, Babak Hodjat, Risto Miikkulainen, Xin Qiu

entry.summary: This paper characterizes a paradox in using evolution strategies to fine-tune billion-parameter LLMs: all offspring can perform worse than the parent, yet the parent consistently improves during training, across models, tasks, and modalities. The authors explain it via high-dimensional local reward landscape properties where exploration worsens performance but still highlights good ascent directions.

entry.title: Embodied AI for Scientific Discovery: From Physical Action to Scientific Evidence

author.name: Wenhao Xu, Changwei Wang, Shunpeng Chen, Yukun Song, Sifan Zhou, Kaize Luo, Shibiao Xu, Yuehua Zhao, Rongtao Xu

entry.summary: A review unifying robot learning and AI-for-science under the framing of embodied AI for science, treating the partially observed experiment as the core problem with latent states, costly irreversible actions, and outcome-dependent missingness. It organizes the literature via three closures: operational, epistemic, and presumably inferential, spanning from intended action to evidence-based belief updates. The framing could structure a fast-growing interdisciplinary field.

entry.title: Kierston & KierstonBench: Simulation of Allentown, PA and Evaluation of Language Models in Crime Investigation and Surveillance Tasks

author.name: Andrew Semenov, Svyatoslav Dorofeev

entry.summary: The paper presents Kierston, a city-scale simulation engine modeling roughly 125,000 Allentown, Pennsylvania residents and generating the telecommunications, financial, administrative, and license-plate records surveillance systems collect, plus KierstonBench, which scores LLM capability and accuracy in crime investigation and mass surveillance tasks against known simulated ground truth.

entry.title: Artifact-to-Capability: Diagnosing Breaks in Capability Formation of Self-Evolving Agents in a Controlled Environment

author.name: Ziqian Ban, Haoxiang Yang, Yanfei Zhang, Shixin Liang, Haoran Yu, Xu Lin, Shaobin Zhao, Xuran Li, Zhiyi Cheng

entry.summary: This paper defines capability formation from artifacts for self-evolving agents as five sequentially dependent properties and introduces a three-scale diagnosis framework (state, game, lineage levels). Testing Reflexion, Voyager, and DGM on freestyle Gomoku shows all display surface signals of improvement (artifact accumulation, behavior change, metric gains) while still exhibiting breaks in genuine capability formation.

entry.title: From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?

author.name: Jeremy Qin, Ruizhi Deng, Mohamed Osama Ahmed, Frederick Tung, Leo Feng

entry.summary: The paper introduces Continual AutoResearch, an open-ended environment comparing persistent versus reset agent instances under matched task streams across nine task families including symbolic regression, forecasting, and tabular AutoML. It measures whether autoresearch agents can retain and apply insights across tasks, addressing a cost and capability blind spot in prior evaluations that start fresh each session.

entry.title: The Web Doesn't Sit Still: Adversarial Self-Evolving Attacks on Search Agents

author.name: Geyuan Wang, Shunyu Liu, Siyuan Liang, Chenyang Lyu, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: The paper proposes an adversarial self-evolution framework for attacking LLM-based web search agents, using bi-level optimization that jointly evolves attacker strategies and defender mitigations to expose vulnerabilities beyond static hand-crafted injection templates. This better emulates dynamic real-world web threats against information-seeking agents.

entry.title: What Is the Influence of Task Order in Continual Learning? An Empirical Study and Order-Aware Evaluation for Motion Forecasting

author.name: Zirui Li, Yunlong Lin, Haohan Yang, Xiaocong Zhao, Chen Lv

entry.summary: The authors formulate continual learning comparison as an expectation over a declared task-order distribution and evaluate 288 runs across four road-layout motion forecasting tasks and all 24 task orders. Task order explains 65-91% of variation in current-task error and backward transfer, with 90-99% attributable to the identity of the starting task.

entry.title: ReSI-Math: Exploring Recoverable Capability Frontiers for Efficient Reasoning Improvement

author.name: Yao Cui, Zhen Yang, Yuandong Wang, Yangfu Zhu, Tianyu Wo, Zhenzhou Shao

entry.summary: The paper shows that when an LLM fails to solve a math problem, it does not necessarily lack the capability: some failures are recoverable via trajectory-level search over the model's own generations, defining a recoverable capability frontier. ReSI-Math exploits this frontier to construct more efficient RL with verifiable rewards for reasoning improvement.

entry.title: Trajectory Evaluation via Rollout-Free World Model for End-to-end Autonomous Driving

author.name: Junzhe Wang, Jinqing Zhang, Qingjie Liu

entry.summary: RFWorld is a rollout-free world model for end-to-end autonomous driving that evaluates candidate trajectories without explicitly predicting future scenes for each candidate. It builds a shared scene memory shaped into a future-readable representation, avoiding the high inference cost and error accumulation of rollout-based evaluators. This improves the efficiency-accuracy tradeoff for planning.

entry.title: Going Deeper With Memories

author.name: Afshin Khadangi

entry.summary: DeepMem is a causal multiscale architecture for byte-level language modeling that separates semantic compression from exact byte preservation, using a learned invertible subband transform, lossless carrier and detail sidebands, fast-weight memory blocks, and an attention-based super-resolution decoder. It outperforms a matched byte-level transformer on FineWeb, addressing the cost of processing every byte at full resolution. The design targets tokenizer-free modeling without the usual efficiency penalty.

entry.title: Forget What Comes Next: LLM Unlearning via Statistical Independence

author.name: Andrii Shkabrii, Claudia Plant, Martin Pawelczyk

entry.summary: PINT is a machine unlearning algorithm that uses the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion to reduce statistical dependence between tokens to be forgotten and the internal representations predicting them, with a formal connection to exact memorization via a computable upper bound. It is motivated by the observation that poisoned examples can remain statistically detectable after conventional unlearning.

entry.title: Structure, Dimensionality, and Distribution Shape - What Makes Pretraining Data Transferable, and Why the Input Pipeline Decides Which

author.name: Sangyoon Bae, Jiook Cha

entry.summary: This work proposes a Transfer-Invariance Principle: whether a corpus property (structure, dimensionality, or distribution shape) matters for transfer depends on the model's input transform rather than the data modality. The authors build TransferForge, a synthetic-data generator that prescribes these properties, and show concrete cases where standardization makes distribution shape inert while other pipelines make it decisive. This gives a principled lens on pretraining-data design beyond intuition.

entry.title: Curriculum unlearning in humans and neural networks

author.name: Jirko Rubruck, Alice Zhang, Andrew Saxe, Christopher Summerfield

entry.summary: Using a behavioral task and neural network modeling, the authors develop and test a theory of why simple-to-complex curricula help learning: both humans and networks show simplicity biases with compressed representations, and curricula help overcome this compression. They confirm predictions about the representational dimensionality developed under different curricula.

entry.title: Beyond Multi-Index Models: Learning Intersections of Degree-2 PTFs

author.name: Ilias Diakonikolas, Daniel M. Kane, Mingchen Ma, Lisheng Ren, Trung Tran

entry.summary: The paper gives a PAC learning algorithm for intersections of k degree-2 polynomial threshold functions under Gaussian distributions, achieving d^{O(k)} time and samples with 2^{O_k(log^3(1/epsilon))} dependence on accuracy, improving on polynomial regression's d^{O(k^2/epsilon^2)}. It is the first result with dimension exponent independent of the accuracy parameter, even for k=2, and includes a matching SQ lower bound showing d^{Omega(k)} is unavoidable. Strong theoretical learning theory from a leading group.

entry.title: iGC: Antibody Optimization via Reinforcement Learning over a Learned Somatic Hypermutation Prior

author.name: Thao Nguyen, Robert G. Alberstein, Ewa Nowara, Homa MohammadiPeyhani, Holly R. Steach, Sarah A. Robinson, Yuval Shechter, Donald W. Lee, Jason A. Vander Heiden, Franziska Seeger, Andrew Leaver-Fay, Richard Bonneau, Joshua Yao-Yu Lin

entry.summary: iGC is a two-stage RL framework for antigen-specific antibody optimization: stage one learns a somatic hypermutation prior from B-cell lineage trees and adapts it to targets, and stage two optimizes binding while keeping mutation trajectories biologically plausible. This bridges the gap between realistic mutation modeling and affinity optimization in silico germinal centers.

entry.title: EpiLoRA: Fusing Many LoRA Adapters into Low-Precision GEMMs for Serving and RL

author.name: Hieu Tran, Hong Yu

entry.summary: EpiLoRA is a vLLM plugin that fuses LoRA adapter down-projections into the epilogue of low-precision (FP8/4-bit) base-model GEMMs, eliminating separate small kernels whose latency grows as a share of decoding steps in multi-tenant serving. The key insight is that the GEMM only needs the down-projection at output-writing time, enabling fused execution for serving and reinforcement learning workloads.

entry.title: Regret-based Characterization, Information Limits, and the Sample Complexity of Auditing Adaptive Policies

author.name: Irene Aldridge

entry.summary: Characterizes the adaptivity gap of Markov policies in finite-horizon MDPs, showing the value difference between a policy and its open-loop marginal equals a sum of covariances, bounded by the information the policy uses. It derives sharp sample complexity results for estimating this gap from bandit-feedback logs, with implications for auditing adaptive decision-making systems.

entry.title: PACT: Certifying What Is Written in Parallel Decoding of Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yanchao Li, Yusu Zhang, Jiaqing Xie, Yi Ban, Ben Gao, Zhongyu Huang, Tianfan Fu, Yuqiang Li

entry.summary: Proposes PACT, a training-free commit rule for parallel decoding in masked diffusion language models that draws tokens first and certifies the set before writing, spacing step positions apart. The certificate holds at every temperature and the paper argues no rule with the same guarantee commits more positions, with experiments on LLaDA-family models.

entry.title: Do Multi-Turn Conversational Capabilities Carry Over from Text to Speech? A Parallel Multilingual Benchmark

author.name: Jiaming Zhou, Pei Zhang, Shiwan Zhao, Zhijun Wang, Baosong Yang, Yong Qin

entry.summary: The authors present Omnilingua-AudioMC, a strictly parallel multilingual extension of Audio MultiChallenge with 354 conversations and 1,404 rubric items across ten languages, to test whether multi-turn conversational abilities transfer from text to spoken input. The aligned design lets researchers isolate whether speech modality degrades state tracking, instruction following, and revision handling.

entry.title: Sketch-Omni: Instance-Level Sketch-Based Visual Prompting for Perception MLLMs

author.name: Dongyu Wang, Dar-Yen Chen, Zhiming Hong, Arkaprabha Basu, Yi-Zhe Song

entry.summary: Sketch-Omni is claimed to be the first perception MLLM built to work on sketches and from them: sketches serve both as the image to be analyzed and as visual prompts that localize objects in photographs, even distinguishing among several instances of the same category where text or photo exemplars fall short. It addresses the photo-training bias of existing promptable perception models.

entry.title: Is Forgetting Unified? Exploring Concept Unlearning in Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Zhongkai Xue, Junkai Chen, Mingcong Lei, Rumo Zhang, Yixiao Liu, Zhimin Sun, Shu Wu, Qiang Liu, Lihua Zhang, Liang Wang

entry.summary: Studies cross-pathway concept unlearning in unified multimodal models that both generate and understand images, introducing UUBench with 30 target and 60 neighboring concepts. Finds that single-pathway unlearning methods strongly suppress generation of target concepts but produce limited forgetting on the understanding side, exposing an unsolved safety gap.

entry.title: Phase-DGS: Phase-guided Dynamic Gaussian Splatting from Unsynchronized Multi-view Video

author.name: Hosung Jeon, Jun Young Jeong, Sangwoon Kwak, Joonsoo Kim, Sangmin Kim, Jaesik Park, Won-Sik Cheong, Hyon-Gon Choo

entry.summary: Replaces timestamps with a semantic motion-phase representation so dynamic Gaussian splatting reconstruction works from unsynchronized multi-view cameras without specialized sync hardware. Frames at the same motion state share a phase regardless of capture camera.

entry.title: OCR in the Foundation Model Era: From Specialist Models to Unified Models

author.name: Zhiheng Li, Zongyang Ma, Jiaxian Chen, Cheng Cui, Yi Liu, Ziqi Zhang, Chunfeng Yuan, Bing Li, Xiang Bai, Weiming Hu

entry.summary: A survey tracing OCR development from specialist models to unified foundation models, defining OCR as faithful, visually verifiable transcription and organizing contemporary systems across detection-recognition, structured sequence generation, and vision-language model approaches. Includes respected authors in the document analysis community.

entry.title: When Cell Crops Share a Parent: Measuring and Isolating Acquisition Leakage in Cervical Cytology Benchmarks

author.name: Snehasish Ghosh, Soham Mitra, Antareep Majumdar, KC Santosh, Nibaran Das

entry.summary: This preregistered study shows that crop-level train/test splits in public cervical cytology benchmarks cause acquisition leakage, with sibling cell crops from the same slide inflating accuracy by up to 12 points on CRIC. Through factorial analyses it isolates the gain to sibling exposure and quantifies decodable parent identity in features.

entry.title: Online Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability Onboard the Robot Control Loop: A Real-Time GPU Solver for Safety-Critical Autonomy

author.name: Kevin Weekly, Alexandre M. Bayen

entry.summary: This work presents a CUDA implementation of the canonical WENO5 + TVD-RK3 + Lax-Friedrichs Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs level-set solver for 2D-4D dynamics that is fast enough to run inside a robot control loop. Since HJ reachability provides certified backward reachable tubes, this enables a deterministic safety layer with formal guarantees around black-box learned policies in ADAS, humanoids, and VLA systems.

entry.title: HiLo-WAM: Decoupling Long-Horizon Task Evolution and Local Dynamics in World Action Models

author.name: Xingyu Wang, Yanjiang Guo, Zhijing Ding, Jiaxin Fang, Zeyu Lai, Jiayu Dong, Weikang Wan, Jianyu Chen, Yuxiang Gao, Mengdi Xu

entry.summary: HiLo-WAM is a World Action Model architecture for robotic manipulation that decouples long-horizon task evolution from dense local visual dynamics, using a sparse long-horizon visual stream for historical task context and a dense local stream for fine-grained interactions. By jointly modeling both streams with robot actions, it avoids the uncertainty and computation blowup that comes from naively extending prediction horizons. This aims to improve manipulation policies that need both local precision and long-range task understanding.

entry.title: WASP-Mem: Let Agent Organize Procedural Memory. Human Spend Effort on Diagnosis

author.name: Peizhi Niu, Ge Shi, Vaibhav Gorde, Sarthak Ghosh, Christos Faloutsos, Min Cheng, Kevin Chen

entry.summary: WASP-Mem distills agent execution traces and feedback into persistent, interlinked wiki pages as procedural memory, enabling continual agent learning without retraining for complex enterprise procedures. On TheAgentCompany benchmark it raises task performance by consolidating repeated successes and diagnosed failures into reusable actions and recovery strategies.

entry.title: Reliability Stress Testing of RAG Retrieval under Query-Relevant Corpus Poisoning

author.name: Janet Sung, Kainan Zhou, Gangzhen Qian, Hang Xiao, Lu Yi

entry.summary: This paper systematically stress tests the retrieval admission step of RAG systems under query-targeted corpus poisoning, varying document content, attacker query knowledge, poison budget, and contamination scope; five query-targeted documents per query reduce classical-retriever nDCG@10 by 40-62% across BEIR queries. It quantifies how easily attackers achieve 100% target exposure with small budgets, highlighting a practical RAG security weakness.

entry.title: ScamWorld: An Interactive Environment for Evaluating Web Agents Against Online Fraud

author.name: Yutao Wu, Xiao Liu, Ming Wen, Hanxun Huang, Jun Wang, Xingjun Ma

entry.summary: ScamWorld is an interactive environment that reconstructs reported scam websites across diverse fraud scenarios, mechanisms, and languages to systematically evaluate how web agents respond to online fraud during task execution. It addresses the difficulty that scam sites are short-lived, enabling repeatable study of agent susceptibility to human-targeted fraud beyond prompt injections.

entry.title: LatentTriad: Pre-Action Risk Representations for Malicious Agent Skill Detection

author.name: Zhe Yu, Yi Liu, Ying Zhang, Simin Chen

entry.summary: LatentTriad detects malicious reusable agent skills before execution by reading task-operation consistency information from hidden states formed during prefill, combining boundary features, operation directions, and baseline departures. This avoids both shallow pattern matching and the cost of dynamically executing untrusted skills, generalizing across held-out expression forms in controlled evaluations.

entry.title: Dr. No: Feature Steering for Abstention in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Farid Hasanov, Riccardo Renzulli, Bahram Zonooz, Mykola Pechenizkiy, Decebal Constantin Mocanu

entry.summary: Dr. No mines sparse autoencoder features associated with abstention and commitment in a vision-language model and modulates a small set of them during the prefill pass, enabling abstention control without retraining. Evaluated on LLaVA-1.6 Mistral 7B across multimodal abstention benchmarks, it shows inference-time steering can improve trustworthy behavior in insufficient-evidence situations.

entry.title: On the Feature Evolution of Temporal Difference Learning

author.name: Shangzhe Li, Dechen Zhang, Difan Zou, Weitong Zhang

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes how predictive features emerge and propagate under temporal-difference learning, using finite-width two-layer ReLU critics on constructed stochastic-horizon MDPs. It shows that informative TD updates acquire the quadratic Bellman signal and that simultaneous hidden-weight and head updates yield strictly better finite-sample prediction risk than head-only SGD, with provably larger progress. This advances theoretical understanding of representation learning in reinforcement learning.

entry.title: A Universal Raw-IQ Radar Encoder for Cross-Sensor Human Sensing

author.name: Jonas Leo Mueller, Dario Zanca, Sebastian Hoefler, Jan Petermann, Thomas Altstidl, Naga Venkata Sai Jitin Jami, Emmanuelle Salin, Bjoern M. Eskofier

entry.summary: The paper argues micro-Doppler spectrograms transfer poorly across radar hardware because the Doppler axis rescales with carrier frequency and angular information is discarded. The authors pretrain a convolutional beta-VAE on clutter-removed raw radar measurements from four platforms (60 and 77 GHz, 4-12 antennas) on a unified spectral grid, keeping the encoder frozen for all downstream tasks.

entry.title: iMED: A Multi-Endoscope Dataset for Surgical 3D Perception

author.name: Sierra Bonilla, Fengyi Jiang, Chinedu Nwoye, Jingpei Lu, Kailey Reardon, Humphrey W. Chow, Francisco Vasconcelos, Sophia Bano, Adam Schmidt, Omid Mohareri

entry.summary: Releases iMED, the first synchronized multi-endoscope dataset for robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery with 340 sequences and about 170K synchronized timepoints from two independent stereo endoscopes across ex vivo, postmortem, and live settings. It enables distinguishing geometric generalization from photometric interpolation in surgical vision benchmarks.

entry.title: M\"obius: A Unified Motion-Language Model Bridging Understanding and Generation

author.name: Jiazhi Shu, Chengfeng Zhao, Jinyi Wang, Yubo Zhao, Zhiyang Dou, Ronghui Li, Yu Lu, Xinwei Jiang, Zijiao Zeng, Yuan Liu

entry.summary: Moebius is a unified motion-language model that brings the entire diffusion process into the same multimodal representation space used for motion understanding, with clean motion, noisy motion, and text jointly attending in shared attention. It operates directly on continuous frame-level raw motion without discrete tokenization and supports understanding, generation, and editing in one framework.

entry.title: Spectrally Routed Diffusion Policy for Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Mingcong Li, Yihan Zhou, Jiayu Qu, Xueyang Guo, Yilin Mo

entry.summary: SR-DP addresses the gap between joint multi-task diffusion policies and per-task specialists by attacking two failure modes: non-discriminative visual conditioning from convolutional encoders and destructive gradient interference in the shared denoiser. It uses a frozen VGGT encoder with a spatial-compression adapter for compact multi-scale semantic features and a spectral routing scheme to separate incompatible action-mode gradients.

entry.title: VagueBench: Benchmarking the Robustness of Embodied Agents on Ambient Context Illusions

author.name: Yang Qu, Qiang Fu, Zonghao Ying, Jiayi Zhao, Yaoyuan Zhang, Jinyang Guo, Jian Yang, Aishan Liu, Yingxun Wang, Xianglong Liu

entry.summary: VagueBench identifies and studies a novel failure mode, Ambient Context Illusion, where embodied agents fail on semantically sufficient but contextually minimal instructions when non-essential contextual details are omitted. The benchmark is built on AI2-THOR and shifts robustness evaluation away from the usual hazardous-instruction and jailbreak focus.

entry.title: HybridSpec: Throughput-Aware Speculative Decoding for Hybrid GDN-MoE Models

author.name: Haiyu Wang, Sai Qian Zhang, Zechun Liu, Steven Li

entry.summary: HybridSpec analyzes how speculative decoding verification costs scale differently for hybrid Gated DeltaNet plus MoE models versus dense models, showing verification time rising 71% from draft length 4 to 16 on a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B profile versus 4-6% for a dense 4B model. It proposes throughput-aware verification length selection, addressing an increasingly common architecture class in efficient inference.

entry.title: Planning-Coding Separation in LLM-Based Code Generation: An Empirical Study

author.name: Wentao Wang, Zeyu Sun, Ruwei Pan, Yueyi Xiao, Qingyuan Liang, Lu Zhang

entry.summary: Presents the first comprehensive empirical study of separating planning and coding across different LLMs in code generation pipelines, varying planner-coder combinations and measuring the effect of further coder training. The study clarifies how well coders can consume planning information from stronger or weaker planners. It is practically relevant for multi-model agentic coding architectures where roles are split across heterogeneous models.

entry.title: Twice as Fast, Until It Isn't: Quantized Serving of Mid-Size Open LLMs

author.name: Smit Kadvani, Kriti Faujdar, Spurthi Tallam

entry.summary: Assembles and audits the publicly verifiable record of speedup and accuracy numbers for quantized serving of 9B-20B open-weight LLMs on vLLM and SGLang, finding the evidence base remarkably thin (only two INT4 Gemma 3 12B checkpoints have both a timing and an accuracy score, and that score covers a single MMLU subject). It confirms the memory-bandwidth explanation for batch-1 4-bit speedups while cataloging major gaps for AMD, Intel Gaudi, and FP4. A valuable reality check for practitioners choosing quantization recipes.

entry.title: Learnings and Pitfalls from AI-Assisted A/B Experimentation at Scale

author.name: Brett Daley, Ilya Gorbachev, Anubhav Natani, Nicholas Brown, Athena Dai, Rachel Song, Marcin Pekalski, Josip Domazet, Anchal Choubey, Daniel Ting

entry.summary: The authors report lessons from building and operating an LLM agent that automates parts of A/B experimentation workflows, keeping the statistical foundations deterministic while letting agents handle anomaly diagnosis, debugging, and follow-up analyses. The paper articulates a division of labor between nondeterministic agent reasoning and trustworthy statistical infrastructure.

entry.title: Catalyzing Interactive HTML Generation Capabilities via High-Fidelity Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xujia Wang, Yixuan Liu, Shaohan Huang, Furu Wei, Lei Hou, Bin Xu, Juanzi Li

entry.summary: WebCatalyst is a browser-interaction reinforcement learning framework for generating functional, interactive HTML from natural language, using mini-games as a testbed to expose failures in functionality and visual quality that shallow webpage checks miss. It combines a game-level GUI assessor with components addressing interaction experience, reward signal, and credit assignment fidelity.

entry.title: Multi-layer Indexer: Overlapping Selection and Attention in DeepSeek Sparse Attention

author.name: Serdarcan Dilbaz, Arjun Krishna, Kiran Kamble, Daniel M. Bikel

entry.summary: Analyzing DeepSeek Sparse Attention as used in DeepSeek-V3.2 and the GLM-5 family, the authors observe that adjacent layers select nearly identical tokens, so a layer can attend to the previous indexer layer's selection instead of running its own scan, removing serial dependency. This targets the indexer scan, not the sparse attention itself, as the decode-time bottleneck at long context.

entry.title: FlowTranslator: Training-Free In-Image Machine Translation with Flow-Based Editing

author.name: Zhixian Li, Xingsong Ye, Yongkun Du, Yunyan Xiao, Yanglin Huang, Pinxuan Chen, Jiyu Zhuang, Cong Xu, Zhineng Chen

entry.summary: FlowTranslator performs in-image machine translation without task-specific training by using OCR plus an LLM to build translation prompts injected into a multilingual text-to-image diffusion model. It introduces trajectory controls, including Region Coupling, to generate accurate and natural translated text while preserving visual context.

entry.title: CANDO: Conservative Action-Noise Directional Optimization for Residual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zeyu Gao, Chengkai Hou, Chaoyue Li, Zhuangzhe Wu, Jiaming Liu, Yao Mu, Peng Jia, Li Zhang, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: CANDO adapts frozen generative policies for robot control via noise-space residual RL, using conservative directional optimization of noise edits instead of fixed latent feasible regions. This aims to preserve the structure learned from offline demonstrations while improving sample efficiency over existing noise- and action-space residual methods.

entry.title: Best-of-Depth: Learning Exploratory Dynamics in Looped Transformers

author.name: Shota Takashiro, Takeshi Kojima, Masanori Koyama, Kohei Hayashi, Yusuke Iwasawa

entry.summary: Best-of-Depth trains looped transformers so that every intermediate depth produces useful candidate solutions, by minimizing prediction loss across depths without architectural changes or depth-specific labels. On N-Queens completion and graph coloring, it substantially improves solution coverage over final-depth training (91.03% versus 45.75%).

entry.title: Asymptotic Optimality of $c\mu$-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint

author.name: Zhenghao Li, Shengbo Wang, Nian Si

entry.summary: The paper models LLM inference scheduling as a queueing problem where requests with heterogeneous prompt and output lengths compete for finite KV-cache capacity, and proves asymptotic optimality of a c-mu-rule-style policy under memory constraints. This bridges classical scheduling theory with the practical bottleneck of KV-cache memory in serving workloads.

entry.title: Do Agentic Policies Need to Look at Every Step? Geometric Abstraction for Reasoning and Action

author.name: Yihang Liu, Yiming Chen, Mingzhe Zheng

entry.summary: This paper proposes moving routine spatial reasoning in robot manipulation from raw images to a lightweight 3D geometric abstraction expressed in text and symbols, refreshed locally from calibrated RGB-D observations. Language models read compact textual checkpoints with metric residuals after each action, reusing symbolic task structure across decisions. The approach could reduce the computational burden of repeatedly reinterpreting visual scenes at every step of an interaction.

entry.title: Mixture of Wide Experts: Sparse Routing for Interpretable Native Coordinates

author.name: Tavish Mankash, Vardhaman Kalloli, Keshava Prasad, Deepan Muthirayan

entry.summary: Mixture of Wide Experts (MoWE) is a sparse feed-forward layer where selected experts read the full representation but write to fixed, disjoint output coordinates, encouraging concepts to localize into interpretable native dimensions. At matched compute (10B tokens, 19-layer models), MoWE preserves performance while localizing causal factors more clearly than dense or standard MoE models.

entry.title: One Mistake, Three Layers: Persistence Rules Under Depth Correlation

author.name: Maryam Rahimimovassagh, Michael Brown, Sanjeda Sara Jennifer, Niloofar Yousefi

entry.summary: This paper shows that the common practice of declaring when a representation first becomes decodable across transformer layers, using a rule requiring probe scores to exceed a threshold for several consecutive layers, can report onsets drastically too early because neighboring-layer probe scores are correlated. The authors propose an estimator with permuting-based null trajectories whose error rate is calibrated rather than assumed, importing a hazard known from neuroimaging into probing methodology.

entry.title: Computer-Use Agents Gain Little Benefit from a World Model When Conditioned on Tutorials

author.name: Anh Nguyen, Tianyi Xu, Phat Tran, Harry Yu, Huazheng Wang, Stefan Lee

entry.summary: This paper dissects which components drive recent gains in computer-use agents by building two curated multimodal tutorial datasets (OSWorld-Tutorial and ScienceBoard-Tutorial) and proposing RAG-PJ, a policy-judge framework conditioned on tutorials. By isolating tutorials, judge, and world-model contributions, the authors find that a world model adds little benefit once tutorials are provided. This offers useful ablation evidence that challenges assumptions in the fast-moving CUA literature.

entry.title: SKILL2STEER: One-Pass Hypernetwork for Mapping Natural-Language Skills to Low-Rank Post-Block Activation Shifts

author.name: Ran Li, Lei Chen

entry.summary: The paper tests whether compiled skill artifacts injected into model activations actually carry skill content, finding via controlled experiments that they encode a domain-general behavioral prior rather than skill-specific information. A wrong skill document performs on par with the correct one, and an averaged bundle matches per-skill routing.

entry.title: Logarithmic Regret for Alternating Mirror Descent

author.name: Tianlong Nan, Christian Kroer

entry.summary: This paper resolves an open question by proving that alternating online mirror descent achieves O(log T) regret in two-player zero-sum bilinear games, improving prior O(T^{1/3}) and O(T^{1/5}) bounds. The result holds under mild regularity assumptions on regularizers and is verified for standard choices.

entry.title: BEND 2.0: Benchmarking the Capabilities Needed to Design DNA

author.name: Andreas Bjerregaard, Rachael DeVries, Dionysia Danai Brilli, Panagiotis Antoniadis, Yan Li, Anders Krogh, Wouter Boomsma, Ole Winther, Frederikke Isa Marin

entry.summary: BEND 2.0 benchmarks genomic foundation models on predicting the effects of DNA changes and using those predictions to guide sequence design, across eight tasks built on five experimental datasets. It finds that linear readouts on frozen representations can match native outputs and that functional post-training substantially improves design capabilities.

entry.title: Nearly Linear-Time Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader for Weakly Observable Graph Bandits

author.name: Jongyeong Lee, Hyundam Yoo

entry.summary: This work proposes an FTPL policy for online learning with directed weakly observable feedback graphs that achieves best-of-both-worlds guarantees with nearly linear time complexity. It introduces a novel graph-based loss estimator combining forced exploration, conditional geometric resampling, and adaptive learning rates, achieving strong regret bounds in both adversarial and stochastic regimes.

entry.title: Post-stratified importance sampling

author.name: Yuling Yao, Sergei Tikhonov

entry.summary: Proposes post-stratified importance sampling (PIS), which reformulates high-dimensional importance weighting into two one-dimensional probabilistic modeling problems: regressing the conditional mean given the importance ratio and estimating the ratio's marginal density. Inspired by multilevel regression and poststratification, PIS addresses the high or infinite variance that plagues standard importance sampling.

entry.title: Typological Feature Induction as a Benchmark for Inductive Metalinguistic Reasoning

author.name: Chen Zhang, Seth Aycock, Yusuke Miyao

entry.summary: The paper introduces typological feature induction (TFI), a benchmark where models must infer typological features of an unnamed language from sentence pairs with pivot-language translations, built from Grambank over 195 languages. Strikingly, LLMs identify 59-80% of languages from only 16 sentence pairs, and scrambled translations barely hurt accuracy, indicating reliance on memorized prior knowledge rather than genuine inductive reasoning.

entry.title: Heads That Write, Not Just Point: Image Retrieval Heads in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Junsung Park, Sangwon Yu, Donghun Kang, Yeongtak Oh, Jaewon Jeong, Gyeongtae Yoo, Han Cheol Moon, Jungbeom Lee, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: This interpretability study of large vision-language models identifies sparse pointer heads that reliably attend to the question-relevant image in multi-image contexts, using head-level attention over image-token spans via the ICIR-MCQ probe. A single pointer head rivals external retrievers on naturalistic multi-image retrieval, but attention alone proves insufficient to explain behavior, with some heads actively writing information.

entry.title: Beyond Proposals: Region-Consistent Open-Set Object Detection

author.name: Jiehui Tang, Yunlong Yu, Zhao Wang, Jungong Han

entry.summary: This paper identifies a core flaw in open-set object detection: overlapping proposals for the same object receive contradictory known/unknown labels when reasoning is done per proposal. OCSI-Net reformulates the task as object-centric semantic inference, letting correlated proposals jointly support a coherent region-level decision via semantic consistency and geometry-aware uncertainty modeling.

entry.title: ReconDreamer#: Self-Evolving Closed-Loop Synergy of Reconstruction and Generation for Dynamic Driving Scenes

author.name: Songling Liu, Guosheng Zhao, Xiaofeng Wang, Chaojun Ni, Guan Huang, Jiwen Lu, Xingang Wang, Zheng Zhu

entry.summary: ReconDreamer# creates a self-evolving closed loop where generative and reconstruction models iteratively refine each other for dynamic driving scene reconstruction, narrowing the gap between synthesized novel trajectory renders and real sensor observations. It builds on the ReconDreamer line of work for driving scene simulation.

entry.title: StepX-OPD: Rethinking Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Diffusion Models

author.name: Chenru Wang, Xuanyang Zhang, Yucheng Han, Wenbo Nie, Wei Cheng, Xianfang Zeng, Gang YU, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: Merges capability consolidation and step compression in text-to-image diffusion distillation into a single stage: one student acquires capabilities (instruction following, text rendering, preference) while learning few-step sampling, with frozen specialist teachers supervising on the student's own rollout states. Traditional two-stage pipelines degrade every model tested and serialize training.

entry.title: PATTS: Parallel-Aware Test-Time Scaling for Thought-Image Generation in Multimodal Discrete Diffusion LLMs

author.name: Yasong Dai, Zeeshan Hayder, David Ahmedt-Aristizabal, Hongdong Li

entry.summary: The paper studies test-time scaling for parallel multimodal discrete diffusion LLMs where reasoning and image tokens are decoded jointly, diagnosing that CLIP-style verifiers align poorly with compositional correctness on GenEval. It proposes PATTS, a parallel-aware framework that supervises intermediate trajectory states rather than only ranking final images.

entry.title: Wonder 4: A Mixture-of-Experts Recipe for Image Quality Enhancement

author.name: Yunan Wu, Bin Sun, Partha Acharjee, Xiaoyu Wang

entry.summary: Presents Wonder 4, a mixture-of-experts model for all-in-one image quality enhancement that routes each image patch to 5 of 13 experts per block, correcting multiple co-occurring defects (blur, noise, compression artifacts, scratches, low resolution) locally rather than with a single global description. It requires no degradation classifier, mask, prompt, or task label.

entry.title: StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Ai2 introduces StateBench, a benchmark evaluating how language models track changing information across long documents at four difficulty levels, revealing systematic weaknesses in state tracking and showing that targeted training improves recurrent and hybrid architectures on longer sequences. The benchmark isolates a core capability gap relevant to long-context reliability.

entry.title: Thinking Fast, Trading Late: System One Decision Models vs the Market

author.name: Amir Dehkordi (Independent Researcher), Alireza Kargarzadeh (TailState Intelligence Ltd), Nariman Khaledian (Independent Researcher), Navid Parvini (Zanista AI Ltd), Sid Ghatak (Increase Alpha, LLC), Arman Khaledian (Zanista AI Ltd)

entry.summary: The paper proposes OLIVIA, a protocol for testing whether LLM-based stock-return predictability survives controls for look-ahead, memorization, and selection, using point-in-time masked inputs, validation-only selection, cryptographically frozen analysis plans, and logged test-period unblinding. It applies this to a fine-tuned open-weights decision model, three commercial models, and baselines on S&P 500 news.

entry.title: AceAction-5M: Hierarchical Goals for Generalist Action Learning Across 3D Game Worlds

author.name: Kailing Li, Ruoxuan Zhang, Zheyuan Zhou, Boyang Chu, Yingshan Lei, Hongxia Xie, Liang Du, Zixun Sun

entry.summary: AceAction is a vision-language-action dataset of human gameplay across multiple 3D games, organized around complete tasks with overall instructions, ordered subgoals, and local skill instructions aligned to visual observations and keyboard-mouse actions, annotated via a vision-language model pipeline. Games serve as a scalable proxy for costly physical-environment VLA data collection.

entry.title: Where Is the Truth When AI Agents Disagree? Dependence-Aware Belief Propagation for Unsupervised Truth Discovery (Extended Version)

author.name: Laure Berti-Equille

entry.summary: The paper studies unsupervised truth discovery among LLM agents whose errors are correlated because many are variants of one base model. The proposed BP-TD method adds per-agent decorrelation weights to mean-field variational inference on a one-coin Dawid-Skene model so correlated agents count as roughly one vote, beating majority vote on MMLU with 13 agents without any labels.

entry.title: GC-MoE: Overlapping Expert-Parallel Token Dispatch with FP8/FP4 Grouped GEMM via CUDA Green Contexts

author.name: Yong Li, Kan Liu, Tao Lan

entry.summary: GC-MoE is an open-source FP8/FP4 mixture-of-experts inference operator for NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs that uses CUDA Green Contexts to overlap expert-parallel token dispatch with grouped GEMMs, addressing low tensor-core utilization and resource contention in decode with few tokens per rank.

entry.title: $\tau$-Rec-Books: A Disclosure-Controlled Benchmark for Requirement Elicitation in Agentic Recommender Systems

author.name: Bharath Sivaram Narasimhan, Karthik R. Narasimhan

entry.summary: Tau-Rec-Books is a benchmark for evaluating how conversational recommender agents progressively discover user requirements, holding requests fixed while varying disclosure conditions: fully volunteered, mixed, or partially hidden requirements inferable only from accept/reject feedback. It includes 450 tasks over a 20,000-book catalog with a rule-based simulated user.

entry.title: LLMs as MDP Designers: A Dependency-Aware Agentic Framework for Automated Robot Policy Generation

author.name: Hong Je-Gal, Jinwoo Kim, Chanbin Yi, Hyun-Suk Lee

entry.summary: ARPG uses LLMs as designers that build RL pipelines before deployment from natural-language task descriptions, including MDP formulation and simulator implementation, rather than as runtime decision makers. It exploits a phase-wise structure (sequential dependency-structured MDP modeling, then modular simulator coding) with localized verification and correction.

entry.title: Personas Are Not People: Identity as State, Not Attribute

author.name: Tamunotonye Harry, Yuanyuan Feng

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that persona-based synthetic populations rest on a flawed assumption: that identity is a stable attribute, contradicting three decades of personality research showing behavior varies more across contexts than people vary from each other. Drawing on identity economics, the authors propose treating identity as state rather than fixed trait in simulations of users, surveys, and communities. It challenges a core design assumption in the growing field of agent-based social simulation.

entry.title: Probabilistic Steering of Generative Priors for Lab-in-the-Loop Antibody Optimization

author.name: Anisha Parsan, Sebastian Ober, Calvin McCarter, Nick Bhattacharya, Hunter Elliott

entry.summary: The paper unifies antibody discovery and optimization by smoothly transitioning a generative structure model into iterative black-box optimization, with the handoff guided by posterior uncertainty of a probabilistic surrogate. This yields improved optimization efficiency in the low-data (low-N) regime for lab-in-the-loop therapeutic development.

entry.title: Tokenizer Myths and Where To Find Them

author.name: Rylan Schaeffer, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: This paper identifies and empirically challenges three myths in tokenization research: that bits-per-byte is tokenizer-agnostic, that lower BPB implies a better model, and a third related misconception. Using untrained models and models trained on identical data, it shows BPB systematically prefers some tokenizers and vocabulary sizes independently of downstream accuracy.

entry.title: Ablating Design Choices for Protein Ensemble Generators Across Structural Regimes

author.name: Eoin Quinn, Oliver Bent

entry.summary: Using a minimal C-alpha flow-matching model, the paper ablates architecture, sequence conditioning, rigid-body alignment, and training source choices for protein conformational ensemble generation, evaluating against experimental SAXS and NMR data across ordered, disordered, multi-domain, and transitional regimes. Notably, several inherited design choices (MoE routing, static pair representations, a disorder probe) show no detectable effect.

entry.title: Same Rule, Different Verdicts: Rubric Language and Clause Structure in LLM Judges for Korean Support Dialogues

author.name: Sangdo Han, Moonsoo Kim

entry.summary: Systematically tests whether LLM-judge verdicts depend on rubric language (Korean vs English) and clause structure (affirmative, negated, conditional, exception) using a pre-registered analysis over roughly 52,000 judging requests across seven models. Results show lower cross-provider agreement with Korean rubrics, exposing sensitivity of LLM-as-judge pipelines to phrasing.

entry.title: WMIP: A Working-Memory-Inspired Programmable Probe of Cumulative State Tracking in Large Language Models

author.name: Dengzhe Hou, Lingyu Jiang, Deng Li, Zirui Li, Fangzhou Lin, Kazunori D Yamada

entry.summary: WMIP is a working-memory-inspired probe of cumulative state tracking with program-computed answers, comparing final-state, intermediate-state, and multi-target query protocols on identical items across 3 to 100 updates. Across 18 LLMs, accuracy drops from 84.9% on single-step arithmetic to 31.7% on core items with three to seven updates, and no model exceeds 10% at 50+ updates.

entry.title: Mamba3R: Fixed-Capacity Selective State Memory for Long-Sequence 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Zhenxiang Xiong, Tianchen Deng, Nailin Wang, Lei Zhao, Guole Shen, Weidong Che

entry.summary: Mamba3R adds a trainable state-memory adapter to a frozen pretrained recurrent model for streaming 3D reconstruction, using a selective state-space mixer with explicit read/write paths and a decomposed feedback path, training only 1.28M parameters. It lowers trajectory error under a fixed GPU budget and shared periodic-reset protocol for long sequences.

entry.title: Efficient and Faithful High-Resolution Image Editing with Sparse Cross-Resolution Denoising

author.name: Maosen Zhao, Xianfang Zeng, Pengtao Chen, Peng Ye, Gang Yu, Jiayuan Fan, Tao Chen

entry.summary: Introduces FLASH, a native high-resolution (2K/4K) instruction-based image editor using sparse cross-resolution denoising: a frozen 1K branch anchors semantics and structure while a target-resolution branch reconstructs detail within the same Transformer, with an asymmetric topology guiding high-res queries from aligned low-res states. Avoids both expensive dense high-res attention and the trajectory disconnect of external upscalers.

entry.title: BhopalMLS: A LiDAR Dataset for Semantic Scene Understanding in Heterogeneous Urban Environments

author.name: Pyare Lal Chauhan, Vaibhav Kumar, Bharat Lohani

entry.summary: Releases a large-scale mobile laser scanning dataset from Bhopal, India with about 1.2 billion points, 19,518 annotated instances, and 62 fine-grained categories across 10 km of dense, unplanned urban corridors. Findings show fine-tuned foundation models surpass supervised baselines on this underrepresented setting.

entry.title: Robot-Matched Soft Fingers for UMI Data Collection: Lessons from 100 Hours of Pick and Place

author.name: Kobi Kelemen, Tomasz Niedzia{\l}kowski, Marcin Paszczak, Victoriano Montesinos

entry.summary: Describes a battery-powered handheld Universal Manipulation Interface with soft, angled fingers that deform under load as a visual force proxy and match the target robot gripper, used to collect a 99.7-hour dataset over 53 objects. Policies trained with pi0.5 on 49 objects generalize to 4 held-out objects, with practical findings such as a top camera raising success by 13 points.

entry.title: Safeguarding Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Connected and Automated Vehicles with Recursively Feasible Control Barrier Functions

author.name: Jianye Xu, Yousef Sayed, Bassam Alrifaee

entry.summary: The paper proposes Backup-Horizon CBF, a control barrier function that evaluates safety along a horizon until all vehicles stop, achieving recursive feasibility under control bounds while respecting exact vehicle and road geometry. From it, the authors derive a fully decentralized safety filter for multi-agent reinforcement learning coordination of connected automated vehicles requiring only one broadcast of states and routes per step.

entry.title: LOLPlay: Benchmarking Real-Time Visual Agents in League of Legends

author.name: Zhaojian Yu

entry.summary: LOLPlay is a benchmark for visual agents in native League of Legends featuring 36 champion-specific tasks spanning resource management, combat, cooperation, and objectives, with automated initialization and 82 executable subgoal checks. Across 324 evaluations, GPT-6 Astra (an existing model released in September 2026) reaches only 25.0% task success, and high reasoning effort improves nothing over low effort.

entry.title: DoGNAVY-Exploit: Harnessing Parallel Open-Weight Agents for Stage-Aware Vulnerability Exploitation

author.name: Yuxuan Wang, Dadi Guo, Weijie Guo, Zikai Xu, Chen Lu, Yizhe Zhuang, Peng Huang, Yuejin Xie, Guopeng Lin, Xuangan Xiao, Shipei Qu, Dongrui Liu

entry.summary: DoGNAVY-Exploit is a multi-agent harness that enables open-weight LLM agents to convert known vulnerabilities into working exploits via stage-aware decomposition with progressive expert knowledge disclosure and hierarchical orchestration with parallel exploration. It demonstrates that accessible open-weight models can match frontier-agent exploitation capabilities with the right scaffolding, which is a notable dual-use security finding.

entry.title: Goal-Driven Autonomous Optical Experimentation via a Self-Recursive Hardware-Software Harness

author.name: Tianxing Zhu, Huacheng Lu, Ming Liu, Malte Hillebrand

entry.summary: Proposes a framework in which agents autonomously revise the hardware, software, models, and protocols used to pursue a scientific goal, using physical evidence, with a formal relation between physical attainability, command access, and model approximation error. Demonstrated in an optical see-through color-matching case study with real instruments where the agent modified glasses firmware behavior to keep displayed colors stable during spectral acquisition. An early demonstration of self-modifying autonomous experimentation loops.

entry.title: When Should an LLM Steering Edit Depend on the Input?

author.name: Rachael Harkness, Konrad Rawlik

entry.summary: This paper analyzes when activation steering edits in LLMs should be input-dependent, arguing that Contrastive Activation Addition's fixed direction cannot express within-class variation in required displacement. The authors study a spectrum from difference-of-means edits to per-query retrieved destinations (mean of k nearest stored states), providing a principled account of steering expressiveness.

entry.title: Modelling lock-in of AI adoption through skill erosion

author.name: Renaud Lambiotte

entry.summary: The paper presents a mathematical model of AI adoption in which individuals imitate successful peers while independent skills grow with practice and erode with reliance on AI. The model yields exactly derived skill distributions and shows that skill erosion produces bistability and hysteresis between a low-adoption/high-skill and high-adoption/low-skill state, with asymmetric transition conditions.

entry.title: The Platonic Brain: Representational Convergence in EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Nicolas Waehner, Enzo Tagliazucchi, Jacobo Sitt, Demian Wassermann, Giovanni Franco Gabriel Marraffini, Trinidad Borrell

entry.summary: This work tests the Platonic Representation Hypothesis in the neuroscience domain, examining whether EEG foundation models converge on shared representations of brain activity using recordings from six participants watching television with aligned visual and language content. It finds that models with greater decodability show stronger cross-family alignment, though alignment does not consistently increase with model performance.

entry.title: rTaste: Do Research Agents Have Taste? Evaluating Early Stage Research Judgment

author.name: Art Kanke

entry.summary: This evaluation gives six frontier models seven recent NLP papers and asks them to propose, forecast, and rank minimum viable experiments, which a separate executor then runs and three model auditors judge. Of 415 proposed experiments, 194 were judged sound and new, but only 73 were both non-obvious and beyond the seed paper, and agent first choices did not demonstrably beat choosing the extreme-ranked option.

entry.title: From Forecasting to Feedback: Evaluating Learned Dynamics for Tokamak Control

author.name: Guoyang Shi, Siqi Ding, Xuanhe Wang, Pei Guo, Changquan Yu, Jiale Hu, Jiayi Zhi, Zhengyuan Chen, Jianguo Chen, Tianyuan Liu

entry.summary: Using a calibrated free-boundary Grad-Shafranov solver, this study trains 16 action-conditioned Transformers across a 2x2 data design and evaluates PPO policies optimized in learned surrogates on unseen tokamak control scenarios. It quantifies the forecasting-control gap, showing logged-trajectory accuracy need not predict closed-loop performance under optimized policies.

entry.title: LoRA-Patch: Defending Against Backdoored LoRA Adapters via Directional Steering

author.name: Shengyan Huo, Peihai Jiang, Xixiang Lyu, Yige Li

entry.summary: LoRA-Patch defends against backdoored third-party LoRA adapters by exploiting how backdoor injection distorts the directional geometry of an adapter relative to its trusted base model, applying a lightweight directional steering correction. Unlike prior defenses that update or distill the whole model, it keeps the trusted base frozen, matching adapter-based deployment.

entry.title: FlagRot: Selective Rotation for Low-Bit KV Caches

author.name: Kunming Shao, Xijie Huang, Jierun Chen, Jiaqi Shao, Yanli Wang, Jiangnan Yu, Qiwei Li, Wei Zhang, Kwang-Ting Cheng, Chi Ying Tsui

entry.summary: FlagRot improves 2-bit KV cache quantization by observing that rotation does not uniformly help: it can flatten spiky channels but create new peaks in flat ones. The method stores each 32-channel piece rotated or unrotated based on calibrated attention error, rotating queries at read time, and adapts decision granularity to per-channel versus per-token cache designs.

entry.title: SEAM: Situated Executable Associative Memory for a Co-located Community

author.name: Keru Wang, Michael Xu, Ken Perlin, Nebojsa Jojic, Andrzej Banburski-Fahey

entry.summary: SEAM is a social app prototype that maintains a shared associative memory for a community, relating members' posted moments and responding in situated ways; some memories act as executable instructions that reprogram system behavior. It was deployed for two weeks with 46 users plus a 14-person follow-up workshop.

entry.title: BtsPruner: Role-Aware Visual Token Pruning for Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zihao Qi, Zhibo Zhang, Miaoxin Zhang, Jincheng Cai, Zengqiang Yan

entry.summary: BtsPruner is a training-free visual token pruning method for LVLMs based on the observation that tokens transition from local detail carriers to globally referenced representatives during encoding. By treating tokens according to their evolving roles rather than uniform criteria, it reduces computational and memory overhead more effectively.

entry.title: One Assistant, Many Memories: Benchmarking Real-World Group Assistance When Recall Is Not Enough

author.name: Zhanghao Hu, Linhai Zhang, Qian Zhao, Qi Zhu, Yuan Hua, Di Liang, Jiasheng Si, Xin Zhao, Yulan He, Zhumin Chen, Lin Gui

entry.summary: GroupAssistBench is presented as the first memory benchmark built from real-world group conversations, requiring assistants to integrate information across multiple members, track revisions and conflicts, and produce appropriate group-level responses. It moves evaluation beyond recall of fixed answers toward genuinely helpful assistance.

entry.title: Language Models Can Benefit from Domain-Specific Inductive Biases

author.name: Damien Teney, Liangze Jiang, Zachary Shinnick, Hemanth Saratchandran, Simon Lucey

entry.summary: The authors train small language models from scratch on domain-specific subsets of pretraining data (web, code, math) using transformer variants with learned spline activations, testing whether a single general-purpose architecture is optimal across data types. The mix-and-match evaluation of cross-domain architecture transfer shows domain-tuned inductive biases can improve over standard transformers.

entry.title: TB-Transolver: Parallelized and Coherent Long-Horizon Rollouts via Temporal Bundling for Time-Dependent PDEs

author.name: Sidharth S. Menon, Ameya D. Jagtap

entry.summary: TB-Transolver augments the widely adopted Transolver neural PDE solver with temporal bundling so that long-horizon rollouts for time-dependent PDEs can be executed in parallel rather than sequentially via autoregressive or time-conditioned stepping. This removes the linear cost scaling with temporal horizon while maintaining rollout coherence on unstructured meshes.

entry.title: Decomposing Rank Reversals under Temporal Nonstationarity: Alignment, Aggressiveness, and Instability

author.name: Deying Song, Xueying Ding

entry.summary: The paper derives a model-agnostic decomposition of out-of-sample R-squared into target alignment, miscalibrated aggressiveness, and predictive instability, explaining why model rankings reverse under temporal nonstationarity. It establishes closed-form optimal-memory results for ridge regression under local drift and extends guarantees to more complex architectures. This unifies previously separate strands on adaptive lookbacks and effective model complexity.

entry.title: Proper Agnostic Learning of Affine Halfspaces under Log-Concave Marginals

author.name: Zhijie Zheng

entry.summary: The paper gives a proper constant-factor agnostic learner for affine halfspaces under full-dimensional log-concave marginals, achieving error at most C times OPT plus epsilon with polynomial sample and arithmetic complexity. A key geometric result relates global disagreement to disagreement on a balanced restriction for minority halfspaces.

entry.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Submodular Trajectory Rewards

author.name: Yasaman Zolfimoselo, Nikolas Geroliminis, Maryam Kamgarpour

entry.summary: This theoretical MARL work studies cooperative settings with decoupled dynamics and monotone submodular rewards over joint trajectories, where optimal policies may depend on full multi-agent history. It introduces pre-window curvature to bound the error from restricting each agent's policy to a finite recent window, enabling a greedy algorithm with provable guarantees. Relevant to traffic control and other multi-agent coordination problems with non-additive objectives.

entry.title: Empirical Bayes Flow Matching for Continuous Cryo-EM Heterogeneity

author.name: Daniel Aibinder, Azmi Haider, Dan Rosenbaum

entry.summary: EB-FM learns generative flow matching priors over high-dimensional 3D molecular structures from noisy 2D cryo-EM projection images using a Monte Carlo EM framework, alternating posterior sampling with prior updates. This addresses continuous heterogeneity analysis in structural biology where structures are never directly observed.

entry.title: Testing Processor Contracts in Speculative Decoding Engines

author.name: Tianyu Ding, Yaocheng Tong, Muzhi Yang, Lei Yang, Fei Jiang

entry.summary: The paper formalizes the processor-prefix contract in speculative decoding—logits processors must receive the correct token prefix and state at each verification position—and presents BADC, a branch-aware differential conformance testing framework. Experiments on real Transformers and llama-cpp-python releases confirm two real bug classes: processors reading unverified drafts or advancing state without rollback, breaking the lossless-speedup guarantee.

entry.title: Sparse Internal Control of Language Models

author.name: Xizhe Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces sparse internal control, a framework for steering language model behavior at inference time by intervening on a small set of internal model nodes. It formulates a local target-controllability objective characterizing candidate site-direction pairs with constraints on target recovery, off-target preservation, and intervention strength.

entry.title: PolicyIK: High-Precision Inverse Kinematics for Robot Arms with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuhan Liu, Xinqi Liu, Zixuan Dong, Keith W. Ross, Shenji Wan

entry.summary: Introduces PolicyIK, a goal-conditioned RL policy for high-precision inverse kinematics of robot arms that updates joint-position references from pose feedback and handles redundancy, singularities, and controller offsets. It supports vision-language-action policies by enabling accurate action execution and cross-embodiment transfer.

entry.title: TraceRouter++: Causal Semantic Routing Realignment via Optimal Transport

author.name: Chuancheng Shi, Shangze Li, Wenhua Wu, Hengzhi Chen, Fei Shen, Li Zhuo, Zhiyong Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: TraceRouter++ proposes a routing-level safety intervention for large foundation models that traces causal pathways activated by harmful inputs and realigns unsafe activation states using optimal transport, in a Discover-Trace-Realign paradigm. It argues against brittle localized neuron suppression, instead targeting distributed cross-layer circuits to resist complex jailbreaks while preserving utility.

entry.title: FlowRig: Unified Skeleton Generation for 3D and 4D Meshes via Flow Matching

author.name: Fengzhi Guo, Nate Morrill, Shiqi Li, Cheng Zhang

entry.summary: MoTWorld is a template-free framework that unifies rigging for static 3D meshes and dynamic 4D mesh sequences using flow matching, generating temporally aligned skeletons in a single feedforward pass. It avoids the temporal instability of frame-by-frame 3D riggers and the expensive per-sequence optimization of existing 4D methods.

entry.title: SEEK-VAU: Towards Evidence-Faithful Video Anomaly Understanding via Agentic Search

author.name: Minghe Wang, Weijun Zeng, Dapeng Luo, Xinyue Wang, Nong Sang

entry.summary: Reframes video anomaly understanding as an agentic search-and-verify protocol in which the model actively gathers evidence across precursor, trigger, and aftermath stages within a bounded budget, verifying sufficiency before reasoning. This contrasts with feed-forward pipelines that cannot recover missing evidence.

entry.title: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval

author.name: WonJun Moon, Seongchan Kim, Dahun Kim, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: FactEmbed argues that composed image retrieval underuses MLLM compositional understanding when queries are mapped directly into a single contrastive embedding. It decouples compositional query comprehension from discriminative embedding construction, having the model explicitly resolve intended visual modifications before building retrieval embeddings.

entry.title: OpenBrain: An Auditable Generated-Label Release for Whole-Brain MRI Parcellation

author.name: Qizhen Lan, Yu-Chun Hsu, Yuxiang Wei, Lijing Zhu, Zenan Sun, Liang He, Lishan Yu, Xiaoqian Jiang

entry.summary: Releases OpenBrain, a confidence-aware dataset of 35,838 provenance-verified OpenNeuro T1w MRI cases with whole-brain parcellations organized as auditable case records, including committee parcellations, a reference-free QC-7 reliability panel, percentile risks, and confidence tiers. This lets users filter generated labels by trustworthiness rather than treating all model outputs equally.

entry.title: Trusting Imagined Futures: Auditing Imagined Rewards for VLA Post-Training

author.name: Zicheng Kong, Zhenbo Xu, Haoyan Zhang, Jinghan Yang, Zhenzhen Li, Yiwei Ru, Liuyu Xiang, WanTing Xu, Min Ren, Zhaofeng He

entry.summary: Presents TIF, an offline supervision selection method for VLA post-training that audits reward predictions from video world models using real execution feedback, with a multidimensional reward model and an auditor that detects reward overestimation patterns. Candidates are accepted only when their predicted advantage over the current trajectory exceeds a margin.

entry.title: Action Intent as a Bridge: Transferring Manipulation Knowledge from Human-Centric Videos to Robots

author.name: Zhiqian Xia, Lianyang Ma, Haifeng Xia, Siyu Xia, Wei Wang, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: AIT transfers manipulation knowledge from human-centric videos to VLA models through a clean shared action representation: it first extracts and disentangles explicit action intents from manipulation videos, then uses this latent action intent as a bridge between human and robot domains. This avoids the scene-specific noise that entangles latent action representations in prior video-transfer approaches.

entry.title: From Logs to Faults: Reference-Free Fault Localization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Pipelines

author.name: Hira Naveed, Scott Barnett, Stefanus Kurniawan, John Grundy, Chetan Arora, Hourieh Khalajzadeh, Omar Haggag

entry.summary: RAGLog detects and localizes faults across RAG pipeline stages using execution logs alone, without reference answers or code instrumentation, by normalizing heterogeneous API logs into a common schema and combining rule-based and embedding-based analysis. This tackles the practical problem that fault propagation across interdependent stages masks fault origins.

entry.title: AlgoPilot: Cross-Paradigm Reasoning in Language Models via Strategy Selection and Guidance

author.name: Yilun Hao, Ruixiao Yang, Hudson Hilal, Yongchao Chen, Kaizhi Qian, Yada Zhu, Yang Zhang, Chuchu Fan

entry.summary: AlgoPilot is a framework enabling LLMs to adaptively select solving strategies across paradigms - program synthesis, symbolic reasoning, planning, optimization - via a SteerLM trained with SFT and RL, followed by structured problem formulation and execution. It addresses the dual challenge of choosing the right approach and encoding it correctly before solving.

entry.title: A Parametric Linear Conic Projection for Structured Sparse Attention

author.name: Michel Barlaud, Clement Genninasca, Maxime Zanella, Benoit Macq, Benoit Legat

entry.summary: Introduces the Cone Alignment Index (CAI), a scale-invariant sparsity measure based on Lorentz-cone geometry with probabilistic analysis showing samples lie in the convex cone with probability tending to one in the high-sparsity regime. It derives two projections, the closed-form PLCP and the exact PECP, with guarantees supporting structured sparse attention. A theory-forward contribution to efficient attention mechanisms.

entry.title: The Pen is Mightier than the Pixel: Natural Textual Unlearnable Example for Large Vision Language Models

author.name: Chenyu Yi, Jiawen Zong, Sami Hormi, Bingquan Shen, Xudong Jiang, Alex Chichung Kot

entry.summary: This is the first exploration of Unlearnable Examples for large vision-language models, proposing Natural Textual Unlearnable Examples (NTUE), which mislead LVLMs by subtly manipulating image labels to establish shortcuts between identities without introducing factual misinformation or harming readability. It highlights new privacy-protective defense options and attack surfaces unique to multimodal models.

entry.title: PianoBench: Evaluating Musical Perception and Reasoning in Language Models

author.name: Louis Bradshaw, Irmak Bukey, Daniel Chenyu Lin, John Thickstun, Chris Donahue

entry.summary: PianoBench evaluates whether multimodal language models can perceive and reason about music, using congruent acoustic and symbolic piano representations derived from a new 20,000+ hour dataset of interleaved music and spoken commentary from instructional piano videos. Open-weight audio-language models reach at most 52.8% accuracy and barely beat a no-audio control, while frontier chain-of-thought models perform considerably better.

entry.title: SaMA: Morpho Adaptation via Asymmetric Expansion of Kronecker Product

author.name: An Nguyen, Anh Tong

entry.summary: SaMA is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method based on a generalization of the Kronecker product that relaxes LoRA's shared-block constraint. It spans low to full rank, achieving effective rank that scales quadratically with parameter budget, and addresses LoRA's flat optimization directions.

entry.title: Cycle WAM: Coupling Action and Video through Cycle Consistency

author.name: Qinglin Yang, Jiepeng Wang, Yuxing Huang, Haibin Huang, Kai Xu, Chi Zhang, Ruizhen Hu, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Cycle WAM treats video and robot actions as causally paired modalities and learns their correspondence through cycle consistency, ensuring that predicted actions and their visual consequences in generated video remain aligned. This improves on world action models that decode or infer actions from pretrained video priors without enforcing such consistency.

entry.title: The Right Source Is Not Enough: Understanding History Interference in Speech-LLM Memory

author.name: HongJin Song, Weiqiao Shan, Runwu Shi, Yifei Wu, Yujin Wang, Jiale Luo, Jiasheng Kuang, Xinyu Yang, Zhaoqi Cui, Chuizheng Kong, Ziyu Wu, Guowu Tan, Qiuyu Fang, Chunxiang Jin

entry.summary: This study investigates why irrelevant historical audio in speech LLM conversations changes answers even when the queried event is still represented in context. Controlled experiments on MOSS-Audio and MiMo-Audio with causal interventions distinguish two pathways: open-ended QA errors vanish when computation cannot access the irrelevant source, while multiple-choice errors persist through question-side influence. It provides a mechanistic account of memory interference in audio-capable LLMs.

entry.title: Weight-space programming for auditing clinical decision networks

author.name: Humza Nusrat, Omar Nusrat

entry.summary: The study tests whether a frontier LLM (Claude) given only a clinical protocol and a small network's raw weights can audit and repair the network, using networks of 433 to 4,801 parameters trained to screen head-and-neck radiotherapy planning requests against four rules. Flaws were planted through training data, including confounds, a threshold shift, and a hidden trigger. It explores a novel use of weight-space programming for model auditing in a clinical safety context.

entry.title: Decision Transformer with Task-Aware Representations for Offline Meta-Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xinbo Zhao, Yuhang Liu, Xin Zhang, Lei Le, Zhaohan Xi, Yingxue Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes CoTA-DT, a Decision Transformer framework for offline meta-reinforcement learning that learns latent task representations by combining contrastive learning on offline trajectories, alignment with natural-language task descriptions, short-horizon supervision from a task-conditioned world model, and long-horizon supervision from a task-conditioned Q function. These representations condition policy generation to improve generalization to new tasks.

entry.title: Sample-Grained Approximate Unlearning with Provable Per-Sample Bounds

author.name: Yaxin Xiao, Yulin Jin, Li Tang, Haoyang LI, Huadi Zheng, Qingqing Ye, Haibo Hu

entry.summary: The authors introduce SALA, a plug-in optimization framework steering individual examples toward their correct target distributions during approximate unlearning, with provable per-sample bounds. This moves beyond dataset-level aggregate metrics that can mask sample-level deviations from retraining.

entry.title: Deep Neural Operator Learning for stochastic heat equations and applications

author.name: Hengrong Du, Qi Feng, Weinan Wang

entry.summary: This paper extends universal approximation results for deep operator networks to semilinear stochastic heat equations in dimension d>=2 with distribution-valued Gaussian forcing, using Fourier cutoffs and Besov/Schauder estimates to control the reduction error. ReLU branch networks with grid-based trunk functions then approximate the finite-dimensional solution map with explicit bounds, matched in every finite stochastic moment. A rigorous theoretical contribution to neural operators for SPDEs.

entry.title: Macrocanonical Generator Networks: Data-Efficient Neural Surrogates for Amortized Physics Simulation

author.name: Niall Jeffrey, Benjamin D. Wandelt

entry.summary: The authors introduce macrocanonical generator networks, which train a neural generator to match multiscale statistics of a physical process in expectation, preserving realistic sample-to-sample fluctuations for fast amortized simulation. They provide theory showing gradient descent training induces preconditioned gradient dynamics, targeting data-efficient surrogates for simulation-based inference.

entry.title: ScrambleMark: Zero-Query Watermark-Agnostic Black-Box Evasion of Modern Speech Watermarking

author.name: Binhao Ma, Weikang Ding, Hanqing Guo, Wenwei Zhao, Xiaowen Li, Leah Ding, Zhuo Lu, Rui Duan

entry.summary: ScrambleMark demonstrates a zero-query, watermark-agnostic black-box attack that evades modern speech watermarking by scrambling detection rather than erasing the watermark, defeating systems like TrustedAudio that restrict detector access and feedback. The work shows evading a watermark does not require knowing whether a sample is watermarked or removing it without quality loss.

entry.title: MiCaDe: Online LiDAR-Camera Miscalibration Change Detection for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Carlo Sgaravatti, Riccardo Pieroni, Matteo Corno, Sergio M. Savaresi, Luca Magri, Giacomo Boracchi

entry.summary: MiCaDe is an online method that detects when extrinsic LiDAR-camera calibration drifts in autonomous vehicles, using sequential change detection on 3D-2D bounding box signals without calibration targets or perception-stack modification. It provides low false-alarm rates with negligible computational overhead against drift from vibration, thermal effects, and shocks.

entry.title: Physics-informed traditional and generative Mori-Zwanzig-reduced models for multiscale systems

author.name: Emily Williams, Saad Qadeer, Amanda Howard, Panos Stinis

entry.summary: Extends the Mori-Zwanzig formalism for model reduction to bases discovered by physics-informed machine learning, using the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to close the resulting non-Markovian equations. Also introduces a complementary generative closure, with both approaches substantially improving filtered-state predictions over Markovian dynamics alone.

entry.title: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution

author.name: Dian Jin, Jinluan Yang, Kairong Han, Baohong Li, Zijing Hu, Yi He, Wenlin Zhong, Yunze Tong, Minqin Zhu, Linchuan Li, Yanan Niu, Kun Kuang

entry.summary: MDSKILL tackles noisy and redundant skill memories in self-evolving agents by organizing them into complementary views and applying multi-view distillation with On-Policy Self-Distillation to internalize knowledge into policy under limited training budgets. It aims to make RL-based agent self-improvement more sample-efficient and robust to noisy self-generated memories.

entry.title: SurgEye: Instruction Tuning-Free Perception-Reasoning Framework for Surgical Scene Understanding

author.name: Qing Xu, Xiechen Shen, Xianjian He, Guqiao Liang, Zixiao Chai, Jiale Qin, Yifan Chen, Siyi Li, Tian Yuan, Yiwei Li, Ziheng Meng, Zhen Chen
