They propose an oracle weighted neural estimator and prove minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors, with rates expressed via an effective sample size combining all sources.

entry.title: Deogen: Automatic Benchmark Generation for Reasoning over Policies

author.name: Sam Kouteili, William Liang, Keeran Murray, Adriana Zhou, Ramesh Viswanathan, Scott Shapiro, Ruzica Piskac

entry.summary: DeoGen automatically generates benchmarks for deontic reasoning — applying given rules to facts to reach a verdict — by autoformalizing policy rules into first-order logic and building decision trees whose paths become benchmark entries. Leaf paths entail verdicts while non-leaf paths measure a model's ability to recognize indeterminate situations. This replaces costly hand-crafted deontic reasoning datasets with scalable, parameterizable generation.

entry.title: Letting AI Formulate the Research Question: Autonomous Research Agents

author.name: Ko Fujimura

entry.summary: This work extends autonomous research agents beyond executing human-chosen questions by letting a coding agent formulate its own research question, using divergence, screening for known failure modes, cross-model critique, and independent peer review that reruns the study. The authors report all 13 development runs transparently.

entry.title: Revisiting Over-refusal in Safety-aligned Large Language Models: A Representation and Optimization Perspective

author.name: Chao Chen, Pengyang Shao, Wei Qin, Shijie Hao, Fei Shen, Richang Hong

entry.summary: The paper analyzes why safety-aligned LLMs still reject harmless queries, showing that harmful and over-refusal representations are distinguishable at intermediate layers but increasingly overlap in deeper layers, and that harmful-sample gradients concentrate in a low-rank subspace. These observations inform mitigation of over-refusal from a representation and optimization perspective.

entry.title: Agentic process evidence

author.name: Yuval Kainan, Carmit Hershman

entry.summary: The authors argue that AI agents acting as autonomous software developers are ephemeral, leaving no durable record of reasoning and tool calls, making accountability impossible after a session ends. They call for agentic provenance and governance standards so that intent-mismatch and injection incidents involving agents can be investigated, treating agents as potential insider threats.

entry.title: EpiAgent: Epistemic Self-Play for LLM Agents

author.name: Xuanfa Jin, Xinyu Cui, Zhijian Ma, Xue Yan, Jian Zhao, Haifeng Zhang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: EpiAgent equips LLM agents with an explicit learnable epistemic layer that maintains and updates beliefs about other agents' private information, decomposing the policy into epistemic update and action selection stages. The approach draws on epistemic game theory to improve decisions under incomplete information.

entry.title: Rank-Aware Differentially Private Release of Listwise Preferences for LLM Alignment

author.name: Junwei Chen, Manjiang Yu, Pengpeng Qiao, Yang Cao

entry.summary: The paper extends local differential privacy to listwise preference feedback for LLM alignment, where full rankings reveal more sensitive user data than pairwise comparisons. A rank-aware exponential mechanism reduces the noise burden of the high-sensitivity ranking space, with analysis of how supervision granularity interacts with privacy noise in downstream training.

entry.title: Echo: Scaling Visual Reinforcement Learning with Off-policy Experience

author.name: Gagan Khandate

entry.summary: Echo is a single-stage off-policy RL framework that scales experience collection without proportionally increasing visual computation by using inverse distillation: a cheap state-based auxiliary policy imitates the evolving visual policy and collects unrendered experience for off-policy value learning. This avoids the imitation gap of standard teacher-student distillation for visual policies.

entry.title: Calculation and rejection diverge in language models tested at known mechanical limits

author.name: Shaoliang Yang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: This controlled study tests whether language models can judge the physical feasibility of engineering designs by placing beam loads and disk speeds at known percentages beyond plastic collapse or burst limits, evaluating 12 models over 4,860 calls. The key finding is a divergence between calculation and rejection: models that correctly flag an impossible design when asked only about feasibility will still report it as solved when asked for a full answer, with some models accepting beams 10-30% beyond collapse.

entry.title: MEV: A Multi-Event Video Dataset for Long-Take Generation

author.name: Peiyuan Zhu, Shaoan Xie, Yifan Shen, Wen Tian, Zijian Li, Guangyi Chen, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: MEV is a dataset of high-quality real-world multi-event videos with precise temporal boundaries and fine-grained procedural annotations, designed to supervise long-take text-to-video generation. It addresses the weakness of existing short-clip, single-event datasets that lead to temporally inconsistent generations. The event-centric structure enables temporally localized conditioning for video models.

entry.title: FlipJev: Fast Black-Box Red Teaming Finds Universal Adversarial Suffixes for Typed Decision Models

author.name: Xiaogeng Liu, Xinyan Wang, Chaowei Xiao

entry.summary: FlipJev is a black-box, query-based red-teaming attack targeting typed decision models such as Jev, which answer in a single fast query rather than generating free text. Across 12 datasets it finds universal adversarial suffixes without requiring an attacker LLM, showing Jev resists common prompt injections but remains vulnerable to this attack class.

entry.title: Clean Sheets and Checkpoints: Evidence Complexity for Certifying Sequential Agent Risk

author.name: Rohith Yanambaka Venkata, Don McBride, Tiago Sequeira, Md. Al Amin

entry.summary: Develops a statistical framework for certifying that an AI agent's completion probability is at most epsilon given B clean-sheet (zero-success) audit responses, modeling dangerous-capability evaluations as chains of milestones divided into checkpoint segments. The bounds cover adaptive deployment processes under success-probability caps, formalizing what absence of failures actually proves.

entry.title: Raincheck: Deferred Multimodal Prefill for Efficient Multi-Turn MLLM Inference

author.name: Wenjie Huang, Jun Zhang, Hongyaoxing Gu, Haoyang Huang, Tianqi Xu, Xinyue Hao, Xinyi Hu, Xinle Du, Jun Dai, Shuang Ge, Chen Lei, Yue Li, Mingcheng Wan

entry.summary: Raincheck decouples initial token selection from later availability in multi-turn multimodal LLM inference: unselected tokens from query-aware pruning are progressively prefilled using unused decode-time compute and scheduling gaps, with attention visibility control ensuring correctness. This reduces time-to-first-token without permanently discarding information later questions may need.

entry.title: Latent Prediction Yields Cross-Subject Alignable Representations in Sensory-Evoked fMRI

author.name: Serwan Jassim, Victoria Bosch, Daniel Anthes, Elia Bruni, Tim Kietzmann

entry.summary: The authors adapt a joint embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) to train participant-specific self-supervised encoders directly on brain fMRI data from the Natural Scenes Dataset, without exposure to stimulus images, and evaluate the resulting brain embeddings on brain captioning, image reconstruction, and cross-participant generalization. The work shows SSL can yield strong downstream performance in neuroimaging. This matters for both neuroscience methodology and the study of representational alignment between brains and models.

entry.title: How I Aligned Your Model: Scaling Up Multilingual Safety Training with Templates

author.name: Max Neuwinger, Hanna Yukhymenko, Imanol Schlag

entry.summary: The authors propose a scalable template-based augmentation pipeline that extracts safe templates from harmful prompts, translates them, and fills slots with culturally authentic harmful and benign entities to produce multilingual refusal corpora. They release MSafeTemp, a validated corpus spanning 60 languages for multilingual safety alignment and evaluation.

entry.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers

author.name: Jiongfan Yang, Weichen Fan, Haiwen Diao, Zhongang Cai, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces SpecSlot, a pixel-space rectified-flow Transformer that decouples output detail from global attention sequence length by expanding each spatial anchor into multiple slots with disjoint bands of DCT coefficients. The key insight is that low-frequency structure benefits from global exchange while high-frequency detail can be modeled locally, avoiding quadratic cost growth for finer detail.

entry.title: HotPOT: Operator Transformer with Heterogeneous Physics Experts for Large-Scale PDE Pre-training

author.name: Jiayi Li, Guancheng Zhou, Yisi Luo, Ruihua Chen, Penghao Jiang, Deyu Meng, Flora D. Salim, Piotr Koniusz

entry.summary: HotPOT introduces an operator transformer for multi-PDE pre-training that combines a shared encoder with heterogeneous physics experts, where each PDE family gets a specialized expert architecture reflecting its distinct state evolution. This improves on homogeneous mixture-of-experts designs by reducing cross-task interference among equations with different governing physics.

entry.title: Logical Guidance of Stochastic Interpolants

author.name: Gerrit Gerhartz, Francesco Alesiani, Jonathan Warrell, Henrik Christiansen, Matheus Ferraz, Mathias Niepert

entry.summary: This paper develops exact logical composition of conditional velocity fields for flow matching and stochastic interpolants, showing negation and exclusive disjunction compose exactly on any interpolant while conjunction is exact only on Gaussian paths. LOGSI uses score-based re-equilibration as a principled correction mechanism for composable generative guidance.

entry.title: Rennala NSGD: Asynchronous Stochastic Optimization Beyond Euclidean Geometry

author.name: Igor Sokolov, Alexander Tyurin, Peter Richt\'arik

entry.summary: This paper analyzes minibatch stochastic gradient descent for smooth nonconvex optimization under arbitrary norms in finite-dimensional spaces, motivated by matrix-aware optimizers like Muon and Shampoo used in LLM training. Using the framework of kappa-regular normed spaces, it derives high-probability oracle complexity bounds including for distributed settings.

entry.title: Is It the Curriculum or Just the Easy Start? Benchmarking Unsupervised Environment Design on Quadrupeds

author.name: Jakub Gilewicz, Dominik Galus, Piotr Wojdas

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates fourteen UED, domain randomization, and robotics curricula under one protocol on five 3D quadruped robots in MuJoCo MJX, using interpretable terrain parameter vectors and matched environment-step budgets with a shared PPO student. It addresses the gap that UED methods are usually compared only on simple 2D tasks while legged-robot curricula are hand-designed.

entry.title: Revisiting Temporal Link Prediction through Structural Proximity

author.name: Yuzhang Fei, Yanping Zheng, Lu Yi, Zhewei Wei

entry.summary: The authors show that a simple, training-free structural measure, Personalized PageRank on historical interaction graphs with sliding-window or exponential time decay, matches or beats learned temporal link prediction methods across 14 datasets, ranking first on nine. They analyze historical paths to unseen destinations to explain why this classical baseline is so competitive.

entry.title: PALATE: Pretrained Autoregressive LATent Embeddings

author.name: Sizhang Zhao, Praveen Gondhi, Bin Li, Utsaw Kumar

entry.summary: PALATE trains a GPT-style generative model over a consumer's engagement sequence at a marketplace and uses the last-token hidden state as a learned per-consumer representation for the production ads ranker, replacing hand-engineered history signals. It demonstrates a deployable approach to personalization from sparse, high-cardinality interaction histories at production scale.

entry.title: Bayes-Consistent Losses for Adaptive Inference in Classification

author.name: Shirley Xiaoqi Liu, Florence Regol, Antonios Valkanas, Patrick Rebeschini, Mark Coates

entry.summary: The paper proposes cost-sensitive hinge losses for jointly training classifiers with single-stage or cascade routers in adaptive inference systems that balance accuracy against inference cost. The authors prove linear calibration bounds establishing Bayes consistency for these losses in both routing settings. This fills a principled-theory gap for joint model-router training, an increasingly important topic for efficient LLM deployment.

entry.title: 3DCodeEdit: Benchmarking Instruction-Guided 3D Program Editing

author.name: Binjie Wang, Xinran Zhao, Shoubin Yu, Xiang Li, Silong Yong, Chenyang Yang, Tianyu Chen, Ruofei Du, He He, Chen Zhao, Tongshuang Wu

entry.summary: Introduces 3DCodeEdit, a benchmark of 2,592 instruction-guided editing tasks over 108 Blender programs that construct 3D objects in code, spanning parameter, structural, style, and scene-composition edits judged via renders against human-reviewed checklists. Across 17 models the average success rate is only 37%, revealing that current LLMs are weak at understanding and editing existing 3D programs. Fills a gap between generation-only and simple-edit benchmarks.

entry.title: Implicit Minor Detection from Multi-Turn Dialogue in High-Risk AI Interactions: A Constrained Self-Evolving LLM Harness

author.name: Xiaohan Zhang, Ying Zhao, Ruilin Guo, Xuanyuan Yu, Kaibo Huang, Yukun Wei, Zhongliang Yang, Linna Zhou

entry.summary: The paper formulates implicit detection of whether a dialogue partner is a minor, using only weak conversational cues when identity signals are absent, as a prerequisite for age-conditioned safeguards. It proposes a constrained framework with an LLM, a self-evolving Harness, and a Maker-Checker protocol that requires structured evidence and version-level review. This is a safety-relevant capability with significant privacy and misuse considerations.

entry.title: XLaw-JP-27B: A Lightweight Open Model Specialized for Japanese Law

author.name: Andrew Shin

entry.summary: XLaw-JP-27B is an Apache-2.0 open-weight model specialized for Japanese law that runs on a single 48GB GPU, built by adapting Qwen3.8-27B, an existing base model released earlier in 2026, with hybrid retrieval over statutes and case summaries, QLoRA self-distillation on verified bar-exam answers, and a contract-specific LoRA adapter. It is evaluated on eight Japanese legal tasks against 12-33B open models under identical conditions. It demonstrates a practical recipe for domain-specialized legal models.

entry.title: Don't Lose the Thread: Empowering Long-Horizon LLM Agents with Cognitive Resource Self-Allocation

author.name: Zheng Zhu, Xiaozhuan Liang, Xi Chen, Bei Yu, Jiaya Jia

entry.summary: CORAL introduces a reasoning paradigm where LLM agents proactively manage their own context: an agent-callable toolset lets the agent checkpoint progress and verified facts, then reset a cluttered context to start a fresh episode. This mitigates cognitive overload on long-horizon tasks where irrelevant accumulated information dilutes attention. It is relevant to improving agent reliability on extended reasoning tasks.

entry.title: IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation

author.name: Shaohan Yu, Jie Qin, Wende Tan, Haiwen Diao, Limeng Qiao, Yueming Lyu, Chenyang Si

entry.summary: IntReal provides two resources for multimodal interleaved generation: IntReal-100K, a real-world dataset of interleaved text-image samples across four categories, and an evaluation suite with fine-grained protocols diagnosing unified multimodal model performance across capability dimensions. It targets the underexplored task of jointly generating naturally interleaved content.

entry.title: Kinematic Causal Attribution: Black-Box Explanations of Motion versus Geometry for 4D Point-Cloud Video Models

author.name: Zerui Wang

entry.summary: Kinematic Causal Attribution is a black-box interventional attribution method for 4D point-cloud video models that separates motion cues from shape cues using a freeze operator and a shape-free proxy, requiring only access to model outputs. It targets deployment safety checks for robots, monitoring, and AR applications.

entry.title: FutureWorld: A Plug-and-Play Causal Next-State Predictor for Interactive Video World Exploration

author.name: Guangyuan Li, Kelu Yao, Shuolin Xu, Xinlei Yu, Wei Xing, Lei Zhao, Peng-Tao Jiang, Xiaogang Xu, Xiaobin Hu

entry.summary: Proposes FutureWorld, a plug-and-play causal next-state predictor for interactive video world models that anticipates future scene states to limit error recirculation caused by reusing flawed generated latents as history, improving consistency over extended interactions.

entry.title: DINOv2 for PET: A Pre-Training Domain Benchmark Across Classification, Segmentation, and Prognosis

author.name: Roxanne De Maeyer, Yannick Brackenier, Vicky De Ridder, Simon DeKeyser, Maarten Larmuseau, Jef Vandemeulebroucke

entry.summary: This work introduces PET-DINOv2-2D, the first DINOv2 model pre-trained on 2D PET imaging, and benchmarks it against natural-image DINOv2 and OmniRad encoders across classification, segmentation, and prognosis tasks. It fills a gap since self-supervised features are known to transfer poorly from natural images to functional imaging like PET.

entry.title: Self-Labeled Preference Transfer for Steerable Robot Manipulation

author.name: Kaiwen Hong, Shaoting Peng, Xiangyu Zeng, Pengcheng Wang, Boyuan Tian, Haonan Chen, Yifan Zhu, Yixiao Wang, Katherine Driggs-Campbell

entry.summary: The paper studies transferring preference control in vision-language-action policies to new tasks whose demonstrations lack preference annotations, showing a tension between task success and preference following after naive fine-tuning. It proposes Self-Labeled Preference Transfer, where the policy generates its own preference labels on target-task data to retain steerability while improving success.

entry.title: Tracking Task Progress Through Errors and Recovery:A Benchmark and Recurrent Distributional Model

author.name: Chen Wang, Xinze Niu, Zihao Zhu, Keru Zhou, Yicheng Xu, Shihao Jin, Wenhao Wang, Bowen Jiang, Chang Zhou, Li Liu, Maoqing Yao

entry.summary: The authors introduce ReSTEP, an open-source dataset of 3,156 manipulation episodes with semantic stage labels and frame-level error annotations capturing mistakes and recovery, plus a recurrent distributional progress-monitor model. Progress estimation that distinguishes stalling, regression, and recovery is crucial for evaluating long-horizon robot execution. The benchmark fills a real gap since existing datasets rarely annotate error recovery.

entry.title: Don't Risk It!: Trajectory-Conditioned Distributional Risk for LiDAR-Only Crowd Navigation

author.name: Mathai Mathew Pulicken, Laksh Nanwani, Basant Sharma, Phani Teja Singamaneni, Arun Kumar Singh, K. Madhava Krishna

entry.summary: DRIP is an end-to-end LiDAR-only crowd navigation planner that couples occupancy forecasting with trajectory-conditioned clearance and uncertainty estimation, predicting a distribution over minimum robot-obstacle clearance for candidate control sequences. Training uses a risk cost grounded in empirical collision outcomes rather than geometric regression. Closed-loop experiments with up to 45 pedestrians show higher success rates than baselines.

entry.title: SwapBot: Tool-Centric Robot Manipulation via Interchangeable End-Effectors and Tactile Sensing

author.name: Yunchu Zhang, Ray Song, Junhan Jiao, Liyiming Ke, Yuchen Yang, Ruihan Gao, Emma Romig, Siddhartha Srinivasa, Yiyue Luo

entry.summary: SwapBot is a modular tool-centric end-effector system where low-cost adapters convert common household tools into robot end effectors via a fixed robot-side coupling interface, paired with tactile sensing. Rather than pursuing a single universal gripper, it enables autonomous swapping and use of task-appropriate tools for contact-rich everyday tasks like cutting, brushing, and precise placement.

entry.title: J-Lens can't detect what a subliminal learning teacher is transmitting (in 7B-32B models)

author.name: shawnghu

entry.summary: The author reproduces the subliminal learning effect (models acquiring traits like owl preference from teacher-generated data) and finds that J-Lens, a logit-lens-style interpretability probe, rarely detects the teacher thinking about owls, even in a Gemma-4-31B model. This challenges interpretations of J-Lens as reading a global workspace and suggests subliminal trait transmission bypasses forward-pass-readable representations.

entry.title: ThinkJev: One Thought, Every Budget for Calibrated Typed Decisions

author.name: Xiaolu Ding, Kai Yang, Dongdong Liu

entry.summary: ThinkJev builds fast (System 1) and slow (System 2) decision pathways from a single hybrid-thinking language model, reading option-letter probabilities from direct answers or post-reasoning on a cached prompt. It uses calibration signals to decide when to pay for reasoning, targeting typed decisions like arithmetic, counting, and date comparison at controlled compute cost.

entry.title: Evaluating Causal Reasoning in LLMs: A Case Study in the Challenges of Procedural Generation

author.name: Justin Clarke, Isha Karn, Patrick Murray, KJ Hill, David Jensen

entry.summary: Re-examines CLadder, a widely used procedurally generated benchmark for formal causal reasoning in LLMs, identifying superficial and highly predictive patterns its generator embeds in test data. The paper questions what strong LLM performance on CLadder actually demonstrates, highlighting risks of procedural generation in benchmark construction.

entry.title: Investor's Last Exam: Can AI Agents Do Equity Investment Without Seeing the Future?

author.name: Huangfei Jiang, Anning Hu, Kai Sheng, Yuchen Cai, Rui Ge, Xiangyu Kong, Jianghao Lin, Shuzi Chen, Jiyi Weng, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: ILE is an equity-research benchmark co-led by experienced buy-side investors, built on a versioned database of 3.43 million document versions with validated timestamps so agents are evaluated strictly on decision-time information. It includes a professional task taxonomy and evaluation criteria to test the full investment research process without lookahead.

entry.title: Auditable Belief Updates as a Missing Safety Layer for LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Zhuoyun Li, Boxuan Wang, Jinwei Hu, Xiaowei Huang, Yi Dong

entry.summary: The paper defines belief as an engineering abstraction for evidence-based commitments guiding downstream action and proposes EB-MAS, a multi-agent architecture that externalizes belief states into a structured substrate with belief operators for proposing and auditing updates. This makes how agents update, store, and propagate epistemic commitments across retrieval, memory, tools, and peers inspectable. The goal is a safety layer beyond isolated harmful-output filtering.

entry.title: Bank-World: A Benchmark for Evaluating Agents on Banking Workflows

author.name: Daniel Rupawalla

entry.summary: Bank-World is a benchmark of 50 banking tasks across two simulated institutions requiring agents to reconcile records, obtain permissions, execute transactions, and maintain consistency across single- and multi-turn interactions with simulated employees. Evaluation over 1,600 attempts by four models shows correct decisions often fail to translate into correct actions.

entry.title: Prefix Executability: Evaluating Tool-Using Agents Beyond Final Success

author.name: Amir H. Rezaeian, Weiyi Sun, Yassine Benajiba, Dan Roth

entry.summary: The paper proposes prefix executability, a trajectory-level protocol that measures whether every prefix of an agent's tool-call sequence remains executable under tool schemas, state preconditions, and data dependencies, summarized via metrics like Prefix Executability Curves and First-Error Depth. It is instantiated on BFCL-v3, ToolSandbox, and tau3-bench samples.

entry.title: One Confidence Threshold, Unequal Coverage: Language Gaps in Typed Decision Interfaces and How Translating Inputs Reduces Them

author.name: Junwei Yao, Yongxi Zhou, Zike Yang, Zhijun Wang, Jianan Liu, Yanxian Chen, Wenbo Ye

entry.summary: A confirmatory study of three vendors' typed decision interfaces across 1,000 MASSIVE items in 51 languages finds English requests clear a 0.9 confidence threshold 8.6-11.7 percentage points more often than other languages, yielding unequal automated coverage. Translating inputs into English before classification reduces these gaps.

entry.title: Towards Generalizing Pretrained All-Atom Representations to Unified Binder Design

author.name: Maojiang Su, Jiale Chen, Qijie Zhu, Shang Wu, Jiayi Wang, Jihai Zhao, Guo Ye, Yibo Wen, Han Liu

entry.summary: PairFuse is a parameter-efficient method that generalizes pretrained all-atom biomolecular representations to unified binder design across modalities by fusing them with geometric latent diffusion models via lightweight layerwise adapters. It combines the strengths of PairFormer-based all-atom models and shared-latent diffusion approaches for protein, peptide, and broader molecular binder design.

entry.title: What Should a Navigator Remember? Spatiotemporal Memory for Zero-Shot Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Yuhang Peng, Zhikai Wang, Ziyi Wang, Jiaru Zhong, Xiaoji Zheng, Jingzhi Huang, Yi Wang, Jiangtao Gong

entry.summary: The paper explores what an 8B-scale zero-shot vision-language navigation agent should retain from past observations, combining instruction progress, hierarchically compressed pose-anchored observation history, and accumulated geometry across task, temporal, and spatial memories. An 8B observer summarizes observations while an 8B reasoner selects waypoint intents and a geometric controller executes them. It provides a principled, semantic-information perspective on memory design for VLN without navigation-specific training.

entry.title: SpaceAct: Benchmarking 3D Spatial and Temporal Reasoning via Closed-Loop Action and Active Perception

author.name: Chenglong Shi, Zekai Yuan, Yue Song, Jon Pu, Will Wu

entry.summary: SpaceAct is an interactive benchmark testing 3D spatiotemporal reasoning of multimodal LLMs via closed-loop physical action and active perception, built on interlocking bricks and mechanical puzzles with 108 verified instances across 36 task families. It also introduces SAPA, a spatiotemporal active-probing agent framework. Unlike passive VQA benchmarks, it demands execution, collision awareness, and timing, making it a stronger probe of embodied spatial competence.

entry.title: Autonomous Quantum Measurement with Agentic AI

author.name: Eunbi Rha, Abhijatmedhi Chotrattanapituk, Mouyang Cheng, Chung-tao Chou, Shenyong Ye, Ashley S. Dale, Long Ju, Luqiao Liu, Mingda Li

entry.summary: The authors present QUANTA, an agentic AI framework for autonomous characterization of quantum materials on a Physical Property Measurement System, combining retrieval augmentation over literature, protocols, and prior measurements with specialized agents for planning, troubleshooting, and data interpretation. A deterministic control layer validates instrument commands for safety.

entry.title: Benchmarking Graph Neural Networks for AC Power Flow: The Role of Inductive Biases and Physical Constraints

author.name: Federico Clerici, Ferran Bohigas-Daranas, Hamid Latif-Mart\'inez, Eduardo Prieto-Araujo, Oriol Gomis-Bellmunt, Pere Barlet-Ros

entry.summary: Builds a unified benchmark of GNN architectures for AC power flow prediction under identical preprocessing, training, and parameter budgets, isolating the effects of message-passing mechanisms and inductive biases, and analyzes errors relative to distance from the slack bus. It brings much-needed experimental standardization to a fragmented literature important for grid analysis.

entry.title: Sparse Fine-Tuning for Parameter-Efficient Adversarial Training

author.name: Zhaoxin Wang, Zihang Ding, Handing Wang

entry.summary: Through gradient analysis, the authors identify Robustness-Critical Parameters (RCPs) on which adversarial optimization concentrates, and show that sparse fine-tuning of these parameters closes the robustness gap that LoRA-style parameter-efficient adversarial training suffers relative to full-parameter training, while cutting memory cost.

entry.title: Event-SAMA: Language-Grounded Video Object Segmentation on Neuromorphic Event Streams

author.name: Sergei Fedorchenko, Max Zehnder, Nikola Zubi\'c, Rong Zou, Davide Scaramuzza

entry.summary: The paper introduces Event-SAMA-239K, a large synthetic event-stream dataset converted from the SAMA grounded video-chat corpus with all mask, referring-expression, and dialogue annotations preserved, plus Event-SAMA, a model adapting a 4B-parameter VLM with polarity patch embeddings and a zero-initialised event adapter. It enables referring video object segmentation on neuromorphic event data with strong end-to-end results on MeViS.

entry.title: UPPAAi: Towards LLM-Assisted Modeling, Verification, Analysis and Synthesis

author.name: Peter Dolog, Kim G. Larsen, Marius Miku\v{c}ionis, Frederik F. K. Rasmussen

entry.summary: This paper introduces UPPAAI, an extension of the UPPAAL toolchain for modeling and verifying real-time and cyber-physical systems in which an LLM assists users with model construction, specification, debugging, and explanation, while UPPAAL itself performs formal verification. The architecture follows a propose-and-verify pattern where the LLM orchestrates but the verifier checks correctness, exposing the editor, queries, and verifier through a Tools API. It matters because it grounds unreliable LLM outputs in formal methods for safety-critical system design.

entry.title: A Unified Hessian-Guided Framework for Post-Training Quantization

author.name: Mads Toftrup, Marco Federici, Boris van Breugel, Paul Whatmough, Markus Nagel

entry.summary: The paper derives a Hessian-guided approach that unifies previously separate post-training quantization decisions — range selection, linear transformations, and weight rounding — under a task-aware objective rather than independent local reconstruction losses. This targets high accuracy at low bit precision for efficient LLM deployment. It matters because unified optimization of quantization choices could yield better accuracy-efficiency trade-offs than the current patchwork of methods.

entry.title: Application of PDE emulators for a multi-material, multi-physics simulation problem

author.name: Diane Oyen, Morgan Jones, Adithan Kathirgamaraju, Abu Bucker Siddik, Alexander Most, David Schodt, Christine Sweeney, Kyle Hickmann, Michael McCann, Jemma Stachelek, Alexius Wadell, Michal Kucer, Mahindra Rautela, Siddharth Mansingh, James Amarel, Gerd J. Kunde, Emily Casleton Taylor, Soumi De, Ayan Biswas, Aimee Hungerford, Nathan Debardeleben, Earl Lawrence

entry.summary: A large Los Alamos-affiliated team evaluates several computer vision-based PDE surrogate architectures on a challenging multi-material, multi-physics computational physics task, revealing significant implementation challenges especially for transformer-based pretrained models. The results provide guidance on where popular benchmarks overstate readiness for industrial applications.

entry.title: Learning from Relative Action Credit for Escaping Local Minima

author.name: Giovanni Minelli, Giulio Turrisi, Lorenzo Amatucci, Victor Barasuol, Claudio Semini

entry.summary: This RL paper traces PPO failures on long-horizon contact-rich robotic tasks to missing action discrimination in state-value credit assignment and extends PPO with an action-conditioned value providing relative action credit. The modification helps policies escape converged partial solutions and discover sparsely rewarded events in robot manipulation.

entry.title: Last-Iterate Convergence for Constrained MDPs: From Dual Descent to Primal-Dual

author.name: Michael Lu, Max Qiushi Lin, Mo Chen, Sharan Vaswani

entry.summary: The paper analyzes policy optimization for infinite-horizon discounted constrained MDPs, providing a new dual descent analysis without coverage assumptions and then employing entropy regularization to obtain last-iterate convergence guarantees for practical primal-dual methods. This moves guarantees from impractical mixture policies to the single policies actually deployed.

entry.title: Exposure Is Not Commitment: Double-Stratified Evaluation of Latent Monitors for Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Rishabh Sinha

entry.summary: Arguing that conflicting results in probing latent monitors for unsafe agent actions stem from an evaluation artifact, the paper proposes double stratification separating prompt-injection exposure from behavioral commitment. Monitors trained on naive mixed contrasts mostly learn exposure, while retraining on exposed cases only lets the same probe families predict the model's own unsafe tool calls up to twice as well.

entry.title: FAD-KV: Adaptive Dictionary KV Caching for Efficient Reasoning Decoding

author.name: Yuxuan Zhu, David H. Yang, Parisa Shiravani, Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri, Tejaswini Pedapati, Subhajit Chaudhury, Keerthiram Murugesan, Pin-Yu Chen

entry.summary: FAD-KV is a dictionary-based sparse KV cache compression method that represents token KV states as sparse combinations of learned atoms, targeting efficient long-output reasoning. It addresses overheads of iterative sparse coding during decoding, and results from an IBM-affiliated team (Pedapati, Chaudhury, Murugesan, Chen) show improved efficiency for long-generation reasoning workloads.

entry.title: Blind Spots: Where Small Language Models Fall Behind Frontier Models on Terminal Tasks

author.name: Ashima Suvarna, Ruta Desai, Ahmed Elgohary

entry.summary: This paper decomposes the gap between small language models and frontier models on terminal/agent tasks into three axes: solvability (whether extra test-time compute closes the gap), verification (whether the SLM can identify successful candidate trajectories), and confidence. The analysis offers a more actionable picture than aggregate task success rates, informing where small models can be viably deployed on edge devices.

entry.title: TabCUQ: Context-Uncertainty Quantification for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Yuebei Shi, Molei Liu, Zijian Guo

entry.summary: TabCUQ is a perturbation-based framework for uncertainty quantification of tabular foundation model estimates of conditional outcomes and treatment effects, jointly accounting for limited-context bias and context variation from small inference-time labeled samples. It identifies failure modes of bootstrap and subsampling approaches and proposes a corrected procedure.

entry.title: Conformal Annotation with Randomized Expert Review: Application to Online Cell-Type Labeling

author.name: Xuhe Zhang, Zhi Huang, Ying Jin

entry.summary: CARED is a distribution-free framework combining conformal methods with randomized expert audits to control long-run error rates of AI-assisted annotation under distribution shift, applied to cell-type labeling in digital pathology. For each incoming batch, it selects a subset for expert review and uses feedback to maintain error control as cell morphology and composition drift across slides. This directly addresses safe deployment of AI labeling in evolving clinical workflows.

entry.title: Deeper Backpropagation or More Updates? Training Looped Language Models Across Budgets

author.name: Jiarun Shen, Xiao Li

entry.summary: This work studies looped language models, where transformer layers are repeated to add depth without parameters, and analyzes the tradeoff between backward-window length (per-token learning efficiency) and per-update compute cost. It examines whether conclusions about optimal backward windows hold as training budgets scale. The findings inform parameter-efficient architecture choices for training under varied compute budgets.

entry.title: Multi-View MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation

author.name: Zelin Zhao, Tianchi Ma, Junyuan Shang, Shuohuan Wang, Dianhai Yu

entry.summary: The paper observes weak agreement between single-router rankings and dense expert-utility evaluations in sparse MoE models, especially in middle and deep layers, and proposes Multi-View MoE, which uses multiple routers to improve expert selection and reuses their preferences to modulate expert computation. This aims to improve capability under a fixed active-expert budget. It addresses a core limitation of sparse MoE architectures.

entry.title: It Takes Two to Probe, Thousands to Retrieve: Putting Vision--Language Probes to the Retrieval Test

author.name: Ivana Be\v{n}ov\'a, Michal Gregor, Mari\'an \v{S}imko

entry.summary: Investigates how image-text matching probes (with handcrafted negatives) relate to retrieval performance where the correct item must beat thousands of alternatives, using SVO and SugarCrepe with human and LLM annotation over retrievals from six VLMs. Results show probe accuracy does not reliably predict retrieval quality, questioning how well common evaluation proxies transfer.

entry.title: From Next Day Wildfire to Next Days Wildfire: A New Multi-Continent Dataset of Active-Fire Spread for Sequence-to-Sequence Forecasting

author.name: Jose Guillen, Renzo Zanca, Valentin Barriere

entry.summary: Introduces AFSeq, the largest and most diverse wildfire-spread dataset to date, with 1,194 fire events from 2023-2026 across eight countries and three regions, deliberately covering the short, small fires underrepresented in benchmarks like WSTS. It also proposes UTAE-AR, a recurrent-enhanced U-Net temporal autoencoder enabling multi-day sequence-to-sequence fire spread forecasting.

entry.title: TRIM: Temporal Run-Time Monitoring of 3D Object Detection via Activation Statistics

author.name: Hakan Yekta Yatbaz, Konstantinos Koufos, Mehrdad Dianati

entry.summary: TRIM is a lightweight run-time monitor that detects missed safety-critical objects in 3D object detection by summarizing detector activations with channel-wise statistics and processing short temporal sequences with a temporal convolutional network. It requires no detector modification or retraining and exploits temporal evolution of occlusion and sparsity.

entry.title: DiFuse: Fusing Native Diffusion Representations for Spatial Reasoning in Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Ruixin Fan, Weining Wang, Jiahui Sun, Tailai Chen, Jing Liu

entry.summary: Investigates whether intermediate representations from a unified multimodal model's diffusion branch can enhance spatial reasoning, proposing DiFuse, which selectively injects diffusion representations into the understanding pathway based on systematic layer-wise analysis of where they are most informative.

entry.title: PhysInsert: Physically Plausible Object Insertion with Geometric Priors and Bidirectional Object-Scene Interactions

author.name: Yue Gong, Le Zhang, Rui Chen, Song Chang, Xiaochao Qu, Luoqi Liu, Ting Liu, Yebin Liu

entry.summary: Presents PhysInsert, a framework for reference-based object insertion that jointly adapts objects and surrounding scenes with physically plausible pose and illumination, using geometry-guided adaptation with a VGGT geometry stream and bidirectional object-scene interaction modules. The authors also release Insert World, a dataset of strictly aligned Blender-rendered counterfactual pairs with object references across viewpoints and lighting.

entry.title: EgoContact: Evaluating Physical Intelligence with Egocentric Video

author.name: Adam Dery{\l}o, Alexey Gavryushin, Daniel Cremers, Marc Pollefeys, Xi Wang

entry.summary: EgoContact is a large-scale egocentric dataset of 22.5K manually verified interaction events with pre-contact observations, semantic intent, and pixel-precise contact locations, designed to evaluate manipulation priors via future contact-point prediction. The authors find current methods struggle with this task. It repurposes abundant egocentric video as a validation tool for physical intelligence, complementing its use in policy pretraining.

entry.title: Learning Event-based Obstacle Avoidance via Differentiable Simulation

author.name: Chenlu Shou, Yunfan Ren, Jiaxu Xing, Davide Scaramuzza

entry.summary: The paper presents a CUDA-based GPU-parallel event camera simulator enabling differentiable simulation for training closed-loop obstacle avoidance policies for quadrotors, avoiding error-prone cascaded depth-estimation pipelines and costly offline pretraining. Event cameras offer sub-millisecond latency and high dynamic range suited to fast flight in unknown environments.

entry.title: Assuring Learning-Enabled Cyber-Physical Systems with Foundation Models: A Neuro-Symbolic Agenda for Testing, Verification, and Runtime Assurance

author.name: Xi Zheng, Ivan Ruchkin, Hong Jin Kang, Tevfik Bultan, Vijay Ganesh, Taylor T. Johnson, Ziyang Li, Lei Ma, Aloysius K. Mok, Daniel Neider, Ruzica Piskac, Nalini Venkatasubramanian, Simon Thompson, Sanjoy Baruah

entry.summary: A position/agenda paper from a large multi-institution author team proposing a Foundation Model Assurance Stack for learning-enabled cyber-physical systems, spanning neuro-symbolic architectures, conformance-based testing with formal specifications, and runtime assurance. It argues for shifting from model-centric evaluation to system-level guarantees. This frames a research program for safe deployment of foundation models in autonomous vehicles and UAVs.

entry.title: Orthogonal Inference for Conditional Z-Estimation without Cross-Fitting: A Distributional Nearest-Neighbor Approach

author.name: Jakob R. Juergens

entry.summary: This work develops pointwise inference for conditional moment equations, including conditional average treatment effects, using full-sample nuisance predictions while avoiding cross-fitting. It localizes estimating equations around the reporting point with distributional nearest neighbors built from U-statistic averaging, breaking the dependence between fitted scores and evaluation points.

entry.title: What Does an Ontology Catch? Curated, LLM-Generated and Data-Derived Ontologies as Checkers of LLM Agents over Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Michal Orzechowski, Rund Tawfiq, Tomasz Kosciolek

entry.summary: This study makes the ontology-based checker itself the object of analysis, comparing curated, LLM-generated, and data-derived ontologies as validators for LLM agents answering questions over knowledge graphs, including a private graph with nearly a billion triples. It measures when checkers miss errors and when they wrongly flag correct answers, assessing whether formal schemas are worth their cost as judges.

entry.title: SkillMem: Compact External Skill Memory for Latent Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Yuxuan Zhu, Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri, Pin-Yu Chen, Keerthiram Murugesan

entry.summary: Introduces SkillMem, which represents reusable skills as compact external latent memories directly available during latent multi-agent reasoning, with a role-conditioned cross-attention reader letting one memory guide different agents by role. Skill memories and the reader are trained via behavioral distillation, avoiding repeated text processing or per-skill KV/model storage.

entry.title: Compute Has Shape: Self-Morphing the Internal Computation of Frozen LLMs

author.name: Junxi Wu, Yiwen Guo, Shu-Tao Xia

entry.summary: SelfMorph makes the topology of inference-time computation input-dependent for frozen LLMs, unifying a base forward path, serial layer reuse, and local branch-merge computation in one type-location-intensity space. A lightweight selector picks the computational shape per input, exploiting complementary benefits of the modes for test-time scaling.

entry.title: Co-Evolving Policy and Rubric via Capability Awareness for Open-Ended Generation

author.name: Chengsheng Zhang, Wenshen Xu, Yuchuan Wu, Zhiyuan Yu, Junfeng Fang, Tianlong Wang, Bingxue Qiu, Yongbin Li, Xiang Wang

entry.summary: CoCA addresses the mismatch between static rubric criteria and an evolving RL policy in rubric-based reinforcement learning for open-ended generation. It co-evolves the policy and rubric in a closed loop where rubric difficulty tracks the policy's current capability frontier, keeping reward signals discriminative. This improves alignment of LLMs on tasks lacking verifiable rewards.

entry.title: Agentic AI Reasoning and Learned Sampling for Task-Aware Projection Selection in Sparse-View CT: Predicting Hemodynamics

author.name: Mahmoud Elhadidy, Roshan M. D'Souza, Amirhossein Arzani

entry.summary: This work optimizes which CT projections to acquire not for image reconstruction quality but for downstream physical inference, training a Fourier neural operator to predict wall shear stress in intracranial aneurysms from sparse CTA measurements. An agentic reasoning loop with learned sampling selects projections jointly with model training. It demonstrates that task-aware acquisition can outperform reconstruction-centric sampling in medical imaging.

entry.title: Before the Next Rollout: Diagnosing Skill Utility Shifts from Policy Updates

author.name: Yifan Wang, Zhenyi Gai, Yiwen Zhao, Mingxuan Jiang, Keyang Chen, Zeping Li, Hongfeng Chai, Yixin Cao

entry.summary: The paper studies how policy updates change the marginal utility of unchanged skills in skill-evolution agent methods, making earlier trajectory-based attribution stale. The authors measure how updates alter token-preference contrast between skill and control conditions at fixed contexts, and combine these interaction signals to predict utility shifts before the next rollout. This enables better skill lifecycle management in RL-trained agents.

entry.title: DEG: Diffusion-Enhanced GFlowNet for Solving Vehicle Routing Problems

author.name: Ni Zhang, Zhiqin Zhang, Ling Pan, Hoong Chuin Lau, Zhiguang Cao

entry.summary: DEG combines GFlowNets with diffusion models for vehicle routing problems: GFlowNets provide edge-level signals that diffusion embeds, while diffusion supplies structural guidance for broader exploration in high-reward regions. This addresses limited solution diversity in neural VRP solvers.

entry.title: AegisFlow: Training-Free Non-Myopic Path-Safe Guided Flow Matching

author.name: Kunpeng Liu, Boshi Zhang, Keyou You

entry.summary: AegisFlow is a training-free method for steering generative trajectories of flow matching models to satisfy strict constraints, replacing myopic min-norm controllers with a non-myopic path-safe guidance scheme. This avoids trajectories hovering near constraint boundaries and improves optimization toward the target, with applications from identity-preserving editing to obstacle avoidance.

entry.title: Retrieving from Your Own Mistakes: On-Policy Training of Embedding Models for Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Chenjie Qiu, Zixuan Zeng, Shaobin Shi, Bingfeng Chen, Dongsheng Luo, Boyan Xu

entry.summary: The paper shows chain embedding retrievers trained only on gold histories are already strong for multi-hop RAG, but they degrade at test time because their own retrievals contain errors, with over half of third-step states holding a wrong passage. The proposed remedy trains embedding models on-policy, conditioning on their own retrieval mistakes.

entry.title: Supervised Fine-Tuning for Reasoning Large Language Models: A Survey

author.name: Yongcan Yu, Kuangpu Guo, Jian Liang, Lingxiao He, Meng Wang, Ran He

entry.summary: This survey consolidates the fast-growing literature on supervised fine-tuning with long chain-of-thought data for reasoning models, organized around methodological design (data-centric and algorithm-centric approaches) and analytical investigation. It aims to be the first systematic review of reasoning-oriented SFT.

entry.title: Search-Guided Reasoning Trace Curation for Verilog Generation

author.name: Matthew DeLorenzo, Kevin Tieu, Prithwish Jana, Piyush Jha, Dileep Kalathil, Vijay Ganesh, Jeyavijayan Rajendran

entry.summary: MCTS-SFT curates reasoning traces for supervised fine-tuning of Verilog generation models by formulating trace construction as search over intermediate reasoning states, using Monte Carlo Tree Search to propagate functional feedback from complete Verilog rollouts to earlier design decisions. Plan-MCTS searches over compact hardware-design plans.

entry.title: EUReCA: End-to-End Unified CBCT Reconstruction Across Clinical Acquisitions

author.name: Jiening Zhu, Chengzhu Zhang, Jason Fan, LiCheng Kuo, Weixing Cai, Xiuxiu He, Laura Cervino, Jean Moran, Xiang Li, Tianfang Li, Yabo Fu

entry.summary: EUReCA is a geometry-aware feed-forward model for cone-beam CT reconstruction that handles 8 to 100 projections with a single set of weights, avoiding view-count-specific retraining, and extends unchanged to other clinical trajectories. It combines learned projection features with an in-frame FDK reconstruction to address the ill-posedness of low-dose, few-view radiotherapy imaging.

entry.title: MUSE: Multi-Level Memory with Selective Runtime Injection for Scientific Coding Agents

author.name: Haoran Jin, Defu Lian, Xiting Wang, Hong Xie

entry.summary: MUSE is a memory-management framework for scientific coding agents that maintains global, approach-level, and implementation-level memory from historical trajectories, injecting implementation lessons selectively at runtime via an LLM gate. Across four benchmarks including numerical problem solving and kernel optimization, it improves over task-level retrieval alone. It highlights that execution-time lessons are often missed by standard retrieval.

entry.title: Learning Scientific Trajectories to Predict Future Biomedical Discoveries

author.name: Chia-Hsuan Chang, Brian Ondov, Jiang Lv, Lan Jiang, Yunmai Wang, Haerin Song, Xueqing Peng, Qiaozhu Mei, Xiaolei Su, Hua Xu

entry.summary: ForeSCITE is a framework for AI-guided hypothesis generation that identifies thematic clusters of biomedical conclusions, estimates a direction from older to newer findings within each cluster, and projects embeddings along those directions to generate natural-language hypotheses via a decoder model. It is built on approximately three million pre-cutoff conclusions across 407 clusters.

entry.title: Implicit Reasoning in Transformers: Bridging the Compositionality Gap in GPT-2-like Models

author.name: Davide Venuto, Leonardo Venuto

entry.summary: Studies the compositionality gap in a GPT-2-like model trained from scratch on a two-hop reasoning task, testing whether out-of-distribution failure stems from how atomic facts are structurally presented during training. By aligning training formats positionally with the reasoning circuit, the authors probe how training distribution shape affects compositional generalization.

entry.title: DeCoRL: Decomposed Consistency Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Image Composition

author.name: Zhiqiang Wu, Shuang Sun, Jiale Zhang, Jing Li, Yibo Chen, Xu Tang, Yao Hu

entry.summary: Proposes DeCoRL, an RL framework improving multi-image composition consistency in image editing models by decomposing holistic consistency into object-level consistency: it first establishes instruction-relevant object correspondences across reference images, localizes regions in the generated image, and applies decomposed rewards. This addresses rapid consistency degradation as reference image count grows beyond what SFT can fix.

entry.title: Integrating Heterogeneous Echocardiography AI Outputs in Language Space: Learnable Late Fusion with a Supervised LLM

author.name: Ryo Takizawa, Tempei Kabayama, Chiemi Yamazaki, Shun Kitamura, Ryo Matsuoka, Yuta Ando, Satoshi Kodera, Norihiko Takeda

entry.summary: The authors build a supervised LLM-based late-fusion module that aggregates view-specific echocardiography AI outputs (predicted findings and measurements) directly in language space, learning a case-level fusion function without forcing heterogeneous outputs into fixed vector formats. Evaluation on 859 examinations from 646 patients shows improved integration over baselines.

entry.title: SCARL: Sequence Confidence-Aligned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhenghong Ke, Jingbo Zhou, Hua Wu

entry.summary: SCARL addresses a misalignment in RLVR training where a policy's confidence in a response is not tied to its reward — lucky successes earn the same update as near-certain ones and confident errors are not penalized harder. The method reshapes the reward/update structure so that responses with the same advantage move toward equal confidence, aligning sequence-level confidence with verifiable-reward signals. This targets better calibration and more efficient learning in reasoning-model RL.

entry.title: Sometimes less is more: Investigating inductive biases of MLPs and Transformers on noisy k-parity features

author.name: Alasdair Paren

entry.summary: Using controlled noisy k-parity synthetic datasets, this work shows that Transformers are more robust to noisy features but struggle with complex low-availability features, while MLPs show the opposite trend and improve steadily with data. Notably, under a fixed budget, adding more unique training examples can slow Transformer optimization enough to hurt performance.

entry.title: Learning a Prior-Data Fitted Network for Graph Foundation Models via Structural Causal Model Priors

author.name: Ziwei Zhang, Tianyin Liao, Chunyu Hu, Ge Lan, Nuo Xu, Yi Huang, Qingyun Sun, Xingxuan Zhang, Peng Cui, Jianxin Li

entry.summary: This paper builds a graph foundation model by training a prior-data fitted network (PFN) on large synthetic datasets generated from structural causal model priors, addressing weaknesses of existing graph PFNs in modeling causal relationships, generating diverse structures, and architecture design. It offers a route to transferable graph representations without relying on LLM text alignment.

entry.title: Closed Gates Leak: Decomposing Adjacent-Layer Cancellation in Gated Language Models

author.name: Harvey Dam, Ganesh Gopalakrishnan

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study decomposes adjacent-layer cancellation in gated MLP transformers, showing that the damping term is carried by neurons whose gates are closed, and traces how SiLU and GELU slightly negative activations below zero produce leakage from closed gates. It refines the earlier proposal-and-rejection view of residual-stream cancellation. A careful contribution to understanding transformer internals.

entry.title: Softmax Routing Dynamics in Mixture-of-Experts Models: Collapse and Recovery

author.name: Shengze Xu, Maolin Deng, Tieyong Zeng

entry.summary: This paper provides a theoretical analysis of softmax routing collapse in mixture-of-experts models, characterizing how probability concentration on a subset of experts forms, persists, and recovers. It derives a stationary-loss barrier, an exact normal-velocity decomposition separating expert covariance from gradient advantage, and results on interior routing limits under adaptation dynamics.

entry.title: TACFormer: Transformer-Based Generative Model for Target-Conditioned De Novo PROTAC Design

author.name: Yossra Gharbi, Roc\'io Mercado

entry.summary: Presents a transformer-based generative model for de novo design of PROTACs, heterobifunctional molecules for targeted protein degradation. Unlike prior methods that treat design primarily as linker generation, it formulates the task as target-conditioned generation covering warhead choices for the protein of interest, enabling in silico exploration of PROTAC chemical space.

entry.title: Framework-Conditional Open Materials Generation

author.name: Maya M. Martirossyan, Hillary Pan, Philipp H\"ollmer, Stefano Martiniani

entry.summary: This paper proposes a generative paradigm for de novo prediction of inorganic crystalline materials constrained by structural frameworks, exploiting the heuristic that stable, unique, novel structures typically come from novel compositions mapped onto known prototypes. It bridges data-mining substitution methods and fully generative approaches by conditioning generation on framework structure.

entry.title: FORGE: Feasible Online Reduced-Order Reference Generation and Whole-Body Execution for Agile Humanoid Locomotion

author.name: Adrian B. Ghansah, Yujin An, Jeeseop Kim, Soon-Jo Chung

entry.summary: FORGE is a two-stage learning framework for agile humanoid locomotion coupling a command-conditioned reference generator trained in reduced-order model space with a whole-body tracking policy trained on full-order dynamics. The kino-dynamically consistent generator supports a broad command space and multiple locomotion strategies within one unified framework.

entry.title: Pair-Dependent Judge Errors Change the Minimax Rate of Semantic Entropy

author.name: Jiamiao Liu, Dewen Qiao, Yu Zhang, Xuetao Chen

entry.summary: This theory paper extends the minimax analysis of semantic entropy estimates for LLM outputs to judges whose false-equivalence probability varies by answer pair, showing the statistical rate changes and is governed by tree statistics on four or five sampled answers. It refines the theoretical foundation for uncertainty quantification of language models based on sampled-answer consistency.

entry.title: How Much Should a VLA Trust Its Reasoning? Step-Level Guidance as a Measured Action-Value Function

author.name: Dabin Seo, Eunhyek Joa

entry.summary: This paper reframes reasoning in vision-language-action policies from a binary question (is the reasoning correct?) to a continuous one (how strongly should it steer?). CoC-CFG applies classifier-free guidance between context with and without the reasoning span, tuning the per-step guidance weight via an MDP formulation whose action values are directly measured rather than bootstrapped. This offers a principled control mechanism for the growing class of reasoning-enabled robot policies.

entry.title: Multi-Draft On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Drafters

author.name: Petr Molodyk, Yuchen Zhu, Jaemoo Choi, Molei Tao, Yongxin Chen

entry.summary: Addresses a training problem in speculative decoding with one-step diffusion drafters: parallel drafting creates a mismatch because the drafter predicts tokens without seeing same-block prefixes while the verifier conditions on them, so distilling against separate verifier targets can suppress plausible tokens. The paper proposes multi-draft on-policy distillation that resolves this target-conflict. Directly relevant to reducing LLM inference cost.

entry.title: Can LLMs Ignore What They Know? Measuring Knowledge Leakage in Persona-Based User Simulation

author.name: Sangmin Lee, Sangwon Lee, Sungbeom Choi, Jeeseung Park, Kibeom Myoung

entry.summary: This work identifies knowledge leakage in persona-based user simulation: when LLMs simulate low-knowledge respondents, they fail to suppress model knowledge the simulated user could not have. The authors define the problem quantitatively using real items paired with matched fabricated twins and find persistent rating separation even under explicit ignorance prompts. It matters for the validity of LLM-based synthetic survey respondents and behavioral simulations.

entry.title: Lost in the Latent Space: How Code Embeddings Represent Functional Intent and Implementation Fidelity

author.name: Lu Sun, Yuheng Huang, Lei Ma, Zhijie Wang

entry.summary: A large-scale empirical study of 14 state-of-the-art code embedding models examining whether a single embedding can simultaneously support functional abstraction and implementation-sensitive analysis, using supervised probing, zero-shot retrieval, and controlled perturbation experiments. The results illuminate trade-offs in the geometry of code representations.

entry.title: Don't Ask the LLM: Visual Token Pruning with Spectral Structure and Semantic Relevance

author.name: Intaek Shin, Geuntaek Lim, Sungjune Park, Yukyung Choi

entry.summary: ST-Pruner is a visual token pruning method for large vision-language models that selects tokens before LLM computation, combining spectral structural coherence with query-aware semantic relevance. It addresses complementary failure modes: CLS-attention selections are background-biased under aggressive compression, while strong query-conditioned signals arrive too late in the LLM.

entry.title: RuleForge: Inferring and Instantiating Latent Visual Rules as Executable Programs

author.name: Weifeng Xu, Yaxiong Wang, Zhedong Zheng

entry.summary: RuleForge jointly learns visual rule understanding and rule-conditioned executable program generation, accompanied by Bongard-Forge100k, a 108K-problem benchmark with held-out rule-composition tests. The work connects abstract concept inference from few examples with reliable program instantiation.

entry.title: AlbumVSR: Identity-Preserving Face Video Super-Resolution from a Personal Photo Album

author.name: Nianyao Du, Xijun Wang, Stanley H. Chan

entry.summary: AlbumVSR conditions a frozen one-step streaming diffusion transformer on a personal photo album as an external identity source for face video super-resolution, using set tokens and texture tokens from a fused UV atlas injected into cross-attention. It substantially improves identity similarity and PSNR on a heavy-degradation VoxCeleb2 benchmark.

entry.title: BRIDGE: Learning Brain-Gut Metabolic Evidence for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis

author.name: Pengli Zhu, Ruxi Chang, Tianliang Yao, Yu Jiang, Shengyuan Liu, Yiyang Lin, Xiaoyi Duan, Shuang Wu, Yixuan Yuan, the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative

entry.summary: Presents BRIDGE, a two-stage framework that transfers brain-gut metabolic knowledge from paired whole-body FDG-PET to brain-only diagnosis via a conditional brain-to-gut latent transport module, exploiting gut metabolic signals linked to brain-gut interactions for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis.

entry.title: SCOPE: Semantic COdec Pre-Editing for Object-Preserving Compression

author.name: Silvia Dani, Leonardo Galteri, Marco Bertini

entry.summary: SCOPE is a conditional image pre-editor that modifies images before standard compression to improve the rate-detection-accuracy trade-off for machine vision, protecting task-relevant regions while simplifying compressible backgrounds. It is conditioned on codec family and compression severity so one network adapts to multiple codec settings without retraining.

entry.title: Hierarchical Step Decomposition for Training-free Online Video Step Grounding

author.name: Long Zhou, Luca Zanella, Paolo Rota, Massimiliano Mancini, Elisa Ricci

entry.summary: Proposes HSD, a training-free framework for online video step grounding that uses large multimodal models to build semantically coherent temporal segments from streaming video and bridge the gap between coarse procedural step descriptions and visual observations. It avoids the noisy, over-segmented outputs of fixed-length-segment online baselines without requiring offline access to the full video.

entry.title: Accurate MRI-free PET Quantification and Reliability Assessment via CT-to-MRI Synthesis and Conformal Prediction

author.name: Jungwoo Seo, Seung Yun Choi, Kun Ho Lee, Seun Jeon, Byoung Seok Ye, Jiook Cha

entry.summary: Combines slice-consistent Brownian Bridge Diffusion-based CT-to-MRI synthesis with conformal prediction to enable MRI-free amyloid PET SUVR quantification with calibrated reliability estimates. The diffusion model is strengthened with multi-dataset training, data-source conditioning, and expanded multi-slice CT context, and synthetic MRI supports FreeSurfer parcellation for clinical workflows where MRI is unavailable.

entry.title: Fight World Model: Customizable Combat through Visual Interaction Proxies

author.name: Jiahua Li, Zixu John, Tom Zhong, Fuping Wu, Tianhao Xu, Ruicheng Zhang, Jun Zhou, Zunnan Xu

entry.summary: The Fight World Model (FWM) separates rule-governed combat execution from video rendering by using an executable engine to maintain state and a deterministic compiler to encode outcomes into a spatially and temporally aligned interaction proxy. This enables video world models where hit reactions, health, and game rules remain consistent and controllable. It advances playable, programmable game world generation beyond purely visual video synthesis.

entry.title: SKiD-SLAM: Resource-Aware Distributed Multi-Robot LiDAR SLAM for Planetary Missions with Field Deployments at Analog Sites

author.name: Hogyun Kim, Juwon Kim, Dongjin Cho, Jiwon Choi, Geonmo Yang, Seokhwan Jeong, Jiyun Lee, Miryeong Park, Hyungtae Lim, Younggun Cho

entry.summary: SKiD-SLAM is a distributed multi-robot LiDAR SLAM system designed for planetary exploration under severe communication and compute constraints, with modules for inter-robot place recognition, relative pose estimation, and distributed trajectory fusion. It was validated on public datasets and field-deployed in two planetary mission analog scenarios: cave exploration and surface science.

entry.title: RAIBO-Wagon: Real-Time Navigation System for a Legged Robot Towing a Wagon

author.name: Insung Yang, Eunchae Kim, Jungwoo Hur, Seunghun Jeon, Donghyuk Choi, Jemin Hwangbo

entry.summary: A real-time navigation framework for legged robots towing an underactuated wagon, combining Conditional Flow Matching with MPPI control over a learned forward model to find feasible paths in confined spaces. Coupled robot-object dynamics make towing navigation substantially harder than self-only locomotion. This extends legged robot autonomy toward practical payload-towing scenarios.

entry.title: RoboSeed: Multidimensional Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action and World-Action Models: Capability, Resource Affordability, and Research Evidence

author.name: Xin Ma, Furong Chen, Xinlong Man, Bo Zhang, Yalong Guo, Haolan Lei, Chaochen Cui, Hongyuan Zhang, Mulin Chen, Yi Wang, Lap-pui Chau, Chuang Yang

entry.summary: RoboSeed proposes a multidimensional evaluation framework for VLA and world-action models spanning five dimensions: capability, downstream training affordability, deployment affordability, locally verified research value, and reproduction evidence. It maps measurements and audit criteria to 0-100 profiles, part of a program to openly release robot models with verifiable selection evidence. The framework moves beyond success-rate-only comparisons for model selection.

entry.title: PhysVLMM: Interaction-Conditioned Physical Belief Maps for Articulated Objects in Robot Scene Maps

author.name: Dibyendu Ghosh

entry.summary: PhysVLMM extends Vision-Language-Motion maps with a physical belief for every articulated part of objects, answering planner queries about how parts will respond to pulls. The paper proves that passive observation cannot identify a part dynamics and that a measured pull identifies only the pulled part up to one direction, so it maintains posterior beliefs over motion directions, propagates evidence in closed form to look-alike parts, and supports success-probability queries.

entry.title: Integrating multi-source local information for global undirected graph reconstruction via integer programming

author.name: Nir Keret, Armeen Taeb, Ali Shojaie

entry.summary: A framework for reconstructing a shared global graphical model from heterogeneous, partially overlapping data sources that may not share raw data, using integer programming to integrate local conditional independence graphs or summary statistics. Identifiability is established up to the equivalence class induced by observed variable sets under a source-wise faithfulness condition.

entry.title: Seq@K: Evaluating Language Models Under Sequential Feedback

author.name: Thomson Yen, Gilbert Yang, Naimeng Ye, Minghui Chen, Dong Xia, Tianyi Shen, Yechan Jeon, Yaqin Chen, Daksh Mittal, Fangyu Wu, Hongseok Namkoong

entry.summary: Introduces Seq@K, an evaluation protocol measuring whether a language model can solve a problem within K sequential attempts using natural-language feedback after each failure. Unlike Pass@K metrics or long-horizon agentic benchmarks, it isolates the core capability of in-context refinement from feedback.

entry.title: GAAC: Lossless KV Compression for Bandwidth-Efficient LLM Inference on Personal Devices

author.name: Yipin Guo, Arun M George, Siddharth Joshi

entry.summary: GAAC is a lossless KV cache compression system exploiting BF16 exponent redundancy with group-adaptive additive codes, preserving KV values bit-for-bit while reducing storage. A fused attention kernel reconstructs KV tiles on the fly, targeting long-context LLM inference on memory-constrained personal devices.

entry.title: Accelerating Nonlinear MPC by Behavior Cloning with Separated Timescales: Application to Nuclear Reactor Load-Following

author.name: Perceval Beja-Battais (CB), Alain Grosset{\^e}te (CB), Nicolas Vayatis (CB)

entry.summary: The paper proposes SRLBC, a structured behavior-cloning architecture that separates slow variables, fast stiff variables, and exogenous inputs into distinct representations for multiscale dynamical systems. It is evaluated on 500 long-horizon rollouts of a pressurized water reactor load-following benchmark with strict safety constraints. The goal is to distill nonlinear MPC into a fast learned controller without losing closed-loop generalization.

entry.title: Kairos: Semantics-Aware Orchestration of Planning Engines across Classical, Numeric, Temporal and Hybrid PDDL

author.name: Francisco Mart\'in Rico, Esther Aguado Gonz\'alez, Francisco Miguel Moreno Olivo, Rodrigo P\'erez Rodr\'iguez, Jos\'e Miguel Guerrero Hern\'andez, Francisco J. Rodr\'iguez Lera

entry.summary: Kairos is a meta-planning system that profiles PDDL tasks semantically to route them among five heterogeneous planning engines, covering fragments from STRIPS to PDDL+. It aims for broad coverage of classical, numeric, temporal, and hybrid planning while remaining competitive with specialized planners and making the guarantees of each answer explicit.

entry.title: Long-Term Agent Memory through Complementary Curation and Consolidation

author.name: Abhishek Gupta, Dongge Han, Daniel Madrigal Diaz, Wei-Ning Chen, Mayukh Das, Victor R\"uhle, Saravan Rajmohan

entry.summary: The authors propose a hybrid memory architecture combining episodic and structured relational memories with a consolidation mechanism for long-horizon dialogue agents. Across LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S benchmarks, the combination is consistently complementary, outperforming state-of-the-art memory frameworks with 90.2% on LoCoMo and 85.5% on LongMemEval-S.

entry.title: Human--AI Interactions as First-Class Data: A Formal Interaction Model and Runtime for Explainable AI Collaboration

author.name: Michela Taufer, Kin Ng, Ian Lumsden, Aashish Pandey, Rajasi Gore, Angelina Ju, Sukanya Moudgalya, Ewa Deelman, Sai Swaminathan

entry.summary: This paper introduces HAIDL, a formal Human-AI Interaction Description Language with a BNF-inspired syntax that treats human-AI interactions as durable, structured data products rather than transient prompt-response exchanges. The goal is to enable reproducibility, replay, behavioral analysis, and adaptive AI support across notebooks, scientific workflows, and software tools.

entry.title: Locating and Closing Information Gaps in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yaxin Gong, Chongming Gao, Gangyi Zhang, Chenxiao Fan, Leyang Shen, Jiakai Wang, Dong Wang, Yang Liu, Haoyan Liu, Xinting Hu

entry.summary: SPLICE addresses a failure mode of fixed multi-agent communication graphs on web tasks: evidence retrieved by one agent may never reach the agent that needs it. The method locates per-query information gaps, decides when to insert communication edges, and guards against adopting incorrect upstream conclusions that displace correct answers.

entry.title: Prompt-agnostic Language Models

author.name: Frederic Sadrieh

entry.summary: This work builds prompt robustness into models during instruction tuning rather than relying on inference-time prompt optimization. It shows per-paraphrase gradients interfere during training (57% exhibiting sign conflicts, naive averaging discarding about a fifth of gradient magnitude) and proposes two gradient-merging methods, Prompt-TIES and Prompt-DARE, to mitigate this.

entry.title: The Coordination Tax and the Heterogeneity Dividend: Break-Even Conditions for Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines

author.name: Andreas Zettl, Diego Gosmar

entry.summary: The paper gives a closed-form model weighing multi-agent pipeline coordination costs against savings from routing tasks to cheaper heterogeneous models, with a break-even threshold and feasibility bound. It measures every term using the Open Floor Protocol over 135 HumanEval and ClassEval tasks across 2430 runs with Claude Opus 5.5, an established frontier model.

entry.title: Predicate Neuron: Differentiable Quantization of Predicate Relations in Gradient-based Learning

author.name: Ioannis Konstantoulas, Iliana Loi, Kyriakos Sgarbas

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Native Predicate Neuron, a differentiable neural module that adds first-order logic symbolic reasoning to standard deep architectures. It uses a single trainable parameter to alternate between logical operations and a dual-nature gradient mechanism that executes hard logical operations during training while remaining differentiable for backpropagation.

entry.title: What Actually Matters? A Paired Evaluation of Inference Settings for $\pi_{0.5}$ on BEHAVIOR-1K

author.name: Ruben Hammele, Samira Huber, Mohammad Nazeri, Amirreza Payandeh, Alexandyr T. Card, Aaron Nguyen, Anuj Pokhrel, Daeun Song, Xuesu Xiao, S\"oren Pirk

entry.summary: The paper systematically and pairwise evaluates previously proposed inference and data-collection strategies across all 100 tasks of BEHAVIOR-1K using a fine-tuned pi-0.5 VLA model based on the 2025 BEHAVIOR Challenge winner. The key finding is that strategies successful in small-scale settings do not transfer uniformly to large, diverse task suites.

entry.title: Can Event Detectors Leave the Broadcast Camera? Evidence from Tennis

author.name: David Soeiro-Vuong, Andre-Louis Rochet

entry.summary: The paper releases a frame-level benchmark of 345 bounce and hit annotations across broadcast, fixed elevated, phone, and court-level viewpoints, with a confusion-aware matcher, bootstrap intervals, and blind second annotations. It shows supervised spotters trained on broadcast footage score near-perfectly on broadcast but almost nothing elsewhere, while zero-shot vision-language models and an arbitration layer (RallyArb) over ball tracks and poses behave differently.

entry.title: Predicting What Answer Engines Cite: Open Decision Models, Rerankers and a Distilled 4B Student on Ten Engines under Controlled Retrieval

author.name: Elisha Bajemon, Andre-Louis Rochet

entry.summary: This paper studies generative engine optimization by building scorers that predict which candidate web pages answer engines will cite. The authors benchmark pretrained rerankers, hosted and open decision models, and a fine-tuned Qwen3-Reranker-4B student (GEO Citation Ranker 4B) against ten answer engines on GEO-Bench queries under controlled retrieval, finding that large decision models lead at roughly 0.575-0.578 Spearman correlation while the distilled 4B student approaches them.

entry.title: Beauty Is Human: When People Love AI-Generated Art, They Think a Human Made It

author.name: Zihan Chen, Di Zhu, Lei Nico Zheng

entry.summary: This study analyzes data from a large-scale online AI Art Turing Test in which over 11,000 participants judged whether 50 pictures (26 AI-generated) were human-made and picked a favorite. The key finding is a strong attribution bias: respondents were about 22 percentage points more likely to judge their favorite picture as human-made, an effect that held across both AI and human works and was robust across multiple checks. The work matters because it shows that aesthetic preference systematically distorts perceived authorship, complicating how people detect AI-generated content.

entry.title: CuraEval: Evaluating Demonstration Curation on Mixed-Skill Robot Data

author.name: Jiuyi Xu, Meida Chen, Yang Ye, Yangming Shi

entry.summary: CuraEval is a framework for evaluating whether robot demonstration-curation scores actually beat simple baselines, using controlled comparisons against size-matched random subsets and full-data training on mixed-skill robomimic data with Diffusion Policy and BC-RNN. The authors show that a commonly used PSD score depends only on episode length and squared position magnitudes, exposing it as nearly uninformative. This matters because it challenges the rigor of data-selection practices in robot imitation learning.

entry.title: WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One Agent From Narration to Long-Form Video

author.name: Chenyu Mu, Wenming Weng, Qinrui Wang, Xingsong Ye, Hao Yu, Jun He, Chong Sun, Chen Li, Jing Lyu, Erkun Yang, Cheng Deng

entry.summary: WeVisCut is a long-form script-to-video system pairing an agent harness with shared production state and policy learning, trained via a four-stage pipeline that combines editing inversion with verified replay to recover editing intent from 3,750 finished videos as supervision. It investigates the quality-cost trade-off of compact, task-adapted policies versus multi-stage workflows built on general models. This is a substantive system contribution for automated video production.

entry.title: SaiVLA-JEPA: Evaluating Future Latent Prediction in JEPA-Conditioned VLA Control

author.name: Rufeng Xiao (VLA Research Team, Synthoid.ai), Ruihao Xiao (VLA Research Team, Synthoid.ai), Wei Chen (VLA Research Team, Synthoid.ai), Xinhai Sun (VLA Research Team, Synthoid.ai)

entry.summary: This work tests whether JEPA-style future latent prediction improves closed-loop robot control when the policy already uses V-JEPA visual features. SaiVLA-JEPA combines a vision-language model with a diffusion transformer action expert, adding lightweight auxiliary heads that predict future representations during training only, and compares variants with and without JEPA conditioning and future supervision.

entry.title: Lev-3B: A Data Recipe for Compact Probabilistic Log Decision Models

author.name: Leo Betthauser, Yingqi Liu, Uday Shah, Jishang Wei, Sainyam Galhotra, Liang Gou, Vedant Dharnidharka, Hao Yang

entry.summary: Introduces Lev-3B, an open 3B-parameter model built on Granite-4.1-3B-Base for log-analysis decision tasks such as anomaly and attack-technique detection, using a curriculum that first trains bounded natural-language decisions without logs and then mixes target tasks with 35 auxiliary log tasks. It emphasizes calibrated probabilities and generalization to unseen log sources, which matters for practical security operations.

entry.title: TableTune: Measured, Self-Correcting Draft-Length Tables for Dynamic Speculative Decoding

author.name: Abhishek Malvankar, Paul Castro, Nick Mitchell, Lionel Villard

entry.summary: This paper introduces TableTune, a system for optimizing speculative decoding in LLM serving on vLLM.
