entry.summary: UnEZ is a fully unsupervised, physics-informed model that predicts spectroscopic redshifts and emission/absorption line strengths for galaxies without any labels, using an encoder that infers line parameters and a fixed deterministic decoder that reconstructs the spectrum. Tested on Sloan Digital Sky Survey data, it avoids reliance on curated templates or redshift catalogs that limit scalability of large spectroscopic surveys.

entry.title: Learning Kolmogorov Backward Operators for Spectral Analysis and Forecasting: A Data-Driven Variational Galerkin Framework

author.name: Yuanchao Xu, Claire Valva, Ben Gao, Isao Ishikawa

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage framework approximating the fixed-lag Kolmogorov backward solution operator directly from data (e.g., via Fourier Neural Operators), then compressing the Galerkin projection onto a chosen finite-dimensional observable space, with error analysis covering learning, sampling, and invariance/reconstruction properties. It enables deterministic linear evolution of observables for stochastic Markov processes.

entry.title: Robust LLM-Generated Text Detection through Matched Conditional-Response Probing

author.name: Junfeng Hao, Wenxian Wang, Tao Leng, Xingshu Chen, Hao Ren, Haizhou Wang

entry.summary: Introduces MCRP, a frozen-LLM probing framework for detecting LLM-generated text that measures how a candidate responds when a semantically matched condition is introduced, removed, or replaced, comparing token-level losses. Designed to stay effective under meaning-preserving edits like rewriting, polishing, expansion, and translation that defeat lexical and syntactic detectors. Addresses robustness, a central unsolved problem in AI-text detection.

entry.title: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker

author.name: Adilet Metinov, Chingiz Arziev

entry.summary: Glance merges reranking into the generator for retrieval-augmented generation: a lightweight decision adapter and pointer head score candidate passages from a shared prefill, avoiding separate reranker residency and per-pair prefilling. A single 9B model handles generation, decisions, and reranking with only ~0.1 GiB per decision skill, matching or beating bge-reranker-v2-m3 on SciFact and NFCorpus after brief fine-tuning. This is a practical efficiency contribution for RAG deployments.

entry.title: VEvo-Harness: Causally-Guarded Self-Evolving Harness for Agentic Image Generation

author.name: Yuan Wang, Yuhang Yu, Mengting Chen, Tianrun Xu, Zihao Pan, Xuetao Feng, Wei Li

entry.summary: VEvo-Harness is a causally-guarded continual self-evolving system for agentic visual generation that addresses the shallowness of generate-verify-rewrite loops by governing skill-library updates and preventing experience poisoning. It aims to convert trial-and-error iteration into a continual self-improving harness.

entry.title: CrossWeave: Cross-Modal Scene and Instance Retrieval from Sparse 2D-3D Alignment

author.name: Aadith Warrier, Gnana Prakash Punnavajhala, Siddharth Tourani, Muhammad Haris Khan, Avinash Sharma, Madhava Krishna

entry.summary: Shows that supervising a single model on sparse patch-point 2D-3D correspondences, without scene- or instance-level contrastive objectives, is sufficient for both scene-level and instance-level cross-modal retrieval between 2D images and 3D environments. This targets spatial reasoning applications in robotics and AR/VR where prior methods learn only whole-scene or whole-object alignment.

entry.title: TACOS: Terrain-Aware COntact Supervision for Visual Footstep Planning

author.name: Jean-Michel Fortin, William Larriv\'ee-Hardy, Gabriel Jeanson, Olivier Gamache, Daniele De Martini, Fran\c{c}ois Pomerleau, Philippe Gigu\`ere

entry.summary: TACOS derives a physically meaningful footstep instability score from factor-graph residuals in legged state estimation and projects it into preceding images to supervise a dense visual predictor, with hindsight (hard) and causal (soft) variants. This gives legged robots terrain-aware contact supervision grounded in actual stability rather than intuition-chosen labels. A solid step toward vision-driven locomotion planning on rough terrain.

entry.title: A Spectral Boundary for Independence Learnability

author.name: Senhan Yao, Yuxin Zhou

entry.summary: The paper identifies a class-level boundary for testing independence between time series from a single observation record, governed by shared nontrivial Koopman eigenvalues representing common persistent oscillatory frequencies. When no shared eigenvalues exist, it constructs a deterministic weakly consistent test via extended shift-based rank calibration with finite-window dependence witnesses.

entry.title: FilingLoop: Evaluating and Evolving LLM Agents for Corporate Disclosure Review and Revision

author.name: Wentao Zhang, Yilei Zhao, Guangyan Gan, Shuo Sun, Lin William Cong

entry.summary: Introduces FilingLoop, an interactive benchmark and self-evolving agent framework for corporate disclosure review built from 380 reconstructed SEC IPO review tasks across 96 companies grounded in real SEC correspondence. The benchmark tests discovering unstated deficiencies, acquiring missing facts, and verifying evidence-backed revisions, capabilities beyond standard financial QA.

entry.title: Assessing Language Models for Scientific Applications: Inertial Confinement Fusion as a Use Case

author.name: P. B. Radha, D. D. Meyerhofer, M. Bhattarai, B. Cheng, L. Diaz, C. L. Rousculp, A. G. Seaton, G. Gupta, P. Gurumurthy, V. Gutta, A. Jhunjhunwala, A. Vem, P. Cook, G. Rowe

entry.summary: Develops an expert-curated 250-question benchmark for inertial confinement fusion spanning qualitative reasoning, numerical calculation, symbolic derivation, and equation formulation, evaluated with deterministic numerical and symbolic checks plus model judges. Compares frontier closed- and open-source LLMs against Prospero, a model specialized via domain-adaptive pretraining and supervised fine-tuning for ICF.

entry.title: SkillCT: A Multidimensional Benchmark and Execution-Free Baseline for Agent Skill Assessment

author.name: Mengyu Sun, Zunlong Zhou, Ziyuan Yang, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: SkillCT is a benchmark assessing agent skills (packaged instructions, scripts, resources) across nine dimensions covering specification quality, behavioral robustness, semantic alignment, and responsibility boundaries. Its execution-free evaluation addresses the scalability limits of task-execution-based skill benchmarks and enables pre-deployment assessment.

entry.title: Can LLMs Faithfully Solve Ontology Engineering Tasks? A Mechanistic Interpretability Study

author.name: Bohui Zhang, Albert Mero\~no-Pe\~nuela, Elena Simperl

entry.summary: The paper introduces MIOE, a causal-abstraction benchmark using interchange interventions to test whether LLMs encode ontological knowledge (entity typing, subsumption prediction) internally rather than just behaviorally. It extends mechanistic interpretability from instance-level facts to ontological, class-level knowledge structures.

entry.title: From Leniency to Suspicion: How an Open Post-Training Recipe Changes Whom LLM Fact-Checkers Believe

author.name: Nouar AlDahoul, Yasir Zaki

entry.summary: The study examines job-based doubt in LLM fact-checking — judging claims as false more often when the poster has a lower-status job — across base and post-trained checkpoints of six model families with randomized poster profiles. It finds the bias emerges only with the open Tulu-3 post-training recipe, with effects under one percentage point but statistically reliable and exceeding training-drift baselines. The paper illuminates how post-training choices shape social bias in fact-checking.

entry.title: Efficient Agentic Audio-Visual Question Answering through Toolset Pruning and Modality Consolidation

author.name: Yi Wang, Tianzi Wang, Peter Bell

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether omni-modal AVQA agents need broad specialized toolsets, pruning the OmniAgent toolset down to essential perceptual capabilities and consolidating modality-specific tools. It shows comparable answer accuracy with compact workflows while reducing long execution trajectories and inference cost. This informs efficient design of active-perception agentic systems.

entry.title: Beyond LLM Wrappers: Context Engineering and the Three-Engine Architecture for Reliable Financial AI

author.name: Pradeep Kumar GS, Ravi Tanniru

entry.summary: The paper presents a production architecture for financial AI that combines a financial knowledge graph with provenance, a deterministic optimization engine for calculations, and a multi-agent LLM layer for interpretation and validation, coordinated through context engineering. The design targets numerical accuracy, traceability, and auditability that LLMs alone cannot guarantee. It offers a template for moving beyond naive LLM wrappers in regulated domains.

entry.title: Timbre: Reliability-aware harmonic consensus for label-free multimodal test-time rexinforcement learning

author.name: Haotian Lyu, Haoyu Wang, Ru Wang, Feng Ji, Ziwen Li, Jiaxian Guo, Mingming Gong

entry.summary: Timbre addresses failure of majority-voting pseudo-labels in label-free test-time RL for vision-language models, where consistent but wrong consensuses can form. It builds a 2x2 grid of original and perturbed images crossed with direct-solving and reframing modes, then selects pseudo-labels via weighted harmonic aggregation that accounts for how much each transformation degrades task evidence. This improves the reliability of self-supervised test-time adaptation.

entry.title: Emergence of the transformer architecture as the score of entropic laws of random measures

author.name: Giacomo Greco

entry.summary: The author derives the transformer architecture from first principles, showing it emerges as the score of last-token laws in a maximum-entropy statistical model of language where sentences are empirical measures of tokens. The derivation recovers the softmax choice rule with the attention cross-moment as its mean parameter via Luce's choice axiom.

entry.title: The Real Cost of Context: Predicting Compute Time and Energy Consumption in LLM Prefill and Decode Phases

author.name: Lars Krupp, Daniel Gei{\ss}ler, Francisco M. Calatrava-Nicolas, Stefan Gerd Fritsch, Paul Lukowicz, Jakob Karolus

entry.summary: The paper systematically profiles compute time and energy consumption of LLM inference across prefill and decode token lengths, showing decode scales linearly with output length while prefill exhibits additional regimes, and fits generalized linear models to predict costs. This enables estimating the energy footprint of agentic workflows that consume large input contexts.

entry.title: Hybrid AI Patterns: Thirteen Ways to Couple Language Models with Rules, and How to Choose Among Them

author.name: Siegfried Handschuh, G\"otz-Henrik Wiegand, Lorena Raichle

entry.summary: This work catalogs thirteen design patterns for coupling language models with executable rule languages, presented in the Gang-of-Four catalogue format covering intent, applicability, participants, and consequences. Patterns are organized by what crosses the model-rules boundary, control relationships, model participation in reasoning, and knowledge persistence.

entry.title: Neighborhood Elites: Quality-Diversity Search for Uncertainty Quantification in Question Answering

author.name: Mesut Ceylan, Arda Baris Basaran, Elgar Fleisch, Filipe Barata

entry.summary: The paper improves perturbation-based uncertainty quantification for QA by using quality-diversity search to construct controlled rewrite sets that explicitly vary the type of context change and how explicitly the context supports the answer. This removes generator-driven bias inherent in free paraphrasing or adversarial perturbation approaches.

entry.title: Where Planning Changes the Outcome of Orbital Games

author.name: Duncan Eddy, Mahdi Al-Husseini, Mykel J. Kochenderfer

entry.summary: OrbitalGym is a JAX-based simulation environment for adversarial orbital rendezvous games, designed to disentangle whether planning quality or vehicle capability determines outcomes. Unlike prior studies with passive defenders, it supports multi-agent differential-reward encounters with varying agents and state representations.

entry.title: Beyond Similarity Search: Knowledge Graph Metadata Enrichment for Enterprise Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Fakabbir Amin

entry.summary: The authors test whether a knowledge graph storing metadata and fast-changing information improves enterprise RAG retrieval over pure embedding similarity search. They evaluate on a snapshot of SEC EDGAR with over 167,000 filings and roughly 509,000 embedded chunks, using a knowledge graph of about 430,000 nodes to simulate metadata enrichment.

entry.title: Statistical Detection of Positional Bias in LLM-Based Recommender Systems: Methodologies and Empirical Evidence

author.name: Carlos Pel\'aez-Gonz\'alez, Francisco Herrera, Andr\'es Herrera-Poyatos

entry.summary: The paper studies positional bias in single-turn LLM-based recommenders built on RAG, where the recommended item depends systematically on candidate order in the prompt. It proposes two detection methods: POB-ICM using contingency tables and Chi-square tests, and POB-UNBP, a sample-efficient permutation-based test with formal statistical guarantees that supports stochastic decoding.

entry.title: Making Smart Homes Fit for Autistic Children: Family Work and Monitored Independence

author.name: Tingting Xiang, Weihan Jiang, Hrishitva Patel, Haiqi Shen, Tianzhi He, Kyrie Zhou

entry.summary: A multi-source qualitative study (caregiver interviews plus Xiaohongshu and Weibo posts) examining how general-purpose smart-home technologies support or hinder families with autistic children. It finds families do substantial ongoing work adapting outputs, prompts, and interaction channels, while sensory intensity and opaque device states create barriers.

entry.title: Measuring Deep Learning Performance - An Empirical Study of Performance Distributions Across Architectures and Tasks

author.name: Kevin L Coakley, Odd Erik Gundersen

entry.summary: This empirical study addresses non-determinism in deep learning by treating model performance as a distribution rather than a single number. The authors ran 186 experiments on image classification and time series forecasting architectures, each repeated 100 times with different random seeds (18,600 runs total), to characterize how performance distributions vary across architectures and tasks and what this implies for robustness.

entry.title: EARS-Info: Information-Aware Event-Driven Reallocation for Multi-Robot Exploration

author.name: Kabeh Mohsenzadegan, Vahid Tavakkoli, Kyandoghere Kyamakya

entry.summary: EARS-Info extends Event-Driven Ant Reallocation Search with information-aware elements such as marginal sensing gain, return-aware routing, sensing reservations, and cached shortest paths for multi-robot exploration on city-map grids. Across 168,000 episodes and 30 implementations on eight maps, it achieves the highest mean operational score, including under 3% communication dropout.

entry.title: Convex-SKM-Net: Low-Latency Block Halfspace Corrections for Neural Convex Constraint Satisfaction

author.name: Haoyu Zhu, Xiaochen Zhang, Qingchun Hou

entry.summary: Convex-SKM-Net is a differentiable convex constraint-satisfaction layer that forms linearization halfspaces from residual and gradient oracles, applying fixed-depth dual projected gradient descent with GPU-friendly matrix operations instead of constraint-specific projectors. The method jointly learns a predictor and a positive-definite mobility matrix, with proven convergence of the outer iterates and improved objective quality on constrained decision-making tasks.

entry.title: Vendster: An Evaluation Arena to Investigate How Forecasting Tool Quality Affects LLM Agent Behaviors in Buyer-Vendor Negotiation

author.name: Charin Polpanumas

entry.summary: Vendster is an evaluation arena measuring how a forecaster's bias and prediction-interval width affect outcomes of buyer-vendor discount negotiations between LLM agents, using the M5 dataset. It evaluates two closed-model families (Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.6 Sol) and two open ones (DeepSeek-V3.2 and Qwen3), all long-established models, as tool-consuming negotiators. The core idea is measuring decision value of forecasts rather than accuracy alone.

entry.title: Statutory Article Retrieval from Arabic Judicial Narratives: Family Law and Law of Evidence in Saudi Arabia

author.name: Zarah Shibli, Areej Alhothali, Lulwah Alharigy

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks retrieval of Saudi Arabian statutory articles from Arabic judicial narratives across 200 synthetic cases and 381 articles, comparing BM25 variants, dense encoders, reciprocal rank fusion, and a proposed Decompose-and-Refine pipeline that splits narratives into legal issues with multi-channel queries. It addresses the narrative-to-legal-rule abstraction gap in Arabic legal NLP. This is valuable for grounding legal reasoning in authoritative sources in a low-resource setting.

entry.title: Benchmarking decision models against generative large language models on medical multiple-choice questions

author.name: Oscar Freyer, Daniel Glauert, Moritz Hofmann, Max Ostermann, Stephen Gilbert, Jakob Nikolas Kather

entry.summary: The paper compares 13 specialized decision models with 15 generative LLM configurations on 1,273 MedQA questions, finding generative configurations reach higher accuracy (up to 96.86% vs 89.08%) while decision models offer advantages in cost and latency, e.g., Mercury Decide at USD 0.0069 per 1,000 questions. It also reports error rates among high-confidence predictions for decision models. A useful cost-accuracy-reliability trade-off analysis in medical QA.

entry.title: The Artificial Personality Model: Theory, Implementation, Measurement and Experimental Validation in Conversational Agents

author.name: Alexander Dregger, Barbarella Petz, Erik Kuhn, Pia Volk, Andreas Oberweis, Stefan Hillmann, Jannik Str\"otgen

entry.summary: This paper refines and empirically validates the Artificial Personality Model (APM), a hybrid framework combining human-centred and machine-specific personality dimensions for conversational agents, measured via the Artificial Personality Questionnaire (APQ). Across three experiments with 395 participants, factor analyses show some human dimensions partially transfer while others, like extraversion, do not, and machine-specific dimensions emerge.

entry.title: AtomTree: A Hierarchical Framework for State-Aware Embodied Instruction Following with LLMs

author.name: Haotian Zhai, Tianming Sha, Junnan Li

entry.summary: AtomTree is a hierarchical planning framework for embodied instruction following in which an LLM incrementally builds a tree of subgoals and actions, deciding at each step from the current symbolic state whether to decompose further or execute. This contrasts with one-shot planning approaches that commit to full plans upfront and only recover after failures.

entry.title: Representation Complexity Along Learning Trajectories: Trading Width for Precision and Time

author.name: Ryan Singh, Miguel De Llanza, Christopher L. Buckley

entry.summary: Introduces an oracle model of neural network learning using Kolmogorov n-widths to quantify representation complexity, distinguishing the complexity needed for prediction from that needed to make a target visible through gradient feedback. The main theorem transfers complexity bounds from forward representations to gradient-query features, giving a theory of why transient overparameterization helps learning.

entry.title: From Local Recovery to Unified Generation: Discovering Triple Set in Knowledge Graphs via Observation-Anchored Latent Diffusion

author.name: Jiaqi Wang, Yisen Gao, Huayang Shi, Junhao Hou, Wengen Li, Jihong Guan, Yichao Zhang, Shuigeng Zhou, Yangqiu Song, Hong Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes LatentDiff, a latent diffusion framework that reformulates knowledge graph triple set prediction as unified latent-space graph generation rather than independent subgraph completion, using a relation-aware residual-quantized encoder. This addresses fragmented reasoning and missing cross-subgraph predictions in existing completion paradigms.

entry.title: Soei: Structured Observability of Evidence and Intent for Multi-Agent AI Software Engineering

author.name: Mohammed Nayeem Khan, K S Sarun Kumar

entry.summary: Soei addresses observability for long-running multi-session AI coding agents, asking what was actually done, by whom, and whether it is finished. The work audits an existing open-source observability tool (finding an unauthenticated mutation surface among other issues) and prototypes its own system on 45 real coding-agent sessions covering over 100,000 records, with blind-audited results.

entry.title: SHPRR: An Algorithm for Pure Exploration under Constrained Regret

author.name: Georgina Nouli, Flore Sentenac, Maximilian Schiffer

entry.summary: The paper studies best-arm identification under both a fixed sampling horizon and a regret budget relative to a trusted baseline, noting that regret has distinctive structure since sampling better arms is cheaper. The authors prove the regret cost of exploration decreases across phases of Sequential Halving, yielding improved guarantees and motivating the SHPRR algorithm.

entry.title: One Vector or Many? Clustered Optimal-Transport Steering under Quantization

author.name: Illia Makarov

entry.summary: The paper analyzes activation steering methods for mitigating toxicity in small language models, comparing the simple difference-of-means (DiM) vector against clustered optimal-transport approaches like CHaRS, and proves an identity showing what the transport plan actually contributes. It further examines whether steering benefits survive INT8 and NF4 quantization in Gemma-2-2B and Granite-3.1-2B. This matters for understanding which inference-time interventions are practical in quantized deployment settings.

entry.title: Localizing Concepts in Visual Autoregressive Models

author.name: Nanxiang Jiang, Yang Liu, Yuanhao Wang, Min Xu

entry.summary: This work introduces LoCo, claimed as the first model-agnostic framework for localizing where and when specific concepts emerge within next-scale visual autoregressive generation models, mapping concept routing across layer, scale, and position dimensions. It also contributes LoCoBench, a dataset for evaluating concept localization without context bias. It matters because interpretability of autoregressive image generators lags behind that of diffusion models despite their growing adoption.

entry.title: Escaping Path Mirages in Offline Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Junhyeon Bae, Jaebak Hwang, Gwanwoo Choi, Minung Kim, Seungyul Han

entry.summary: The paper identifies the path mirage problem in offline goal-conditioned RL, where stochasticity in datasets leads agents to overcommit to spuriously successful trajectories, and proposes Branch-aware Graph Planning (BGP) to capture stochastic branching structures and avoid unreliable branches. This targets value estimation errors in stochastic long-horizon settings. It matters because reliable long-horizon goal reaching from offline data is a core open challenge in RL.

entry.title: CADENCE: Distributional Next-Transaction Forecasting for Business Cash-Flow Underwriting

author.name: Alexander Wu, Jingchao Huang

entry.summary: CADENCE is a compact causal Transformer treating transactions as tokens that predicts payment amounts plus full nonparametric timing distributions of next cash flows, with calendar-aware handling of recurrence conventions. It targets small-business cash-flow underwriting where ambiguous transfers and short histories make recurrence estimation hard.

entry.title: B2P-Corr: Batch-to-Population Gradient Estimators for Non-Decomposable Correlation Losses

author.name: Jingquan Yan, Yuwei Miao, Peiran Yu, Junzhou Huang

entry.summary: B2P-Corr addresses the bias and variance of naive mini-batch optimization of non-decomposable correlation metrics (PCC, CCC) by transforming them into decomposable pseudo-losses driven by lightweight global moment sketches. Two efficient variants bridge the batch-to-population gap so stochastic gradients align with population gradients.

entry.title: RainCheck: Harnessing Historical Weather Data with Machine Learning for Rainfall Forecasting in Bangladesh

author.name: Shahran Rahman Alve, Muhammad Zawad Mahmud, Samiha Islam, Al Jubayer Pial

entry.summary: This study evaluates machine-learning rainfall forecasting on 618,650 station-days from 35 Bangladesh weather stations (1948-2014), showing that random train/test splits leak information across neighboring stations and that a simple seasonal climatology baseline explains most of the variance. It matters because it exposes widespread methodological flaws in how ML weather models are benchmarked.

entry.title: How Much Do Teacher Bridges Matter in Interleaved On-Policy Distillation?

author.name: Leran Chen, Zhiyuan Yao, Lingnan Kong

entry.summary: This controlled study uses Qwen3-1.7B as student and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 as teacher to test whether teacher-written bridge segments in on-policy distillation help, comparing no loss, forward KL, and reverse KL on identical trajectories. It finds no measurable accuracy benefit from teacher bridges, whose gradient contributions are small and nearly orthogonal to student-token gradients.

entry.title: Two-Stage Clipping: Linear-Time Approximate and Exact Mixed-Norm Projections for Transformers

author.name: Michel Barlaud, Jean-Paul Marmorat

entry.summary: This paper introduces Two-Stage Clipping (TSC), a structured sparsification operator using l1,inf projections that reduces the cost of proximal methods from O(nm log(nm)) to linear time for transformer weight matrices. It enables efficient column-wise sparsity for LLM computational and energy savings.

entry.title: Auditable Hierarchical Inference with Multimodal Evidence and Bayesian Active Inquiry

author.name: Yucheng Liu, Everett X. Wang

entry.summary: This paper presents a synthetic evaluation framework for sequential clinical inference that separates objective multimodal classification (tongue, pulse, and acoustic signals mapped to syndrome families) from active inquiry via Bayesian narrowing with typed questions, while keeping safety questions outside the diagnostic posterior. It includes provenance tracking and preregistered evaluation with leakage probes. Its value lies in modeling the sequential, auditable nature of real clinical questioning rather than assuming all evidence is available upfront.

entry.title: A Novel Approach to Evaluating Evaluation Metrics for Multi-Output Structured Prediction

author.name: Akshay Vyas, Angelo Pimienta, Nicholas Ruozzi

entry.summary: The paper introduces approximate task-specific invariants (e.g., object boundaries in colorization, named entities in translation) as diagnostic tools for systematically testing the reliability of evaluation metrics in multi-output structured prediction, where multiple valid outputs exist. The framework stress-tests metrics by encouraging invariants in model outputs and observing metric behavior. It targets the important meta-problem of metric reliability.

entry.title: More Is Better? Exploring Latent Correspondence in Federated Hypergraph Learning

author.name: Bo Yan, Siming Zhang, Siqi Li, Hang Yu

entry.summary: This work studies federated hypergraph learning with latent cross-client hyperedge correspondence, proving that pairwise assignment is tractable while multi-client hyperedge matching is generally intractable. Building on a cross-entropy decomposition showing when local prediction can outperform predictors with extra cross-client information, the authors propose FedASTRA, which learns correspondence-invariant diffusion operators.

entry.title: LatentWeave: Test-Time Latent Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Fanci Meng, Kun Wang, Guibin Zhang, Xinlei Yu, Jiaming Zhang, Ming Li, Yang Wang

entry.summary: LatentWeave is a test-time framework for large multimodal language models that treats reasoning as a controllable latent trajectory, progressively refining intermediate hidden states segment-wise to correct emerging deviations and reduce autoregressive error accumulation. It operates without modifying backbone parameters, going beyond prompt- or output-level test-time methods.

entry.title: Implicit Bias of (Stochastic) Gradient Descent on Deep Linear Diagonal Networks

author.name: Wiebke Bartolomaeus, Holger Rauhut

entry.summary: The paper extends implicit bias analysis of deep linear diagonal networks from gradient flow to discrete (stochastic) gradient descent iterations for an arbitrary number of layers, showing convergence toward sparse solutions under small initialization. The approach treats SGD as a perturbed gradient flow with perturbation analysis.

entry.title: Surface Conditioning for Zero-Shot Multivariate Correction in a Marine Biogeochemistry Emulator

author.name: Gabriela Mart\'inez Balbont\'in (MOi, PEQUAN), Anastase Charantonis (ARCHES), Dominique B\'er\'eziat (PEQUAN), Stefano Ciavatta (MOi)

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight bias-correction alternative to iterative data assimilation for a neural emulator of marine biogeochemistry, using FiLM conditioning on surface variables as an observation injection point. Substituting satellite chlorophyll-a observations at inference propagates corrections through the water column, improving agreement with depth-resolved data.

entry.title: Does System Size Matter in Uncertainty Quantification for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials?

author.name: Chayaphol Lortaraprasert, Nontawat Charoenphakdee, Wenwen Li, Yong-Bin Zhuang, Yuta Tsuboi

entry.summary: Tests the implicit assumption in ML interatomic potential workflows that per-atom uncertainty aggregated by mean or maximum is comparable across system sizes for OOD detection and active learning. The two aggregations exhibit distinct size dependencies, with mean aggregation losing sensitivity in some regimes, suggesting common thresholding practice is flawed.

entry.title: Uncertainty-aware Feedback Loop Diagnosis: integrating reinforcement learning and conformal prediction for reliable wafer defect classification

author.name: Aleksandr Dekhovich, Carlas Smith, Oleg Soloviev

entry.summary: UFLD combines reinforcement learning for adaptive measurement acquisition with conformal prediction to output calibrated uncertainty at each inspection step, stopping once sufficient information is gathered for wafer defect classification. This avoids full-surface scans required by most deep learning defect detectors, enabling higher-throughput semiconductor inspection.

entry.title: Accelerated Dataflow: scaling inference in streaming data analytics with efficiency

author.name: RuiLong Jiang, Dustin Rhodes, Danny McCormick, Yuta Labur, Reza Rokni

entry.summary: This systems paper introduces a Google Cloud Dataflow design for hybrid streaming ML workloads that mix data movement with GPU-intensive LLM inference, using co-designed autoscaling over heterogeneous worker pools and prefix-aware batching. It reports 1.5x to 2x throughput increases for streaming pipelines using LLMs.

entry.title: Investigating the Early Signatures of Feature Learning in Deep Linear Networks

author.name: Shaunak Bhandarkar, Boris Hanin

entry.summary: This theory paper provides a closed-form account of feature learning in deep linear networks under mean-field parameterization after one gradient step on high-dimensional spiked data. It shows the first update aligns each layer's feature kernel with a rank-one spike amplified by learning rate and depth, then connects these features to generalization.

entry.title: GearUp: DAG-aware Acceleration for Serverless Inference Serving via Slack-guided Pre-loading

author.name: Qi Qi, Yifan Sui, Hanfei Yu, Hong Zhang, Hao Wang

entry.summary: GearUp is a serverless ML inference serving system that removes model, library, and CUDA kernel loading from the end-to-end critical path of DAG-structured inference workflows. It combines DAG-aware scheduling with slack-guided pre-loading, avoiding the waste of DAG-agnostic pre-loading while addressing initialization costs that existing DAG-aware serving systems ignore.

entry.title: Learning Erasing Equal-Length Relational Pattern Languages in the Limit from Positive Data over Binary Alphabets

author.name: S. Mahmoud Mousawi, Sandra Zilles

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies erasing relational pattern languages under the equal-length relation and proves that, unlike alphabets with three or more letters, the class is not learnable in the limit from positive data over a binary alphabet, resolving an open question. The non-learnability already holds for a restricted subclass, and the authors extend the analysis further.

entry.title: Diffusion models for the $O(3)$ nonlinear sigma model

author.name: Daniel Schubring

entry.summary: The paper trains score-based diffusion models on the 2D classical Heisenberg model using multiple coarse-grainings for multiscale sampling, and introduces Stein/Schwinger-Dyson diagnostics to assess learned scores without reverse diffusion sampling, also incorporating them into training. It contributes practical techniques for lattice field theory applications of generative models.

entry.title: Formalizing the Intrinsic Dimension of Objective Landscapes by a Generalized Notion of Co-dimension

author.name: Ernesto Araya, Gitta Kutyniok, Weilin Li, Johannes Maly, Manjot Singh

entry.summary: The authors formalize the empirical notion of intrinsic dimension of loss landscapes (from Li et al. 2018) as the minimal random-subspace dimension guaranteed to intersect a parameter set with probability one. They show this is a generalized co-dimension depending on global geometry and develop estimation techniques for sets arising in learning problems. This provides theoretical grounding for a widely used empirical measure of learning-problem complexity.

entry.title: Hidden Disparities in Ranking: Category-Aware Fairness via Distributional Stability

author.name: Gayane Taturyan, Charlotte Laclau, Stephan Cl\'emen\c{c}on

entry.summary: This work develops a formal probabilistic framework for fair ranking where policies are distributions over permutations and user utility is item exposure relative to an ideal ranking, introducing conditional utility parity as a category-aware fairness refinement. It shows these criteria are equivalent to distributional stability of utility under user-group composition changes, and optimization over policy mixtures yields a second-order cone program with algorithms provided. This advances both the theory and practice of fairness in recommender systems.

entry.title: Continuous-Action World Models: Learning Cross-Embodiment Spatiotemporal Dynamics Priors

author.name: Liangyu Li, Qingwen Liu

entry.summary: CoAWM learns cross-embodiment dynamics priors for robot action generation through a shared latent function space over continuous actions. A function pretraining stage aligns trajectories from different embodiments and sampling frequencies via reconstruction and temporal-consistency objectives, followed by a downstream stage supporting action generation across embodiments and execution frequencies. This targets data reuse and generalization in robot learning, echoing trends toward cross-embodiment foundation models.

entry.title: Large Language Models for Accurate Medical Chart Abstraction: Enabling Scalable and Secure Artificial Intelligence Deployment in Stroke

author.name: Zhusi Zhong, Carl M. Porto, David Hong, Miranda Gonzales, Revyn Kim, Gnaneswari Karayi, Lulu Bi, Joshua R. Feler, Elias Shaaya, Scott Collins, Liqi Shu, Grayson Baird, Mahesh Jayaraman, Shadi Yaghi, Zhicheng Jiao, Dylan N. Wolman

entry.summary: Evaluates 22 instruction-tuned open-source LLMs with Quick Response and Chain-of-Thought prompting for extracting eight clinical variables from 2,416 neurointerventional acute stroke reports across three hospitals. Uses non-expert staff annotations as a cross-model reference standard and reports detailed performance by report-variable pair. Provides practical guidance for deploying LLM chart abstraction in clinical quality monitoring.

entry.title: Human Evaluation with Automatic Scores: Separating Sampling and Estimation Gains

author.name: Yang Liu, Ran Zou, Zhengtao Gui, Chao Xue

entry.summary: Formally compares how automatic judge scores should be used to reduce human annotation costs in model evaluation: guiding sampling, correcting estimates, or adaptive acquisition, with matched comparisons on preference datasets and 19 systems. Finds score stratification is a strong baseline, with the best correction adding only 1.00-5.27% further MSE reduction. Provides rigorous statistical guidance for evaluation-budget allocation.

entry.title: ScienceJudge: Pattern Perturbation Augmentation for Sentence-Level Scientific Claim Verification

author.name: Chuhai Cai, Xin Chen, Min Yang, Feng Jiang

entry.summary: ScienceJudge addresses sentence-level verification of AI-generated scientific claims against multimodal evidence, introducing Pattern Perturbation Augmentation (PPA) that models reporting errors as faithfulness-breaking transformations and constructs hard negatives from reusable error patterns. This targets subtle, fluent-sounding reporting errors that evade detection under sparse supervision. It is relevant to trustworthy AI-assisted scientific writing.

entry.title: Similar Scores, Opposite Failures: Human Correction as an Instrument for Video Caption Evaluation

author.name: Ankit Khedia, Astitva Jaiswal, Chaitanya Prasad, Anisha Raju, Aangeeras

entry.summary: This study tests whether caption metrics designed for single-sentence image captions transfer to dense video description, using trained annotators to post-edit captions from six frontier models against a fixed failure taxonomy (1,144 overview and 4,672 window verdicts). Reference-overlap metrics fail to distinguish accepted from rejected captions (BLEU-4 AUC 0.510). It demonstrates that video captioning evaluation needs human-correction-grounded metrics.

entry.title: FYC: FPR-Disparity Weight Perturbation and Youden Calibration for Fair Deepfake Detection

author.name: Uzoamaka Ezeakunne, Taiwo Olabamipe, Deevesh Jain, Xiuwen Liu

entry.summary: Introduces FYC, a two-stage post-hoc method that perturbs a pretrained deepfake detector's weights under a false-positive-rate disparity criterion and then calibrates per-demographic-group thresholds, requiring no architectural changes, retraining, or demographic-annotated training data. It targets double-digit FPR gaps across gender and skin tone using only the available checkpoint.

entry.title: Neighbourhood shortcuts in building damage assessment from very-high-resolution satellite imagery: diagnosis and a building-evidence plug-in

author.name: JianChong Guo, YuTing Wan, Kefan Li, AiLong Ma, YanFei Zhong

entry.summary: This work diagnoses shortcut learning in deep models for building damage assessment from satellite imagery, showing that spatial clustering of damage lets models score well by relying on neighbors rather than the target building. The authors stratify buildings by neighborhood agreement, relocate buildings to new contexts, and propose a building-evidence plug-in to force per-building evidence use.

entry.title: RoSAMDepth: Robust Self-supervised Depth Estimation Leveraging Segment Anything Model

author.name: Xuanang Gao, Zhiwei Ning, Gengming Zhang, Jiaxi Cao, Runze Yang, Zhonglong Zheng, Jie Yang, Rong Xiao, Wei Liu

entry.summary: RoSAMDepth injects object-level priors from the Segment Anything Model into self-supervised monocular depth estimation via segment-guided representation contrasting and adaptive regional outlier handling. The goal is robust depth prediction under adverse conditions like occlusion and sparse points.

entry.title: LightGenBench: A Benchmark for 3D Emission Generation

author.name: Dongchen Yang, Xingguang Yan, Manolis Savva

entry.summary: LightGenBench introduces the new task of emission generation, predicting spatially varying RGB emission over a 3D asset surface, supported by a curated dataset of 37K artist-authored emissive assets, baselines across four method families, and an evaluation protocol measuring where and how assets emit.

entry.title: PriorMaskMap: Robust Online Vectorized Map Construction with Biased Priors

author.name: Haoming Xu, Wei Li, Yu Hu

entry.summary: PriorMaskMap enables prior-guided online vectorized HD map construction for autonomous vehicles while remaining robust to biased or outdated priors, using a Prior-Aware Confidence Estimator that scores prior regions against current visual observations.

entry.title: PicturePerfect: Diffusion-based Same-identity Facial Replacement

author.name: Manik Dhingra, Yashesh Savani, Mahesh Reddy, Antoine Mercier, Jiahe Liu, Guillaume Berger

entry.summary: This paper presents PicturePerfect, a diffusion-based method built on a pre-trained text-to-image model that replaces a person's face in a portrait with a reference image of the same individual captured under different conditions, while preserving the background. The authors note that despite clear practical utility, recent literature has not directly addressed this specific same-identity face replacement setting, and they contribute a large dataset of paired images depicting the same person to support the task.

entry.title: CASE: Concept-Aware Segmentation from Positive and Negative Visual Exemplars

author.name: Yi-Jen Tsai, Yen-Yu Lin, Chien-Yao Wang

entry.summary: Formulates Specified Visual Prompt Segmentation (SVPS), where the segmentation target is defined by both positive and negative visual exemplars, since positive cues alone are often underspecified (e.g., red cars vs all cars). CASE uses negative exemplars as intent-defining constraints for exclusion and disambiguation in few-shot segmentation.

entry.title: FFAI: Flow Matching with Feedback Training and Adaptive Initialization for CT Reconstruction

author.name: Jigang Duan, Heran Wang, Genwei Ma, Xing Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes a unified conditional flow matching method for low-dose, sparse-view, and limited-angle CT reconstruction that combines feedback-aware training (a teacher simulating inference shifts) with degradation-adaptive initialization conditioned on the initial reconstruction, addressing path deviation and fixed-initialization problems.

entry.title: Confidence Filtering in Video-Based Gait Assessment: Measurement Error versus Selection Shift

author.name: David Regev, Eran Beeri Bamani

entry.summary: This study examines whether keeping only high-confidence pose observations in video-based gait assessment truly improves measurement, comparing confidence selection to budget-matched random selection in Parkinson-related (n=96) and NF2 (n=18) cohorts. It finds a small but consistent selection shift in the movement summary with flat held-out clinical error, arguing that apparent gains mix measurement error with selection shift.

entry.title: BiHashFormer: Hash-Driven Dual-Branch Transformer for Efficient Object Detection in HRW Shots

author.name: Jingchen Huang, Wenxi Li, Chenyang Lyu, Moran Liu, Haozhe Lin, Yuchen Guo

entry.summary: BiHashFormer tackles gigapixel high-resolution-wide object detection with a dual sparsified transformer: a RoI selector predicts foreground proportion for top-k window selection, and a compression branch applies HashAttention that discards half the key-value pairs to cut attention cost amid extreme background sparsity.

entry.title: SynthFaces: Balanced Large Scale Human Dataset

author.name: Sergey Karpukhin, Denis Bobkov, Kirill Morozov, Aibek Alanov

entry.summary: Proposes a pipeline for generating large-scale, demographically balanced synthetic face datasets by extending the Arc2Face diffusion model with flow matching over identity embedding manifolds, addressing bias and privacy risks of real face data. The approach aims to improve fairness of downstream identity-preserving generative models trained on the synthetic corpus.

entry.title: Textual Response-Aware Guidance for Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yubo Cui, Xianchao Guan, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes complementary limitations of visual-feature and prediction-distribution guidance in adversarial fine-tuning of vision-language models and proposes textual response-aware guidance to better preserve pre-trained image-text alignment while improving robustness. The analysis of visual representation drift motivates emphasizing semantically relevant directions during robustness training.

entry.title: Towards Diverse and Comprehensive Benchmarks for Mutual Information Estimation

author.name: Alberto Foresti, Ivan Butakov, Alexander Tolmachev, Giulio Franzese, Alexey Frolov, Pietro Michiardi

entry.summary: This work builds a comprehensive benchmarking framework for mutual information estimators grounded in copula theory, with a copula-first family varying MI, dimensionality, and marginal complexity, plus a marginals-first family coupling real image data with controlled dependence. It replaces simplified low-dimensional test distributions with realistic, complex data. MI estimation underpins many ML methods, so rigorous evaluation matters broadly.

entry.title: MATCH: Execution-Aware Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environment

author.name: Shuhao Ye, Yufei Wei, Demao Wang, Shichao Zhai, Rong Xiong, Yue Wang

entry.summary: MATCH jointly learns a language-conditioned planner and a goal-conditioned executor for vision-and-language navigation in continuous environments, using an execution-aware topological graph that incorporates executor value estimates and realized outcome memory. A transition-aware dense macro reward balances progress along the reference route against execution reliability.

entry.title: Value Function-Guided MPPI for Hierarchical Planning and Control in Off-Road Autonomous Navigation

author.name: Anoushka Alavilli, Raymond Song, Guanya Shi, Jeff Schneider

entry.summary: This paper proposes a hierarchical off-road navigation framework with bidirectional information flow, where an MPPI-style planner at the top level passes waypoints to a pretrained low-level RL controller whose value function feeds back to guide trajectory selection at the planning level. This contrasts with conventional one-way cost-map pipelines that decouple planning from true execution cost.

entry.title: Controlling Continuum Robot Shape in Enclosed Space with Embedded Sensing using IMU and Actuator Feedback

author.name: Jiahe Wang, Sultan Haidar Ali, Eric Weissman, Jiefeng Sun

entry.summary: An embedded shape-sensing framework for continuum robots that reconstructs shape from IMU and actuator feedback using a neural network, achieving 400 Hz feedback for closed-loop control in confined spaces where external observation is impossible. The paper systematically evaluates key reconstruction design choices. This enables real-time shape control of robots in enclosed environments like pipes and tight machinery.

entry.title: SimTO-Robust: Automated Design of Soft Grippers Robust to Grasp Pose and Object Geometry

author.name: Kurt Enkera, Joshua Pinskier, Marcus Gallagher, David Howard

entry.summary: SimTO-Robust generalizes simulation-driven topology optimization to design soft gripper morphologies robust across multiple object geometries and grasp poses, by simulating grasps and aggregating contact forces to guide optimization. The team generated 6,646 designs and physically validated 24, showing that mechanical design can substitute for sophisticated control in unstructured grasping. It fills a gap in robustness-aware gripper co-design.

entry.title: Data-Driven or Model-Constrained? Comparing Airflow Estimation Methods under Sparse Sensing

author.name: Dominik Aigner, Thomas Wiedemann, Javier Monroy, Achim J. Lilienthal

entry.summary: A systematic benchmark comparing airflow field estimation methods under sparse measurements, spanning purely data-driven approaches to physics-constrained priors. The work targets applications like gas source localization and contaminant spread analysis where full spatial sensing is infeasible. It clarifies when physics-based priors actually help under limited data.

entry.title: A Tutorial on Shape Servoing of Deformable Objects-Part I: Fundamentals

author.name: Ignacio Cuiral-Zueco, Alessio Caporali, Miguel Aranda, Gianluca Palli, Gonzalo L\'opez-Nicol\'as, Youcef Mezouar

entry.summary: The first part of a two-part tutorial on data-driven shape servoing of deformable objects, covering the deformation Jacobian, its estimation from observed shape changes under commanded robot motion, and fundamental feedback-control formulations. It consolidates a fragmented literature for researchers entering deformable-object manipulation.

entry.title: Limit Theorems and Optimal Policies for Flock Flight through Poisson Forests

author.name: Lav R. Varshney

entry.summary: Extending single-agent speed-limit results for flight through random forests, this paper formulates a bulk-transport problem for many birds/agents, constructing an explicit corridor network in a Poisson disk forest where maximum flow equals a minimum vertex-cut capacity. It proves that a simple vertex-disjoint path schedule is optimal at every finite horizon with constant speed and no waiting.

entry.title: Finite-Sample LTI System Identification from a Misspecified Finite Model Set

author.name: Nicolas Chatzikiriakos, Andrea Iannelli

entry.summary: This paper analyzes finite-sample identification of unknown LTI systems when the true system is outside the finite hypothesis class, characterizing the resulting estimation target and deriving finite-sample lower bounds on failure probability. It also proves robustness of an exponential-weighting-based algorithm via a matching upper bound analysis.

entry.title: Agent Transfer Protocol: Server-Mediated Agent-to-Agent Communication Architecture for the Agentic Web

author.name: Yuqi Qiu, Zuyao Xu, Lu Sun, Xiang Li, Fasheng Miao, Fubin Wu, Haixin Duan, Zheli Liu

entry.summary: ATP proposes a domain-mediated protocol for cross-organization agent communication that decouples collaboration from continuously-online execution instances, providing stable communication entries, offline message reception, and post-hoc source verification. It targets infrastructure needs of the emerging agentic web.

entry.title: "Close enough?" An investigation into multiplication errors in LLMs

author.name: William Bolton, Bezawit Tilaye, Huw Day

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates multiplication across 16,991 problems in small base LLMs, testing whether the noisy-quantization error model established for addition extends to multiplication. It shows it does not: small Qwen models exhibit a novel error regime where lower-order column errors predominantly preserve parity, while higher-order errors behave differently. The findings deepen understanding of arithmetic failure mechanisms in LLMs.

entry.title: DeFT-RAG: Incrementally Decomposing Multi-Hop Questions into Self-Contained Sub-Questions with Reusable Answers

author.name: Dingyi Kang, Bingzhe Li

entry.summary: DeFT-RAG is a RAG framework for multi-hop questions that incrementally decomposes them into self-contained sub-questions with reusable answers, reducing the planning, rewriting, and tracking burden placed on the LLM in iterative RAG. It addresses the failure of graph-based RAG to recover full evidence chains when questions mention only partial entities.

entry.title: EmbodiExp: Compositional Experience Transfer for Embodied Agents

author.name: Zhifeng Gu, Ying Chen, Rui Jiang, Lei Yi, Bing Wang

entry.summary: Introduces EmbodiExp, a framework for constructing transferable, outcome-grounded subgoal experiences with applicability conditions, adaptable policies, and verifiable outcomes, which embodied agents compose online during task execution. It targets the problem that strategies effective in past tasks often fail when transferred to new states or tasks.

entry.title: FairSplit: Decomposing the Embedding Space for Fair Classification

author.name: Andrii Shkabrii, Anna Beer, Ylli Sadikaj, Claudia Plant

entry.summary: FairSplit decomposes the embedding space into a Fair Space for prediction and a Sensitive Space that isolates sensitive attributes, guided by a learnable mask and the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion, with theoretical guarantees. By giving sensitive information an explicit destination, the fair representation can avoid relying on it while maintaining accuracy. A clean approach to the accuracy-fairness trade-off.

entry.title: Low-Bit GDN Recurrent-State Quantization: Global Gradient-aware Allocation and Pure-Write Sliding Windows

author.name: Qinghang Huang, Xuchu Huang, Xunzhao Yin

entry.summary: Proposes two techniques for quantizing the recurrent state of linear-attention models: Global Gradient-aware Allocation, which assigns per-head bit widths under a mixed-precision budget using residual and gradient sensitivity, and a Pure-Write Sliding Window to preserve recent information. These reduce state precision without degrading long-reasoning quality.

entry.title: The Precision Wall: An Optimizer-Dependent Boundary for Optimization under Power-Law Measurement Spectra

author.name: Lngel Kyo (A2O Labs)

entry.summary: In low-rank matrix sensing with power-law measurement covariance, the landscape remains free of spurious local minima, but division-normalized first-order optimizers stall beyond a critical exponent due to a numerical precision wall: the smallest Hessian eigenvalue decays as a power law and falls below the optimizer's effective denominator floor. The paper derives a leading-order boundary for this failure and implications for different optimizers.

entry.title: The Best Second Opinion Is Right Where the Primary Is Wrong: Partner Selection for Selective Span Tagging

author.name: Varun Kotte

entry.summary: This paper studies which second model best sharpens a span tagger's risk-ranked deferrals, finding that partner selection is conditional: the best partner is the model that is correct where the primary errs. Across 576 primary-partner pairings, choosing partners by held-out accuracy on the primary's errors recovers 82% of the best partner's gain versus 69-70% for span F1, and the rule replicated on a held-out fourth dataset.

entry.title: You Don't Need Aligned Representations: Knowledge Distillation via Random Prototype Spaces

author.name: Hamza Etcibasi, Ramazan Gokberk Cinbis

entry.summary: RPKD challenges the assumption that teacher and student must share an aligned feature space for distillation, instead aligning both to a shared bank of randomly initialized frozen prototype vectors. With a fixed random projection on the teacher side and logit and feature branches, the student adapts to the random reference space and achieves competitive distillation results.

entry.title: In-Context Learning for Multi-Fidelity Multiscale Model Closure and Cross-Operator Out-Of-Distribution Generalization

author.name: Xinyuan Li, Matthew Zahr, Panos Stinis, Zecheng Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose an in-context multi-fidelity learning framework in which one shared model learns multiple multi-fidelity operators from paired low- and high-fidelity demonstrations, avoiding retraining for each new PDE. Given a new coarse-scale solution in context, the model produces corrected high-fidelity predictions and aims for cross-operator out-of-distribution generalization.

entry.title: Memorization Capacity of Invariant Convolutional Neural Nets

author.name: Sjoerd Dirksen, Patrick Finke, Paul Geuchen

entry.summary: This theory paper proves upper bounds on the memorization capacity of convolutional neural networks that are invariant to arbitrary finite groups of orthogonal transformations, covering translations, reflections, rotations, and higher-order tensor invariances. It extends the extensive memorization literature on fully connected networks to practically preferred structured architectures with threshold activations.

entry.title: Component Translation and Judge-Labelled Refusal: A Multilingual Safety Evaluation

author.name: Yongxi Zhou, Junwei Yao, Wenbo Ye, Jiahui Ge

entry.summary: Introduces a paired-reversal methodology for multilingual safety testing: translating either the request component or the operation component of a harmful prompt into Chinese or Spanish while holding everything else fixed, yielding nine configurations over 190 consensus-annotated behaviors. Refusal is scored by LLM judges on existing models including Gemini 2.5 Flash and DeepSeek. Isolates which prompt component drives safety-behavior differences across languages.

entry.title: Repairs for Whom? Evaluator-Executor Mismatch in Selecting Repairs for Failed LLM Agents

author.name: Yijun Liao, Fanwei Liang

entry.summary: The paper studies agent repair selection: evaluators (greedy replay, stronger models, oracles, judges) that score candidate repairs often pick repairs that do not help the deployed agent, with greedy replay losing 0.06-0.13 in expected success or reward on ALFWorld and WebShop relative to rollout-informed selection. This evaluator-executor mismatch matters for self-correcting agent systems. It uses independent rollouts to ground deployment value.

entry.title: Frequency-Adaptive Gaussian Grids for Efficient Image Representation

author.name: Anatolii Evdokimov, Stavros Diolatzis, Bingxuan Li, Akshay Jindal, Patsorn Sangkloy, Qi Sun

entry.summary: Introduces Gaussian-Grid, a hybrid neural image representation that dynamically partitions computation between structured multi-resolution feature grids and unstructured 2D Gaussians according to local frequency content, automatically allocating capacity where detail is needed. It aims to resolve the trade-off between spatial consistency of grids and adaptive expressivity of Gaussians.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Trajectory State Modeling for Few-Shot Action Recognition

author.name: Zhiqi Miao, Marko Haralovi\'{c}, Stanislav Levendeev, Sarvesh Angadi, Jannatul Ferdous, Dan-Cristian Ploesteanu, Jiapan Guo, Estefan\'{i}a Talavera

entry.summary: GeoTRAM improves few-shot action recognition by modeling actions as ordered evolution of 2.5D trajectory states with local geometric interactions, lifting sparse point tracks beyond 2D displacement descriptors. StateMotion captures intra-trajectory evolution while RelMotion captures state-to-state relations, exposing discriminative motion dynamics from few examples.

entry.title: V-CAPE: Visual Consistency Assessment for Product Image Editing

author.name: Iaroslav Melekhov, Roberto Alcover Couso, Francesco Taioli, Daniel Coelho, Artur Bekasov, Virginia Fernandez Arguedas, Jose Miguel Grande Saiz

entry.summary: V-CAPE is a large-scale benchmark for evaluating whether generative image edits preserve an object's intrinsic visual attributes such as geometry, texture, and color, targeting automated quality assessment for product imagery at scale. It addresses the unsolved problem of verifying consistency without manual inspection.

entry.title: Efficient Covariance-Aware Vicinal Latent Diffusion for Continuous Conditional Image Generation

author.name: Xin Ding, Shuo Huang, Zhenglong Ding, Sen Zhang, Nenglun Chen, Peibei Cao, Yongwei Wang, Fei Wu

entry.summary: CAViLD addresses data sparsity and long-tailed label distributions in continuous conditional generative modeling via density-adaptive vicinal learning in a purified condition-aware latent space, avoiding classifier-free guidance and dense pixel-space integration for efficient sampling.

entry.title: Anatomical Prior-Guided Routing for 3D Lung Tumor Segmentation

author.name: Uihyeon Maeng, Jonghun Kim, Hyunjin Park

entry.summary: Proposes anatomical prior-guided routing for 3D lung tumor segmentation in CT, adapting feature processing to the anatomical region each patch comes from to counter location-dependent heterogeneity amplified by patch-based training and sliding-window inference. Targets improved treatment planning and quantitative imaging.

entry.title: BEACON: Distilled Begin/End-Aware Structured Decoding for Continuous Sign Language Segmentation

author.name: Guohou Zhang, Kalin Stefanov

entry.summary: Presents BEACON, a begin/end-aware sign language segmenter combining BIOE labeling, constrained Viterbi decoding over legal transitions, and boundary knowledge distillation from a binary teacher, with strict no-cut evaluation. It reports large segment-F1 improvements (+14.58/14.59) and boundary-F1 gains over prior work.

entry.title: NIF: Normal-Intersection Fields for Geometrically Consistent Oriented Box Refinement

author.name: Shaokai Zheng

entry.summary: NIF replaces a second box regressor with normal-intersection fields for oriented object detection: boundary anchors predict signed distances along outward normals, which admit an exact affine representation in five geometric variables, and a reliability-weighted least-squares fit projects these onto a refined box. This couples box parameters through boundary geometry rather than pooled-region regression.

entry.title: ElasticFormer: Detecting Objects in HRW Shots via Elastic Computing Vision Transformer

author.name: Wenxi Li, Jingchen Huang, Chenyang Lyu, Moran Liu, Haozhe Lin, Guiguang Ding, Yuchen Guo

entry.summary: ElasticFormer is a sparse vision transformer backbone for gigapixel HRW object detection that dynamically allocates computation based on foreground proportion, scoring windows by variance and using an ElasticSelector to predict foreground counts and adaptively adjust sparsity patterns, unlike prior fixed-sparsity sparse backbones.

entry.title: Beyond CCT: Multi-channel SPD recovery for per-shot camera color correction

author.name: Shuwei Yue, Hongke Wei, Qiao Chen

entry.summary: Replaces standard camera color correction based on Correlated Color Temperature interpolation with recovery of the full illuminant spectral power distribution via non-negative least squares against a basis dictionary, conditioned on the white point and a multi-channel ambient light sensor. A closed-form 3x3 color correction matrix is fit per shot, reducing mean angular error from 1.89 to 1.20 degrees with strong tail improvements on LED illuminants.

entry.title: Wavelet Phase Diffusion for Structurally and Semantically Consistent Sim-to-Real Translation

author.name: Kaiwen Wang, Frank Bieder, Yinzhe Shen, Carlos Fernandez, Jan-Hendrik Pauls, Omer Sahin Tas

entry.summary: This paper replaces Fourier-domain phase-preserving diffusion with a wavelet-based formulation for sim-to-real image translation, avoiding global spectral coupling that causes ringing and boundary leakage while preserving structure and semantics. The approach combines realism with spatial alignment without expensive control modules or paired-data pipelines. Relevant to autonomous driving and robotics simulation fidelity.

entry.title: SymAnt: Grounding Long-Horizon Action Anticipation with Adaptable Symbolic Priors

author.name: Fnu Aryan, Yaqi Xie, Joseph Campbell, Woojun Kim, Kwonjoon Lee, Hossein Nourkhiz Mahjoub, Ehsan Moradi-Pari, Katia Sycara, Simon Stepputtis

entry.summary: SymAnt is a neuro-symbolic method for long-horizon action anticipation that jointly searches over scene and knowledge graphs to build a symbolic context unifying spatial relations, object attributes, affordances, and actions, requiring only brief observations. The symbolic priors make predictions interpretable and adjustable, addressing weaknesses of purely neural anticipators. Relevant for human-robot interaction and driver assistance.

entry.title: Compositional Diffusion Planning with Chunk Selection and Reachability Measure

author.name: Chanyoung Park, Youngjoong Kim, Jaesik Park

entry.summary: The paper proposes the Selective Compositional Diffuser, which addresses mode-averaging artifacts in long-horizon diffusion planning by using a self-supervised reachability classifier to select among overlapping trajectory chunks. The classifier is trained on both offline data and generated chunks to mitigate distributional mismatch.

entry.title: A Conveyor Belt Mechanism for Repositionable Magnetic Coupling Between Continuum Robots

author.name: Ella Walsh, Eric Diller, Jessica Burgner-Kahrs

entry.summary: This hardware paper integrates up to three conveyor belt mechanisms inside a 9 mm diameter tendon-driven continuum robot, enabling continuous active repositioning of functional elements such as permanent magnets along the robot body. The authors demonstrate actively reconfigurable inter-robot magnetic coupling whose effective stiffness follows a predictable inverse-cubic relationship with coupling location.

entry.title: Metropolized backward sampling for conditional sequential Monte Carlo

author.name: Adrien Corenflos

entry.summary: The paper shows that the classic Metropolis-Hastings remedy for particle degeneracy in particle Gibbs with backward sampling only helps near the final time step, since its effect decays geometrically backward in time. It proposes Metropolized backward sampling, applying the move at every backward step to forcibly switch trajectories, plus an auxiliary scheme.

entry.title: Verification-Guided Retrosynthesis: Reaction Feedback and Evidence Timing

author.name: Hongxuan Shi, Hankz Hankui Zhuo

entry.summary: VGR integrates reaction verification as a decision action within AND/OR search for retrosynthesis planning, using binary verdicts to exclude infeasible reactions or reprioritize search before full-route evaluation. Verified solvability is introduced as a metric counting only routes accepted stepwise by the verifier.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Optimization for Simulation-Based Redesign

author.name: Chan-Eui Song, Jeremy J. Michalek, Christopher McComb

entry.summary: The authors develop an integrated LLM-optimization approach for engineering redesign, where simulators are too complex for traditional solvers that lack engineering context. The LLM interprets semantic information such as material price changes and system knowledge to guide numerical search. They test how best to combine LLM guidance with solvers in redesign scenarios.

entry.title: Learning Lotteries with Minimal Stakeholder Violations from Membership Queries

author.name: Nicholas Teh, Paul W. Goldberg

entry.summary: The paper models AI deployment mixture selection as choosing a lottery over m alternatives for n stakeholders, where each stakeholder accepts only lotteries in an unknown halfspace revealed via binary membership queries. Extending work from ICML 2026 that sought universally accepted lotteries, the authors study learning mixtures that minimize stakeholder violations when no universally acceptable mixture exists.

entry.title: The Code Behind the Layout: AI Agents for Analog Layout Generators

author.name: Minxing Chu, Anhang Li, Martins Atilla, Ruichen Qi, Mehdi Saligane

entry.summary: The paper studies whether LLMs writing code for generator frameworks like gLayout outperform drawing analog layouts directly from design intent, using controlled experiments on SKY130. It finds the main obstacle to direct layout generation is time and token cost, and characterizes what generator frameworks still contribute when LLMs can produce geometry themselves. This is a useful empirical answer for EDA automation.

entry.title: Spectral Invariant Fusion and Refinement for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Yansong Bai, Yunzhi Zhuge, Xinzhuo Yu, Lu Zhang, Jin Zhan, Pingping Zhang, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: SIFR is a frequency-aware dual-stream framework for domain-generalized semantic segmentation that uses spectral modeling to both regulate fusion of frozen CLIP and DINOv2 features and refine dense decoder outputs. It simultaneously suppresses domain-sensitive interference while preserving fine-grained spatial cues on unseen domains.

entry.title: Radiology Guideline-derived Decision Graph for Efficient Clinical Decision Support

author.name: Xuewen Zhou, Zhen Chen

entry.summary: GDGraph is a framework that decouples clinical guideline compilation from case evaluation: an LLM partitions radiology guidelines into sections, extracts local decision subgraphs, and aggregates them into an executable decision graph, while at inference a fast System One model answers localized questions and deterministic graph traversal resolves the Boolean logic. This converts opaque end-to-end LLM reasoning into auditable, efficient decision support for risk stratification and management planning. It matters for trustworthy clinical automation.

entry.title: A Gradient based Adversarial Augmentation Framework for Mitigating Unlearnable Datasets

author.name: Long Dang, Satpal Sura, Kaiqi Xiong

entry.summary: The paper proposes a gradient-based search over augmentation operations to counter unlearnable-dataset methods, finding adversarial versions of perturbed images that increase loss and force models to learn generalizable features. This replaces heuristic or random search over curated augmentation sets, which does not scale with large candidate pools.

entry.title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting

author.name: Peter Pavl\'ik, Franz M. Rohrhofer, Bernhard C. Geiger

entry.summary: The authors test whether physics-informed and hybrid modeling deliver claimed benefits for photovoltaic power forecasting, building two architectures that integrate the ADR physical PV model with TSMixer via feature augmentation and residual learning. Evaluation spans over 3 million samples from 3,713 installations in 33 European countries, assessing accuracy, convergence, and geographic transferability. A large-scale empirical check of a popular paradigm.

entry.title: DolphinRouting: Cluster-Level Binary Routing for Disaggregated LLM Inference Serving

author.name: Yishuo Yuan, Shaoyu Yang, Chunrong Fang

entry.summary: Presents DolphinRouting, which learns request-level path selection (local vs remote prefill) in prefill-decode disaggregated LLM serving from end-to-end SLO feedback. Requests are clustered by prompt length, cache-adjusted input lengths, and output-length features, with an offline policy search learning one binary action per cluster, validated on a real cluster with benchmarks and production-like workloads.

entry.title: Same Label, Different Interface: Beyond Action-Space Labels in Robot Learning

author.name: Arshia Sangwan, Zhongyang Zhang

entry.summary: This paper argues that robot-learning comparisons of position versus velocity action labels are confounded by omitted implementation details such as filtering, scaling, feedback laws, and effort limits. Across three contact-rich Factory tasks with ten policies per condition, it empirically shows how these hidden properties affect attribution of performance differences.

entry.title: Fisher Contrastive Learning to Mitigate Feature Suppression: A Case Study in Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia Diagnosis

author.name: Shushan Wu, Yongkai Chen, Xilin Gong, Yufang Liu, Wenxuan Zhong, Ping Ma

entry.summary: The authors propose Fisher Contrastive Learning, which uses a regularized Fisher trace criterion to combat feature suppression in self-supervised contrastive learning, where easy-to-learn factors crowd out other class-relevant signals. They prove the learned representations alleviate feature suppression and demonstrate the method on acute promyelocytic leukemia diagnosis from high-dimensional heterogeneous data. This addresses a known representation-learning pathology with theory plus a clinical application.

entry.title: SSQA: Sibling-Selective Quadtree Attention for Hierarchical Modeling in Perception Tasks

author.name: Yufan Chen, Arnav Bali, Angela Liu, Laura Zheng, Ming C. Lin

entry.summary: SSQA exploits axis-aligned structural priors in robotics perception (drone and driving scenes) by processing features hierarchically with sibling-selective quadtree attention, offering a linear-time alternative to quadratic vanilla attention. The hierarchical structure aims to model organized scene layouts efficiently for navigation tasks.

entry.title: Regional Anchor Routing for Multi-Object Motion Transfer

author.name: Yuze Li, Fuchen Long, Xinlong Sun, Cheng Yan, Xinyu Zhang, Xi Chen

entry.summary: Presents RART, a framework unifying object-wise motion extraction, target-region anchoring, and frame-aligned injection into a frozen video Diffusion Transformer for multi-object motion transfer, avoiding cross-object motion leakage and enabling repeated transfers without per-reference re-optimization.

entry.title: DOSE: Dominance-Guided Ordinal Severity Estimation from Sparse Relative Annotations

author.name: Tushir Sahu, Hideaki Hayashi, Hajime Nagahara

entry.summary: Proposes DOSE, a framework for ordinal medical severity estimation trained from sparse pairwise comparisons without absolute annotations, aggregating comparisons through a global graph to estimate dominance scores that bridge continuous ranking and discrete grade prediction.

entry.title: UniTele: Learning Device-Conditioned Degradations for Unified Smartphone Telephoto Super-Resolution

author.name: Yuchen Zhang, Aojie Li, Wei Cheng, Xianfang Zeng, Runxing Liu, haixin hao, Gang YU, Xiaoyun Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes UniTele, which learns device-specific telephoto degradations from a small number of physical captures by factoring degradation into device imaging characteristics plus super-telephoto-specific information loss, enabling a unified smartphone super-resolution model without large-scale aligned training pairs.

entry.title: Parametric Gaussian Noise Mixer (PGNM): Unified Synthesis of Camera Noise and Film Grain

author.name: Mingyang Song (ETH Z\"urich)

entry.summary: PGNM is an explicit statistical model fitted from paired clean/noisy images that synthesizes both camera noise and film grain: a normalized convolution correlates a Gaussian field across pixels and channels, and a lookup maps Gaussian values to intensity-dependent residuals. Without learning a neural generator or modeling full image-formation physics, it achieves the lowest distribution and correlation errors on SIDD among evaluated baselines.

entry.title: Hardware-Aware Model Inversion in Memristive Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Pablo Sorrentino, Fernando M. Quintana, Erika Covi, Fatih Turkmen

entry.summary: The paper introduces Spiking Domain Model Inversion (SDMI) to study whether model-inversion privacy leakage characterized on software SNNs persists when the model is mapped to non-ideal memristive crossbar hardware, and how device variability and faults reshape leakage. Counterintuitively, analog noise does not necessarily protect privacy. This is an early exploration of security for analog neuromorphic deployment.

entry.title: Force-Driven Hook Disassembly via Constraint-Aware Object-Centric Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Nadeen Elhadad, Takuya Kiyokawa, Kensuke Harada

entry.summary: The paper proposes a constraint-aware RL framework for non-destructive disassembly of hook-type connections, inferring feasible extraction directions online from noisy contact forces. Trained in robot-agnostic, object-centric simulation on simplified peg-in-hole pairs, the policy transfers zero-shot to real connections with unseen multi-stage constraint structures.

entry.title: ProLoop: Progress-Aware Closed-Loop Framework via Structured State Relations for Long-Horizon Robotic Task Planning

author.name: Runxin Zou, Qingmiao Liang, Jiatao Zhang, Xinyan Lv, Liangyu Qie, Meiyi Bu, Wei Song, Shiqiang Zhu

entry.summary: ProLoop introduces explicit subgoal progress estimation for LLM-based long-horizon planning, using a learned State-Relation Monitor comparing desired and executed states to classify progress as ongoing, deviated, or completed. This closes the loop so execution can adapt and local errors do not silently propagate. Experiments on AgentBoard ALFWorld-style tasks show improved reliability.

entry.title: Gaze-Assisted Supervisory Control for Lunar Robotic Arm Teleoperation Under Concurrent Monitoring

author.name: Jiayu He, Yifan Li, Oliver R. Runswick, Ernest N. Kamavuako, Yunjie Jia, Peter D. Hodkinson, Yang Gao

entry.summary: The paper presents a gaze-assisted supervisory control framework for lunar robotic arm teleoperation, where eye gaze nominates targets, explicit confirmation authorizes actions, and the robot autonomously executes bounded grasp-and-place. A 16-participant VR study with a 2x2x3 within-subject design shows reduced task completion time versus manual joystick control, even under concurrent monitoring load.

entry.title: DAWN: Diffusion-based Alignment and unfastening Workflow Network

author.name: Hemant Kumar, Piyush Goenka, Nikhil Chopra

entry.summary: DAWN is a hierarchical robotic framework for autonomous unfastening tasks (e.g., screw removal for recycling and disassembly) that splits the procedure into alignment-and-insertion and unfastening stages with multi-modal sensory integration. It uses diffusion-based components to handle long-horizon, contact-rich manipulation with robustness to environmental variability.

entry.title: Non-Asymptotic Confidence Regions for Separable Nonlinear Models

author.name: Szabolcs Szentp\'eteri, P\'eter Kov\'acs, Bal\'azs Csan\'ad Cs\'aji

entry.summary: Two resampling-based methods, Residual-Perturbed Gradient and Global-Fit-Gap, construct joint distribution-free confidence regions for both linear and nonlinear parameters in separable nonlinear least squares. By exploiting group invariance of the noise (sign changes, permutations), the methods achieve provably exact non-asymptotic coverage.

entry.title: Evaluating and improving AI agents for sequencing protocol understanding

author.name: Chi-Lam Poon, Michael Goneos, Zezheng Song, Xi Chen

entry.summary: Introduces LibStructBench, a document-grounded benchmark testing whether AI agents can exactly reconstruct sequencing-library molecular structures and workflows from protocols. Results show frontier agents achieve approximate but not exact reconstructions, with the choice of underlying language model mattering more than the agent harness.

entry.title: The Anatomy of Socio-Demographics in Pluralistic Offensiveness Modeling: When and Where It Helps, and the Role of Reasoning

author.name: Yifan Wang, Leixin Zhang, Jinyi Mu, Yu Wang, Mayank Jobanputra, Isabel Valera, Vera Demberg

entry.summary: Systematically analyzes when and where annotator socio-demographic information helps pluralistic LLM modeling of offensiveness judgments, and what role explicit reasoning plays, across three multi-annotator datasets with prompted and trained models. It clarifies previously mixed findings on demographic conditioning for subjective judgments.

entry.title: GARDEN: Generalist Autonomous Reward Design Through Evidence Navigation for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Dogan Urgun
