entry.summary: Proposes GARDEN, a framework in which one LLM-written reward program is designed for reuse across cooperative MARL settings rather than being tailored to a single environment. It aims to reduce the repeated manual effort of intermediate reward design when environments or agent teams change.

entry.title: FACTS-MAS: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Adaptive Forecasting from Heterogeneous Evidence

author.name: Madumita Karthikeyan, Umang Rajnikant Bid, Rong Pan

entry.summary: FACTS-MAS decomposes forecasting evidence into specialized agent channels (temporal dynamics, exogenous context, seasonality, structure, discrete events), each producing independently testable forecasts. Leakage-safe validation measures per-agent predictive skill, which then weights forecast combination so uninformative evidence is downweighted or removed.

entry.title: PT$^3$: Prototype-Guided Self-Supervised Pretraining for Generalizable mmWave Human Point Cloud Representation

author.name: Ziyang Liu, Kieren Yu, Xiao Yang, Xin Yang, Kaishun Wu

entry.summary: PT3 is a self-supervised pretraining framework for mmWave human point clouds that represents local spatial states as sparse compositions of shared prototypes and models their temporal evolution autoregressively, with observation consistency to stabilize against radar perturbations. A single frozen encoder then supports multiple downstream tasks such as action classification and deployment. This tackles the instability of multi-source mmWave observations.

entry.title: Formal Specifications with Data-Driven Signal Analysis

author.name: Roderick Bloem, Benedikt Maderbacher, Cristinel Mateis, Dejan Ni\v{c}kovi\'{c}, Sergii Tkachov, Bj\"orn Ziegler

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hybrid monitoring approach for analog and hybrid systems that combines specification-based regular expressions with interval operations, classical signal-processing feature extraction, and semi-supervised learning to separate correct from faulty behavior. Learned relationships from normal-behavior data can then flag anomalies automatically. It makes hard-to-formalize domain knowledge usable by both formal methods and machine learning.

entry.title: Does Federated Training Degrade Explainability? A Comparative Analysis of Grad-CAM Faithfulness in Centralized vs. Federated Deepfake Detection

author.name: Muhammad Uzair Shahid, Muhammad Zabil Mehboob

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies whether federated learning degrades the faithfulness of Grad-CAM explanations in deepfake detection, evaluating an EfficientNet-B4 detector on FaceForensics++ across five federated clients. It examines the tension between privacy-preserving training and the explainability that forensic analysts need to trust flagged clips.

entry.title: Agentic University: Collaborative Agents for Personalized Learning

author.name: Jingru Fan, Tianle Zhou, Yunjie Zhou, Zihao He, Yixuan Zhou, Kezhao Wu, Xinyu Zheng, Xiyuan Wang, Yuheng Wang, Zhi Li, Songhua Liu, Weinan E, Chen Qian

entry.summary: The paper introduces Human-Participatory Multi-Agent Organization, instantiated as Agentic University, where learners participate as organization members working with specialized agents to maintain a revisable Capability Program connecting goals, activities, and layered assessment. Learner feedback and performance guide subsequent learning decisions.

entry.title: GenAI as an 'Invisible Hand' in Opinion Dynamics: Evidence from a Group-Level Simulation Study

author.name: Thomas Grisold, Johannes Schneider

entry.summary: Simulating 50,000 group discussions across 50 controversial statements with three LLMs, the authors test whether repeated genAI consultation quietly shapes collective opinions and norms. They vary LLM agreeableness and personalization and compare influence in homogeneous versus heterogeneous groups.

entry.title: DuQUAD: A Dual-View Framework with Quality-Aware Evidence Pruning for Multi-Document Question Answering

author.name: Yeonjun Choi, Seyeon Jeong, Jong Wook Kim, Beakcheol Jang

entry.summary: DuQUAD mitigates the Lost in the Middle problem in retrieval-augmented multi-document QA via dual-view reasoning, combining a Local Agent with a Structural Fusion Score and a Global Agent reasoning over the full document set, plus quality-aware evidence pruning. It targets brittleness of reordering and attention-steering approaches in noisy settings.

entry.title: When More Planning Hurts: Learned Planners for World Models

author.name: Josef Chen

entry.summary: This paper studies learned planners for world models on PushT, comparing a small fixed action updater against Adam-based planning, adapted iCEM, and the released LePlanner under matched compute budgets. The results show that more planning iterations can hurt performance, with the simple released LePlanner solving all 16 evaluation scenes fastest.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Latent Action-Conditioned World Modeling for Time Series

author.name: Chia-Han Kuo, Chengshuai Zhao, Huan Liu, Lo Pang-Yun Ting

entry.summary: ACTS-WM is a self-supervised world model for time series that explicitly models latent actions governing transitions between observations, extending JEPA-style latent-space prediction. The hypothesis is that modeling the information behind changes in a series, rather than only predicting in latent space, improves time-series representations.

entry.title: "It Would Make a Geordie Feel at Home": Regional Accent Perceptions and Speech Accommodation in Voice AI

author.name: Dana Serditova, Kevin Tang, Jochen Steffens

entry.summary: A sociolinguistic study of how speakers of Newcastle English (Geordie) perceive and accommodate regional versus Standard Southern British English voices in voice assistants, including how ASR accuracy disparities shape user responses. It combines simulated VA interactions with semi-structured interviews.

entry.title: A Tutorial on Generative Models for Music Audio

author.name: Mateusz Modrzejewski, Joanna Kurkowska, Dorien Herremans

entry.summary: A tutorial monograph unifying music-audio generation methods — neural codecs, autoregressive and masked token models, diffusion and flow matching, sampling acceleration, and preference optimization — in shared notation with worked examples linking training objectives to published systems. It also maps musical requirements (instrumentals, songs, editing, live performance) to model design choices. Useful as an entry point for researchers new to music generation.

entry.title: LLMs as Judges and Examinees for Medical Item Difficulty Prediction

author.name: Xiaomeng Xiong, Marcus Walker, Yanlin Jiang

entry.summary: The study uses open-weight LLMs in two roles — judges providing difficulty ratings and comparisons, and simulated examinees generating correctness, probability, and entropy signals — to predict difficulty of USMLE and PANCE items from text alone. This interaction-based signal approach improves over prior linguistic-feature methods. It is a creative application of LLM behavior to psychometrics.

entry.title: Episodic looking - using reinforcement learning to bias perception enhances few-shot and continual learning with protection from forgetting

author.name: David Rawlinson, Gideon Kowadlo

entry.summary: The authors propose an episodic-looking mechanism built on the Complementary Learning System architecture, where a short-term memory delegates generalization to a slow statistical long-term memory operating in a space of robust perceptions, using reinforcement learning to bias perception. This aims to reconcile few-shot adaptation with protection against catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: SatOps-Decision: Low-Latency Discriminative Decisions for Onboard Satellite Communication Operations

author.name: Lifan Mei, Yuxuan Li, Jiaxian Tu, Shenghe Xu

entry.summary: SatOps-Decision applies discriminative decision models to onboard satellite communication operations, using a locally adapted encoder with a decision head to select among operational answers in a single forward pass. The authors also contribute the first benchmark dedicated to this setting, with auditable construction and independently checked labels.

entry.title: What Makes Medical Examination Items Difficult? Using Large Language Models to Explore Patterns Associated With Empirical Item Difficulty

author.name: Xiaomeng Xiong, Marcus Walker, Yanlin Jiang

entry.summary: The authors use empirical difficulty labels from USMLE and PANCE items to guide Claude Opus 5 (an existing model released in July 2026) in inducing rubrics for absolute and pairwise difficulty judgment. Induced rubrics ignored surface features like stem length and option count, instead highlighting deeper construct-related factors as difficulty drivers.

entry.title: Data Provenance and Ethics in the Curricula of U.S. Health AI Education Programs

author.name: Raffaele Giancotti, Francesca Santucci, Amama Anjum, Monique de Villa, Rupsa Mitra, Soham Biren Katlariwala, Vishala Mishra, Leo Anthony Celi

entry.summary: A cross-sectional analysis of publicly advertised curricula of U.S. university health AI education programs (searched April-July 2026) coding coverage of data provenance, ethics, sustainability, collaborative structure, and instructor backgrounds. The study asks whether programs training the health AI workforce teach practitioners to examine how training data were generated, given that many clinical AI failures originate in data generation.

entry.title: Rebuilding a Field's Open-Problem Catalog from the Literature: A Two-Layer Knowledge Graph, and Why Status Must Stay Proposed

author.name: Madhulatha Mandarapu, Sandeep Kunkunuru

entry.summary: This work proposes representing a research field's open problems as structured data via a two-layer knowledge graph combining a hand-curated problem layer with a literature-derived evidence layer. LLMs perform extraction, catalog grounding, status verdicts, and idea generation, each constrained to candidate sets so out-of-set answers are refused, with an argument that problem status should remain proposed rather than resolved automatically.

entry.title: The Importance of Speech Genre for End-of-Turn Detector Training

author.name: Rini Sharon, Kadri Hacioglu, Jeena Prakash, Andreas Stolcke

entry.summary: The authors isolate the effect of speech genre on end-of-turn detection by training identical streaming ConvLSTM detectors on matched conversational human-human versus single-turn human-machine corpora. Conversational training yields up to +0.45 F1 improvement, driven by fewer false alarms on mid-turn pauses, and the effect holds at utterance level across models.

entry.title: Accumulating Pruning Constraints: New Exact Polynomial-Space Algorithms for Max 2-SAT

author.name: Konstantin Kutzkov

entry.summary: This paper presents deterministic polynomial-space exact algorithms for Max 2-SAT running in O*(2^((1-gamma)n)) time on several instance classes whose clause density may grow with n. The key technique accumulates pruning constraints from DPLL branching decisions along each branch, eliminating all but an exponentially small fraction of assignments.

entry.title: EPC-RawDC: Equivariant Physics Constrained 3D Diffusion with Raw Data Consistency for CBCT to CT Image Synthesis

author.name: Alzahra Altalib, Chunhui Li, Alessandro Perelli

entry.summary: The authors propose EPC-RawDC, a conditional 3D latent diffusion model for synthesizing CT images from cone-beam CT, incorporating scanner-specific acquisition physics via a geometry equivariant projection constraint and raw-data consistency with the CBCT forward model. This addresses limitations of purely image-driven synthesis methods in radiotherapy. It matters because quantitative CBCT-to-CT synthesis directly affects image-guided and adaptive radiation therapy quality.

entry.title: Learned Terminal Costs for Short-Horizon Model Predictive Control of Autonomous Trucks in Interactive Highway Traffic

author.name: Hooman Hamze, Benjamin Houshmand, Deepthi Pathare, Erik B\"orve, Morteza Haghir Chehreghani, Nikolce Murgovski

entry.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid MPC-RL framework for autonomous heavy-duty truck highway driving in which reinforcement learning supplies learned terminal costs that extend the effective horizon of short, computationally affordable MPC horizons, while MPC retains rigorous constraint satisfaction that RL alone lacks. The combination targets the mass, dimensions, and interaction requirements unique to trucks in critical maneuvers. It matters for deployable autonomous driving controllers with safety guarantees.

entry.title: Bridging Neural Representations and Symbolic Semantics in Audio Classification

author.name: Avishek Das, Pascal Hitzler

entry.summary: This paper presents a model-agnostic neurosymbolic framework for interpreting the final hidden layer of audio classifiers, testing whether individual hidden neurons can be mapped to human-understandable symbolic acoustic concepts. It moves beyond input-level attribution methods toward concept-level explanation of what audio models learn internally.

entry.title: NECA: Neighbor Event Curve Augmentation for Multi-Horizon ICU Deterioration Prediction

author.name: Chenyang Wang, Jiawei Theresa Tang, Xinran Liu, Xinyu Lu, Xulei Yang

entry.summary: NECA is a model-agnostic method for ICU deterioration prediction that retrieves similar historical patients based on early-window profiles and converts their organ dysfunction event timing into cumulative event-curve features over 6h, 12h, and 24h horizons. This leverages population-level event timing patterns that standard supervised models ignore.

entry.title: Anisotropic Trust Region Warping for Prior-Data Fitted Networks in Bayesian Optimisation

author.name: Samuel Younger, Tinkle Chugh, George De Ath

entry.summary: The paper shows empirically that PFN surrogates in Bayesian optimization degrade relative to refitted Gaussian processes when objective lengthscales exceed the meta-training prior's mode, and introduces Anisotropic Trust Region (ATR) warping. Per-dimension lengthscales are estimated via kernel target alignment and an affine input rescaling corrects the prior mismatch without retraining.

entry.title: Replaying the Same Gradients at a Different $\varepsilon$: A Registered Test of the Fixed-Trajectory Account of Adam's $\varepsilon$ for One Rare Row

author.name: Lngel Kyo (A2O Labs)

entry.summary: This registered-report-style paper directly tests the arithmetic reading of Adam's epsilon by replaying a single rare embedding row's updates at different epsilon values using the run's own moment estimates, holding the trajectory fixed. Pre-registered failure criteria were written before the runs, and a small causal transformer is trained in a standard configuration to test whether raising epsilon merely shrinks that row's steps.

entry.title: Progressive Coupling Method for Diffusion Posterior Sampling in Ptychography

author.name: Yihan Qiu, Mingtao Huang, Tianyuan Li, Shudong Li, Yuan Shen

entry.summary: This paper proposes a progressive coupling posterior sampling (PCPS) method that uses diffusion model priors to compensate for reduced measurement redundancy in ptychography when scan overlaps are reduced. It matters because it can shorten acquisition times in computational imaging while maintaining reconstruction quality under weaker physical constraints.

entry.title: REVBRAIN: Real-time Probabilistic EEG Forecasting Using Residual Vector Quantization

author.name: Hanna Pankka, Jaakko Lehtinen, Timo Roine

entry.summary: REVBRAIN is a probabilistic model for real-time resting-state EEG forecasting that replaces autoregressive WaveNet inference, which is too slow for real-time use, with an approach based on residual vector quantization. It retains WaveNet-like accuracy and built-in uncertainty while enabling real-time applications such as brain-state-dependent stimulation.

entry.title: On the Generalization Gap of Streaming Federated Learning with Markovian Data

author.name: Masoud Kavian, Milad Sefidgaran, Youssef Attia El Hili, Malik Tiomoko, Abdellatif Zaidi

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the expected generalization gap of aggregated models in streaming federated learning when client data follow heterogeneous Markov processes, using information-theoretic and rate-distortion techniques. It provides bounds under cross-entropy loss, specialized to linear and self-attention next-token prediction settings.

entry.title: Discovery of Diverse and Realistic Financial Tail-Risk Using Generative Flow Networks

author.name: Adir Serruya, Gilad Katz

entry.summary: GRID applies continuous GFlowNets with a mixture-policy architecture and variable-specific distribution families to generate diverse, realistic financial tail-risk scenarios, addressing the diversity-efficiency gap between SMCMC and deep RL approaches. It demonstrates a niche but natural fit for GFlowNets in stress-testing and risk management. The method targets high-dimensional sequential macro-financial data.

entry.title: Planned Restlessness: Delayed Meta Bandits with Budgets

author.name: Sudipto Guha

entry.summary: The paper studies episodic Bayesian meta-bandits with delayed observations, per-episode play caps, and total budgets, formulating a planning optimization whose LP relaxation values actions through reward, resource cost, and continuation value. Dual prices decompose the problem into local programs and certify policies including hierarchical Thompson sampling. A rigorous treatment of bandits under realistic delay and budget constraints.

entry.title: Grounding Predictive Reliability through Masked Observability

author.name: Shang Gao, Bernhard Sick, Franz G\"otz-Hahn

entry.summary: MORSE addresses semantic ambiguity in evidential regression under masked representation learning by predicting hidden targets under controlled changes in visible context, using normalized cross-context variation to ground predictive-mean uncertainty. This ties uncertainty estimates to observable predictive behavior, giving Normal-Inverse-Gamma components identifiable semantics.

entry.title: Data-driven Random-feature Approximation of Koopman Generators of Nonlinear Continuous-time Systems

author.name: Ana \v{C}ukarska, Maximilian Gollwitzer, Viola Muning Li, Vladyslav Fediukov, Zahra Monfared, Felix Dietrich

entry.summary: Tackles the dictionary-selection problem in Koopman operator theory by proposing a data-driven random-feature approximation of the Koopman generator for continuous-time systems. This provides a principled finite-dimensional function-space representation that captures fundamental dynamical properties from data.

entry.title: Observability-Aligned Evidential Masked Pretraining for Reliable VRU Motion Prediction

author.name: Shang Gao, Franz G\"otz-Hahn, Konrad Doll, Bernhard Sick

entry.summary: Introduces eCoMAE, an evidential masked pretraining method for multivariate time series that aligns predictive evidence with observed inputs, using a Normal-Inverse-Gamma decoder and observability-aware consistency mechanisms. Applied to vulnerable road user motion prediction, it targets reliable uncertainty under partial observability and distribution shift.

entry.title: Reinforcement learning for control of partial differential equations

author.name: Nicol\`o Botteghi, Matteo Tomasetto, Andrea Manzoni

entry.summary: This review surveys reinforcement learning approaches for controlling PDE-governed dynamical systems, unifying perspectives from RL and PDE-constrained optimization across model-free, model-based, and multi-agent methods. It emphasizes sample efficiency, generalization over parametric variations, and scalability to high-dimensional problems.

entry.title: Generation, Not Selection: LLM Proposals for Certified Access-Control Policy Mining

author.name: Gautam Kumar (Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur, India), Ravi Sundaram (Northeastern University, USA), Shamik Sural (Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur, India)

entry.summary: The paper observes that greedy minimum-set-cover guarantees for ABAC policy mining are conditional on candidate pools containing optimal rules, and existing syntactic generators fail on rare exception rules. It replaces the generator with an LLM proposing rules semantically from attribute names while retaining the combinatorial selection step, achieving certified policy recovery.

entry.title: Finite-Sample Optimal Conformal Prediction Sets under Covariate Shift

author.name: Zhongyang Li

entry.summary: This paper proves that, for conformal prediction under covariate shift with known density ratio, a rule combining inverse conditional-density scores with randomized weighted conformal calibration minimizes expected prediction-set length at every calibration sample size. It also provides practical approximations via quantile and kernel histogram estimators with finite-sample excess-length bounds.

entry.title: MiniMMD: Minimization of MMD for Sampling, Inference and Integration

author.name: Zonghao Chen

entry.summary: This thesis develops a unified treatment of numerical integration, sampling, generative modeling, and statistical inference through the lens of minimizing maximum mean discrepancy (MMD). The central claim is that MMD is both a statistically meaningful discrepancy and a tractable optimization objective, unifying problems usually studied separately.

entry.title: CSO: Refining Robotic Policies via Skill Distribution Alignment and Skill-Grained Optimization

author.name: Zhiyuan Xiang, Xiang Deng, Wanjie Tao, Xu Chen, Zhao Jielun, Weili Guan

entry.summary: CSO is a two-stage post-training framework that refines discretized robotic manipulation policies by first aligning observation-to-skill mappings with successful online trajectories via rejection-sampling SFT, then applying skill-grained optimization with a frozen observation encoder. It targets quantization-induced suboptimality in VQ-VAE-style skill priors while avoiding unstable encoder updates and importance-sampling granularity issues.

entry.title: Trajeform: Embedding Crowd Data

author.name: Marilena Lemonari, Panayiotis Charalambous, Yiorgos Chrysanthou

entry.summary: Trajeform trains a reconstruction VAE on real crowd trajectory data to produce behaviour-level embeddings, addressing the limitation that existing crowd-simulation evaluation metrics focus on trajectory-level rather than behaviour-level similarity. It enables richer assessment of how well learned crowd simulators generalize across datasets.

entry.title: Probabilistic Meshless Methods on Manifolds

author.name: Federico Pavesi, No\'emie Jaquier, Antonio Candelieri

entry.summary: This paper extends probabilistic meshless PDE solvers, which place Gaussian process priors on solutions and condition on the PDE at collocation nodes, to compact manifolds and provides the first convergence analyses in this setting. It handles both known manifolds with available Laplace-Beltrami eigenpairs and unknown manifolds, replacing the PDE operator with geometric approximations. This adds Bayesian error quantification guarantees to manifold-domain scientific computing.

entry.title: Adaptive Scenario Generation for KL-DRO Around a Learned Density Model

author.name: Aron Brenner, Saurabh Amin

entry.summary: Proposes a distributionally robust optimization formulation using a Kullback-Leibler ball centered at a learned density model rather than the empirical distribution, allowing the adversary to up-weight costly unobserved realizations without hedging against impossible ones. This bridges divergence-ball and transport-ball ambiguity sets for two-stage stochastic programs. Targets robust decision-making under finite data.

entry.title: CARF: Context-Aware Reasoning Supervision for Scientific Evidence Screening

author.name: Nishtha Agarwal, Adam Visokay, Astha Wahi, Kwabena Owusu Aninkora, Amy Gu, Tyler McCormick, Li Liu

entry.summary: Introduces CARF, a human-in-the-loop framework where domain experts give feedback on model-generated reasoning to adapt LLMs for title/abstract screening in systematic reviews, evaluated on verbal autopsy and cause-of-death reviews for global public health. Targets the bottleneck of manually screening thousands of studies against eligibility criteria. Combines expert oversight with reasoning supervision for high-stakes evidence synthesis.

entry.title: Robustness of Chatbot LLM Judgments of Presidential Actions and Hypothetical Reforms

author.name: Oleg Vasilyev

entry.summary: This 30-day study queried five chatbot configurations (including Mistral, Gemini Flash, Claude Sonnet, and Claude Opus) twice daily through consumer interfaces to score the long-term US effects of 40 presidential actions and 15 hypothetical reforms. Judgments were broadly robust, with consistent signs and rankings across configurations, though isolated disagreements occurred. It provides a longitudinal look at the stability of LLM political judgments in ordinary usage.

entry.title: AI Cosmos: An Agentic Infra for Situated Learning

author.name: AI Cosmos Team, Jinfeng Zhou, Yuxuan Chen, Fangming Chang, Mingyu Su, Yifan Zhu, Yuan Wang, Bo Zhang, Bosi Wen, Chenhao Yuan, Chenwen Liao, Dazhi Jiang, Deyao Hong, Erle Zhu, Genrui Zhang, Guchan Li, Hongwen Gan, Huichao Bi, Jiahao Yan, Jincheng Fan, Kehan Zheng, Qinren Luo, Qiran Liu, Ruoqi Cao, Shizhi Zhang, Sihan Chen, Siyan Deng, Xuehan Zhou, Xujun Li, Yang Dang, Yanzhuo Zhu, Yu Zhang, Zheyu Chen, Hongning Wang, Manli Li

entry.summary: AI Cosmos is an agentic infrastructure for situated learning that organizes learners and role-specialized agents in scenarios with executable workbenches, plus an asset-memory loop that preserves practice outcomes as reusable assets with provenance. It is evaluated with preregistered studies of scenario-based interaction. The work targets whether LLM-assisted learning gains translate into independent skill application.

entry.title: Vision Tomography: Towards Portable 3D Bidirectional Face-Skull Inference from Visual Data

author.name: Zidu Wang, Meng Xu, Miao Xu, Hengyuan Ma, Jiankuo Zhao, Xutao Li, Zhen Lei, Xiangyu Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces Vision Tomography, a framework for reconstructing paired 3D face-skull geometry from visual modalities such as photos or scans, as a portable, radiation-free alternative to CT, with applications in forensics, missing-person identification, and remote healthcare. It contributes a dataset of over 200 CT-based skull cases enabling bidirectional face-skull inference.

entry.title: Volley3D: Unified 3D Full-Sequence Reconstruction from Monocular Broadcasts

author.name: No\^am Boussouf, Adrien Maglo, Mohamed Chaouch, Hideo Saito

entry.summary: Volley3D presents a physics-grounded pipeline for 3D reconstruction of volleyball players and ball from single-view broadcast footage, handling uncalibrated moving cameras, depth ambiguity, and multi-contact dynamics that invalidate planar projection assumptions. The method requires no 3D training supervision and supports automated analytics and AR/VR replay.

entry.title: Structure-retained low-rank adapters for weather synthesis

author.name: Shunxin Wang, Alexandros Stergiou, Luuk Spreeuwers, Estefania Talavera, Nicola Strisciuglio

entry.summary: This paper proposes a weather synthesis framework that uses structure-retaining low-rank adapters to generate controlled adverse-weather variations of scenes, decoupling weather-induced distribution shifts from unrelated scene dynamics. The goal is to produce reliable training data for improving robustness of outdoor computer vision models, where existing datasets conflate weather changes with moving subjects and camera viewpoint changes.

entry.title: Automatic Iconographic Annotation of Medieval Illuminations: Comparing Generative Vision-Language Models and Supervised Discriminative Classifiers

author.name: Vincent Jolivet (ENC, CJM), Lucas Terriel (ENC), Chahan Vidal-Gor{\`e}ne (CJM, ENC)

entry.summary: The study evaluates generative VLMs versus supervised discriminative classifiers for iconographic indexing of 9,735 medieval manuscript illuminations across 2,333 TIMEL concepts. The discriminative ML-Decoder over a frozen DINOv3 encoder achieves the strongest retrieval performance (precision@1 0.696, MRR 0.806), with findings on fine-tuning, structured decoding, hierarchy-aware heads, and loss calibration.

entry.title: Joint Rigid Alignment and Morphable Reconstruction from Partial 3D Face Scans

author.name: Eli A. Underwood, Nicolas Rondan, Angel V. Peterchev, J. Matias Di Martino

entry.summary: Building on GeoTransformer, this work presents a single network that jointly predicts rigid pose and shape-complete facial point clouds from partial 3D face scans, replacing decoupled registration-then-fitting pipelines with a cross-attention regressor producing per-patch morphable model coefficients.

entry.title: MOSAIC-Flow: Orthogonal-Axis and Status-Conditioned Fusion for Missing-Sequence Completion in Brain Tumor MRI

author.name: Pengli Zhu, Zhihao Peng, Yixuan Yuan

entry.summary: Introduces MOSAIC-Flow, a flow-based framework for missing MRI sequence completion in brain tumors that keeps the seven acquired volumes fixed during transport, using modality-aware stems, orthogonal-axis refinement, and status-conditioned prototypes to preserve sequence-specific contrast and 3D detail.

entry.title: Open-set multi-view seahorse re-identification from underwater photograph sequences

author.name: Tristan Fauvel, Sylvie Louisy, Patrick Louisy, Thomas Fauvel

entry.summary: This paper presents methods for taxonomic classification, sex determination, and open-set re-identification of seahorses from underwater photograph sequences, trained and evaluated on 35,914 wild photographs of 474 individuals. Aggregating information across multiple photographs of varying quality yields state-of-the-art performance and enables minimally invasive capture-mark-recapture ecology at scale.

entry.title: Learning a Motion Manifold to Constrain Ambiguity in Unsupervised 4D Medical Image Interpolation

author.name: Haojin Li, Huazhu Fu, Heng Li, Jiang Liu

entry.summary: Develops an unsupervised framework for 4D medical image interpolation that learns a motion manifold to restrict candidate motion fields and mitigate motion ambiguity, where different motion fields fit endpoints equally well but imply different intermediate anatomy. The method uses cross-sample spectral basis learning and sample-conditioned components to retain subject-specific variation.

entry.title: AdMuse: Skill-Guided Creative Advertising Image Generation

author.name: Minyan Luo, Yuxin Zhang, Meng Zhao, Xincan Wang, Fuzhang Wu, Tong-Yee Lee, Oliver Deussen, Fan Tang, Weiming Dong

entry.summary: Presents AdMuse, a skill-guided multi-agent framework for advertising image generation that distills high-quality advertisements into a reusable library of creative bridge patterns, routing skills to new product briefs and coordinating multi-candidate ideation with VLM-guided visual refinement. Rather than retrieving isolated exemplars, it abstracts recurring persuasive concepts into transferable skills.

entry.title: HairDeck: Animation-Ready Stylized Hair Cards from a Single Image

author.name: Yuze He, Yixiang Wei, Wang Zhao, Chuhao Chen, Yanning Zhou, Yong-Jin Liu

entry.summary: HairDeck generates animation-ready stylized hair cards from a single image using a set diffusion transformer in which each hair card is a single token, producing both card geometry and spring-bone chains for downstream animation. This replaces the autoregressive control-point decoding of prior work (CHARM) with parallel set-based generation. It lowers the barrier to creating animatable character assets for games and avatars.

entry.title: Fast rigid rotational alignment of voxelized 3-D density maps in sliced Wasserstein distance

author.name: Oscar Mickelin, Yunpeng Shi, Amit Singer, Eric J. Verbeke

entry.summary: The authors develop a fast method for rigid alignment of voxelized 3D density maps over SO(3) using sliced optimal transport, transforming each map into tensors of one-dimensional quantile functions so Euclidean alignment algorithms apply. They provide theoretical analysis and experiments showing sliced 2-Wasserstein distance is a robust shape metric. Applicable to cryo-EM and scientific 3D shape analysis.

entry.title: Active Constraints for Simultaneous Guidance and Safety in Handheld Micromanipulation

author.name: Roger Ho, Robert A. MacLachlan, Cameron N. Riviere

entry.summary: This work presents an active-constraint formulation for handheld micromanipulation robots that provides task guidance and enforces safety simultaneously, addressing a key limitation of prior formulations that could not do both at once. The application domain includes microsurgery where hand tremor limits accuracy.

entry.title: When "No Worries" Went Wrong: HRI Lessons for Foundation-Model Robots

author.name: Eliahu Khalastchi (The College of Management Academic Studies)

entry.summary: Drawing on a three-year ROS 2 human-robot interaction consortium that integrated large language and vision models as they emerged, this paper recounts real interaction failures, such as socially inappropriate gesture-word ordering and erroneous visitor announcements, to argue that capability alone does not ensure situation-appropriate robot behavior. It distills lessons for deploying foundation-model-driven robots in human-facing settings.

entry.title: SONIC-K1: Porting a Universal Humanoid Motion Tracker to a Small Humanoid on a Single GPU

author.name: Kyrylo Kolesnichenko, Jong-Hoon Kim

entry.summary: SONIC-K1 adapts the SONIC whole-body humanoid motion tracking framework to the Booster K1 humanoid, training open-weights policies on a single GPU with a small fraction of the original compute. It tracks nearly all held-out motion clips in simulation and upper-body/slow motions on real hardware, though stepping, turning, and latency sensitivity remain limitations. The work democratizes humanoid motion tracking for smaller labs.

entry.title: Compressed Orientation Reachability Maps for Sub-Second Robotic Needle Entry Point Planning

author.name: Prabhu Nithin Gollapudi, Andreas Maier, Franziska Mathis-Ullrich, Water Zhao, Jia Wang, Siming Bayer

entry.summary: For robotic liver interventions, the paper precomputes 6-DoF kinematic feasibility across 188,873 workspace positions into a compact 83 MB indexed orientation reachability map. A JIT-compiled lookup pipeline replaces exhaustive inverse kinematics or randomized search, cutting per-target planning from 13-27 seconds to sub-second times. This enables real-time intraoperative adaptation of entry points.

entry.title: MUSBRIC: LEGO-Compatible Pneumatic Muscle Bricks for Reconfigurable Musculoskeletal Robots

author.name: Qiyao Wang, Yinglei Zhu, Liang Zhou, Wenzhe Gong, Xin-Jun Liu, Huichan Zhao

entry.summary: MUSBRIC is a modular hardware platform with LEGO-compatible pneumatic artificial muscle bricks plus a matching MuJoCo simulator for reconfigurable musculoskeletal robots. An elbow-joint prototype demonstrates load-dependent flexion/extension, reversible motion via pulley-guided routing, and stable straight posture via a mechanical stop.

entry.title: Universal Short-Time Fourier Transform: Data-Adaptive Window-Length Selection for Time-Frequency Analysis

author.name: Manan Mittal, Kanad Sarkar, Ryan M. Corey, John R. Buck, Andrew C. Singer

entry.summary: The U-STFT treats the analysis window length of the short-time Fourier transform as a data-adaptive state variable, scoring a bank of candidate window durations at each frame to sequentially resolve the time-frequency resolution trade-off. This yields multi-resolution time-frequency analysis without fixed window choices.

entry.title: What is OpenAI's Mission Advisory Council?

author.name: hersheys

entry.summary: An explainer of OpenAI's safety governance structure, distinguishing the Safety and Security Committee (with veto power over safety decisions), the internal Safety Advisory Group, and the Mission Advisory Council, including Paul Christiano joining the SSC in September 2026. The post lays out open questions about how safety decisions at frontier labs are made and enforced.

entry.title: Speeding up language models for travel applications

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon Science describes applying knowledge distillation and the Medusa parallel-decoding framework to reduce latency and serving cost of large LLMs for travel applications in partnership with Booking.com. The work targets the constraint that multi-second LLM responses are untenable for web and mobile users where 100ms delays cost revenue.

entry.title: From Grind to Grasp

author.name: Peter Sunehag

entry.summary: This theoretical paper formalizes the relationship between algorithmic complexity, computational depth, and the work needed to produce outputs, comparing achievements under work and information limits. It shows deep outputs can require long descriptions at low work budgets, and that learning plus persistence can make previously deep achievements shallow by reusing past products. It defines grasp as performance achievable under a work budget across later tasks.

entry.title: Leaving, Staying, or Living There? Duration Commonsense Reasoning with Human-LLM Co-annotations

author.name: Chenyang Yu, Zhaomin Xiao, Yan Huang, Eduardo Blanco

entry.summary: The paper tests whether vision-language models possess duration commonsense — inferring whether a post implies living, staying, or briefly visiting a place — using a new corpus of geotagged tweets co-annotated by humans and LLMs. State-of-the-art models struggle with duration inference even with multi-turn chain-of-thought prompting. Error analyses show models rely heavily on superficial visual cues.

entry.title: SAG-Sep: Sparse Augmented Graphs and Onion-Guided Search for Rounded Capacity Cut Separation

author.name: Haoran Liu, Guanyi Wang, Yu Yang

entry.summary: SAG-Sep is a neural separator for rounded capacity cuts in capacitated vehicle routing that scores node membership across vehicle-count levels from a fractional LP solution in a single encoder forward pass, avoiding iterative predict-and-coarsen inference. It encodes the LP solution as a sparse augmented graph with flow-informed multi-hop edges to capture long-range routing structure.

entry.title: LiDAR-SHIELD: A Fully Dockerized Adversarial Robustness Assessment Framework for LiDAR-Based 3D Perception Models

author.name: Alexandros Gkillas, Ioulia Kapsali, Christos Anagnostopoulos, Aris S. Lalos

entry.summary: LiDAR-SHIELD is a unified, fully Dockerized framework for assessing adversarial robustness of LiDAR-based 3D perception, inverting the usual workflow by exposing any target model through three lightweight HTTP endpoints (/info, /forward, /gradient) instead of installing models inside the toolkit. This removes manual environment reconstruction and model-specific integration code.

entry.title: Decision and System One models in rheumatology: accuracy and calibration on specialty-training examination questions and diagnostic case vignettes

author.name: Alfredo Madrid-Garc\'ia, Diego Benavent, Fabian Lechner, Phillip Kremer, Johannes Knitza, Beatriz Merino-Barbancho

entry.summary: This evaluation benchmarks four System One models and GPT-6 Luna against GPT-6 Sol and local generative models on rheumatology questions from Spanish specialty-training exams (RheumaMIR) and RheumBench diagnostic vignettes, measuring accuracy, calibration, and discrimination. The models assessed are established systems rather than new releases. It provides specialty-specific evidence on how fast clinical decision models compare with flagship LLMs in a medical domain.

entry.title: FIDE: Fiber-Informed Differentiable Experimental Design for Reference-Relative Law Dynamics

author.name: Pietro Zanotta, J\'an Drgo\v{n}a

entry.summary: Studies how to resolve design freedom in experimental design when aggregate measurements leave an evolving population law underdetermined. FIDE completes candidate constraints via information projection against a frozen reference model and ranks scientifically adequate designs by the dynamical revision they require, connecting optimal experimental design with differentiable simulation.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Global Climate Policy Cooperation

author.name: Anne Moll-Elsborg, Oskar Bohn Lassen, Francisco Camara Pereira

entry.summary: The work extends a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for climate policy with a multi-stage negotiation mechanism where agents propose, accept, or reject agreements and face penalties for non-compliance. This enables studying how agreement design shapes learned mitigation behavior, moving beyond prescribed equilibrium concepts in classical game-theoretic climate models.

entry.title: Two Birds with One Stone: Skill-Augmented Generation via Unified Retrieval and Utilization

author.name: Zihan Luo, Jiahui Kang, Wei Zhou, Qilin Fan, Mingyan Li, Chao Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Skill-Uni, a reinforcement learning framework that jointly optimizes skill retrieval and utilization for skill-augmented LLM generation, replacing separate retriever and user models with a single generative-retrieval model trained via a two-stage strategy. This removes the disconnected optimization of prior skill-augmentation pipelines. Targets improved complex task solving with reusable external knowledge.

entry.title: Self-Consistency Geometry Injection for Multi-view Consistent Image Generation

author.name: Yupeng Xiao, Yankai Wu, Jianjie Luo, Jiajie Lin, Yi Yu, Zhenguo Yang

entry.summary: RGMV improves multi-view image generation by decoupling geometry inference from texture synthesis with an explicit reliability assessment: a parameter-free Self-Consistency Geometry Gate evaluates whether predicted geometry is trustworthy, and Reliability-aware Geometry Injection modulates how geometry conditions generation. This reduces vulnerability to inaccurate geometry predictions.

entry.title: MorphSIG: Subject-Driven Image Generation via Decoupled Anchoring and Feature Transport

author.name: Hailong Yan, Yongrui Zhang, Xiangtao Zhang, Le Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes MorphSIG, a training-free framework recasting subject-driven image generation as pseudo-video feature transport, using frequency-domain decoupled anchoring to avoid structural locking and a latent pseudo-flow field for identity transport. Also introduces a benchmark with diverse stylized subjects to address stylistic homogeneity in prior evaluations.

entry.title: Uncertainty-aware Coarse-to-Fine Main Pancreatic Duct Segmentation for Width Measurement in 3D MRCP

author.name: Zipei Zhang, Jaakko Sahlsten, Mikko Saukkoriipi, Johanna Ronkainen, Mona Lehto, Akseli Aittoniemi, Irina Rinta-Kiikka, Kimmo Kaski

entry.summary: The paper presents an automatic, uncertainty-aware pipeline for main pancreatic duct segmentation and maximum-width measurement from volumetric MRCP scans, using coarse localization followed by fine segmentation. This supports ductal dilatation diagnosis and pancreatic cancer analysis where manual assessment suffers from reader variability.

entry.title: FPGAFly: A 166.7k-Neuron Fruit-Fly Connectome on One FPGA via Deferred Spike Expansion and Shared-Codeword States

author.name: YE Ziyang

entry.summary: FPGAFly runs the full 166.7k-neuron, 25.6M-connection Drosophila CNS connectome on a single FPGA using order-preserving deferred spike expansion and shared-codeword neuron states to fit within limited on-chip memory. This achieves neuron-by-neuron whole-brain simulation without multi-chip neuromorphic hardware or heavy software. A significant systems-engineering result for connectome-based simulation.

entry.title: AI for Science in Space: Orbital Laboratories, Planetary Fieldwork, and Embodied Autonomy

author.name: Zizhe Wang, Jia Deng, Xin Lu, Zehao Jia, Yi Huang, Yao Zhu, Jianing Li

entry.summary: A critical review of AI for science extending into space contexts, covering orbital laboratories and planetary in-situ investigation across biology, materials, and fluid/thermal physics, with attention to embodied autonomy under microgravity and resource constraints. It distinguishes learning from space-derived data versus selecting and executing scientific actions while preserving experimental validity. The paper maps an emerging frontier where embodied AI meets space science.

entry.title: CovFedAvg: Local Low-Loss Curves and Federated Model Selection

author.name: Federico Lucchetti, Marcus V\"olp

entry.summary: CovFedAvg addresses the problem that federated clients observing different data regions learn locally equivalent but behaviorally incompatible models. It retains local models with curve controls, fits a common endpoint via aggregated gradients, and performs distributed model selection with a guarantee that selected models do not exceed the training loss of prior candidates, without centralized calibration data.

entry.title: Neural Compression of Long ADMM Trajectory for Multiparametric Quadratic Program

author.name: Liang Wu, Honghui Zheng, Bo Yang, Xu Yang, Yilin Mo, J\'an Drgo\v{n}a

entry.summary: TQPNet is a self-supervised framework that compresses long ADMM optimization trajectories for multiparametric QPs into a compact neural warm start plus a few refinement steps. The key insight is that a low-dimensional ADMM scheme admits an equivalent ReLU-layer representation, which the authors combine with an MLP to accelerate real-time model predictive control.

entry.title: Recurrent Bipartite Graph Neural Networks for QC-MDPC Error Decoding in McEliece Cryptosystems

author.name: Parth Rajeshkumar Tandel, Elisabeth Fink

entry.summary: The paper proposes a Recurrent Bipartite Graph Neural Network integrating GRUs into message passing, trained with a multi-topology curriculum, to decode QC-MDPC codes used in post-quantum cryptography. This addresses failure modes of classical belief propagation caused by short graph cycles, which in cryptographic settings can leak secret key information.

entry.title: AskStream: When and What to Ask Proactively under Uncertainty in Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Lu Wang, Zhuoran Jin, Longxiang Wang, Junhong Chen, Yupu Hao, Yao Xu, Daojian Zeng, Yubo Chen, Kang Liu, Guang Liu, Jun Zhao

entry.summary: AskStream argues that proactive video-understanding agents should ask clarifying questions when information is incomplete due to video or user uncertainty, rather than only waiting or answering. The work formalizes when and what to ask in streaming video settings, addressing failure modes of indefinite waiting and hallucinatory answering. It extends proactive multimodal interaction research in a sensible direction.

entry.title: Calibrating Track-Query Updates at Test Time for Multi-Object Tracking

author.name: Riku Inoue, Shogo Sato, Yu Mitsuzumi, Kazuhiko Murasaki, Tomoyasu Shimada, Takashi Sano

entry.summary: The paper analyzes identity switches in query-propagation multi-object trackers, showing that propagated track-query representations change abruptly before identity switches because updates contain components directed at nearby active tracks. It proposes a test-time calibration of track-query updates to suppress these interference components during target interactions.

entry.title: Understanding Large Language Models as Numerical Optimizers

author.name: Lingyun Guo, Ali Bereyhi

entry.summary: Develops an evaluation framework distinguishing LLM solution quality from execution failures (numerical inaccuracy, constraint violations, format errors) when using LLMs for numerical optimization in high dimensions. Tests against deterministic reference solvers on convex optimization, fractional programming, and constrained projection problems.

entry.title: BridgeRouter: Gain-Aware Instance Routing over Cross-Modal Bridge Portfolios

author.name: Ruoxi Piao, Alicia Lu, Yunzhen Zhang, Mustafa M{\i}s{\i}r, Hasan Onur Kele\c{s}

entry.summary: BridgeRouter formulates multi-bridge cross-modal transfer (e.g., EEG foundation models applied to other biosignals) as instance-level algorithm selection, routing each sample through the pathway with the greatest predicted gain over a protected default route. A lightweight router trained on validation-derived NLL reductions selects among frozen bridge pathways.

entry.title: Curriculum-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robust Autonomous Rocket Landing under Atmospheric Uncertainty

author.name: Atin Chowdhury, Piyush Joshi

entry.summary: The paper presents a curriculum-driven PPO framework for 3D far-range rocket landing in a stochastic environment including wind shear, turbulence, gusts, uncertain propulsion parameters, thrust misalignment, engine lag, noisy observations, and command latency. Training is staged into approach, soft descent, and integrated landing. The work demonstrates robust policy transfer under dense atmospheric uncertainty.

entry.title: Syntactic Segmentation and Collage Generation for Videogame Levels with Perceptual Distance

author.name: Ross Mawhorter, Matthew Guzdial

entry.summary: The authors introduce perceptual distance, derived from Space Syntax analysis in architecture, to automatically segment hand-authored game levels into chunks and generate new levels from them. They validate on Super Metroid rooms and compare against prior StarCraft analysis work, with a proof-of-concept generator. It automates what previously required manual graph abstraction in procedural level design.

entry.title: Category-Anchored Large Language Models for Next POI Recommendation

author.name: Lexi Bai, Xiaopeng Zeng, Xun Zhou, Yuanshao Zhu, James Jianqiao Yu

entry.summary: ANCHOR is a category-anchored framework that bridges the semantic-to-entity gap in LLM-based next point-of-interest recommendation by predicting POI categories as an intermediate grounding step rather than directly generating sparse, long-tailed POI identifiers. This improves reliability of LLM use on spatio-temporal check-in data.

entry.title: A Negotiation-Aware Hybrid LLM Framework for Intent Interpretation and Service Discovery

author.name: Wided Meflah, Hayet Brabra, Walid Gaaloul

entry.summary: The paper presents a hybrid LLM framework that refines incomplete or conflicting natural-language intents, detects conflicts dynamically, and negotiates with users to discover suitable services from provider catalogs for cloud service composition. It targets the gap between classical structured composition approaches and free-form user intents.

entry.title: Cassette-Editor: A Video Editing Agent That Edits the Way You Do

author.name: Zhixin Zeng, Jiahao Zhong

entry.summary: Cassette-Editor is a video editing agent with a deliberately minimal interface of one read tool and one write tool, where every write passes through the same executor, rules, and commit sequence to keep the timeline structurally valid. It contrasts with approaches using critic agents or restricted output formats.

entry.title: Selective Transfer Learning for Groundwater Level Anomaly Forecasting: Accuracy-Risk Trade-offs

author.name: Yaxuan Wu, Ali Mohammed Mansoor Alsahag, Seyed Sahand Mohammadi Ziabari

entry.summary: This work studies context-aware selective transfer learning for forecasting groundwater anomalies across 457 wells in the Netherlands, showing that naive source-domain pretraining degrades performance on a substantial fraction of heterogeneous wells. The proposed CASL method blends frozen no-transfer and fixed-transfer parents with calibration-fitted weights, evaluated over 13,718 test windows under five seeds.

entry.title: inkGround: Benchmarking Fine-grained Visual Grounding Capabilities of Vision-Language Models for Cursive Handwriting in the Wild

author.name: Sidra Hanif

entry.summary: inkGround is a benchmark for stroke trajectory recovery from camera-captured handwriting images, pairing 537 page images with roughly 18.7k words and 163k strokes to test fine-grained visual grounding in vision-language models. It addresses the gap left by digitizing-tablet datasets that lack writer and stylistic diversity, and provides the first VLM benchmark for this task.

entry.title: Practical Assessment of Agentic Systems in Acoustics

author.name: Arne Hildenbrand, Philipp Diel, Zhuo Cao, Hanno Scharr, Stefan Pischinger, Steffen Marburg

entry.summary: This work empirically measures how LLM choice and harness components affect agent performance on two acoustic engineering tasks, including fault detection in vehicle interior audio with near-perfect accuracy. It finds that a weak model sets a performance ceiling that harness components cannot overcome.

entry.title: EventSeeColor: Learning to Reconstruct Color from Monochrome Events

author.name: Chuanzhi Xu, Langyi Chen, Haoxian Zhou, Zelin Zhang, Haodong Chen, Qiang Qu, Xiaoming Chen, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: This paper presents EventSeeColor, a method that reconstructs scene color from monochrome event camera data by exploiting the dependence of event-triggering patterns on surface reflectance, illumination, and spectral response, jointly using event-reconstructed grayscale and aligned events to guide a diffusion-based colorization. Color recovery reveals surface differences invisible in grayscale intensity reconstruction. This extends event-based vision into a previously unexplored output modality.

entry.title: The Athlete as a Scientist of One: Agentic Bayesian Experimental Design for Individualized Physiology from Consumer Wearables

author.name: Behnam Moradi

entry.summary: EpiCoach is an agentic system applying accountable N-of-1 science to a single athlete using consumer wearable data: hypotheses live in an evidence-gated registry, each issuing pre-registered probabilistic predictions whose beliefs update only through computed evidence from mechanistic digital-twin fits (heart-rate response, fitness-fatigue models) over heart rate, GPS, and altitude data. This contrasts with LLM health agents that recommend without auditable, falsifiable belief updating. It matters as a template for trustworthy personal-health AI.

entry.title: Depth through Recurrence: Towards Ultra-Efficient On-Device ASR

author.name: Chen Feng, Tianyi Xu, Ramchalam Kinattinkara Ramakrishnan, Yicheng Lin, Shaojie Zhuo, Zhaocong Yuan, Chenzheng Su, Xiaopeng Zhang

entry.summary: The paper identifies layer-wise representational dynamics in which most ASR layers learn functionally similar transformations, and proposes a block-recurrent architecture that replaces parameterized depth with recurrence to achieve high representational power without scaling parameters. This targets deployment of ASR on extremely constrained edge devices such as watches and glasses.

entry.title: TGTV: An Interpretable Framework for UAV Fault Detection and Traceability via Spatiotemporal Graph Learning and Large Language Models

author.name: Zixuan Wang, Changbo Shi, Ji Liu

entry.summary: TGTV combines temporal convolutional networks, graph attention with fused adjacency, a hybrid Transformer-variational autoencoder, and a large language model for interpretable fixed-wing UAV fault detection and traceability. The pipeline grounds LLM diagnoses with quantitative evidence from multiscale sensor representations.

entry.title: What to randomize matters: a controlled study of volume, axis and representation in low-data molecular generation

author.name: Neerav Kaushal, Alisa Teige, Ajay MNV Penmatsa

entry.summary: This controlled study compares randomized SMILES and randomized SAFE representations for low-data molecular generation with an autoregressive model trained on 1,000 seed molecules, isolating atom-order versus fragment-order axes of randomization across corpus sizes. It clarifies which sources of representational variation actually prevent memorization and improve generative quality. Useful guidance for chemical language model practice in data-scarce settings.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Guided Cross-Modal Alignment for Diffusion-Based IoT Intrusion Detection

author.name: Mahdi Arab Loodaricheh, Anita Raja, Mohammad Hossein Manshaei

entry.summary: This arXiv paper proposes a reliability-guided alignment rule for diffusion models operating on multimodal data, using normalized VAE posterior variance to control cross-modal influence before diffusion training. The method is applied to generating minority-class attack samples for imbalanced IoT intrusion detection, combining tabular flow attributes, DeepInsight images, and other modalities. It addresses the practical problem that independently trained encoders can map synchronized views into incompatible latent regions, degrading denoising quality.

entry.title: Analyzing Condensation on Patterned Surfaces via Deep Learning

author.name: Tae E. Cooper, Michael Gee, Sheila Whitman, Jemma Dengel, Anthony Katselas, Duygu Dengiz, Frank Keutsch, Joanna Aizenberg

entry.summary: The authors build TileSAM3, a droplet segmentation tool built on Segment Anything Model 3 using hierarchical tiling with per-tile inference and post-processing to extend detection caps and resolve small droplets on inhomogeneous condensation surfaces. They also create new annotated datasets for this task. This enables quantitative characterization of nucleation, growth, coalescence, and shedding rates for engineered condensation surfaces.

entry.title: Multi-Solution Inverse Design of Pixelated Patch Antennas Using an Autoregressive Transformer

author.name: Young-Mok Yun, Seung-Won Shin, Jaeyong Chung, Kyung-Sik Choi

entry.summary: This paper applies an autoregressive transformer to the inverse design of pixelated patch antennas, addressing the one-to-many nature of the problem by generating multiple valid designs rather than a single solution. It aims to overcome limitations of surrogate-assisted metaheuristics, tandem networks, and diffusion models, such as sensitivity to initialization, one-to-one mapping constraints, and excessive data requirements.

entry.title: Quantum-Inspired Convolutional Networks for High-Resolution Pseudo-Label Generation from Multimodal Earth Observation Data

author.name: Abhishek Singh, Giovanni Cuozzo, Alexander Jacob, Claudia Notarnicola

entry.summary: Introduces a quantum-inspired convolutional encoder-decoder that generates fine-scale pseudo-labels for land-cover mapping by fusing Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery, supervised only by coarse MODIS-derived maps. Evaluated on the DFC2020 dataset, it addresses the scarcity of high-resolution annotations in Earth observation.

entry.title: A Deep Learning Framework for Quantile Demand Forecasting in E-commerce with Doubly Censored Data

author.name: Ziwen Ye, Jiawen Wei, Teng Song, Chen Chen, Guangrui Ma

entry.summary: Addresses quantile demand forecasting in e-commerce where observed sales are capped by stock and boosted by promotions, making labels ambiguous relative to true demand. The framework explicitly models doubly censored data to produce uncertainty-aware quantile forecasts that support robust operational decision-making.

entry.title: Learning Graph Beliefs for Active Radio Mapping With Decision-Certified Multi-Step Sensing

author.name: Wangqian Chen, Hao Wang, Yumeng Zhang, Chenghong Bian, Junting Chen, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: GraphBARC is a graph-structured framework for active radio map construction that couples learned spatial modeling with analytical Bayesian inference, learning correlated node and edge factors from acquired measurements to induce a joint full-map belief. It supports decision-certified multi-step sensing that prioritizes informative measurements without the prohibitive cost of dense sampling.

entry.title: Efficient Deep Gaussian Process Surrogates via Mini-Batch Latent MAP Estimation

author.name: Chun-Yi Chang, Chih-Li Sung

entry.summary: LaMP-DGP replaces variational inference or MCMC in deep Gaussian processes with gradient-based MAP estimation of latent representations, enabling efficient probabilistic prediction via linked-GP calculations. A mini-batch optimization algorithm with theoretical convergence analysis scales the method to large datasets for nonstationary surrogate modeling.

entry.title: Barren Plateaus in Quantum Linear Combinations: Interference and Lie-Algebraic Control

author.name: Amir Koutahi, Pouya Kananian, Hans-Arno Jacobsen

entry.summary: This paper analyzes barren plateaus in quantum linear combinations of unitaries (LCU), proving that for single-pass LCUs with independent branches, gradient variance cannot vanish below the branch variance scaled by the fourth power of the branch coefficient. It derives exact loss and gradient formulas capturing interference contributions between branches and distinguishes single-pass LCUs from circuits alternating branch operations with ancilla mixing.

entry.title: DICE: Decentralized Incentive-driven Federated Learning for Efficient & Scalable Customization of Pretrained Models in Web3

author.name: Hong Lin, Zhongle Xie, Lidan Shou, Ke Chen, Gang Chen

entry.summary: DICE is a blockchain-powered federated learning algorithm for customizing large pretrained models among untrusted Web3 participants, using a dynamic progressive learning scheme plus incentive mechanisms to overcome the compute and memory constraints of heterogeneous participants. It targets efficiency and scalability gaps in existing BCFL approaches.

entry.title: Adaptive Federated Optimization Across Smooth and Nonsmooth Regimes

author.name: Zimeng Wang, Ali Dadras, Alp Yurtsever

entry.summary: AdaFed extends AdaGrad-style adaptivity to federated optimization so that a single parameter choice adapts across smooth and nonsmooth regimes with heterogeneous clients and multiple local steps. It achieves O(1/T) rates for smooth nonconvex and convex objectives and O(1/sqrt(T)) for Lipschitz nonsmooth convex objectives, extending to the stochastic setting under light-tailed noise assumptions. This removes the need to specify smoothness order in advance for federated training.

entry.title: LLM-guided Planar Loco-Manipulation for Quadruped Robots

author.name: Georges Jetti, Michael Khayyat, Jean-Pierre Sleiman, Stefano Arrigoni, Francesco Braghin

entry.summary: The paper presents a language-conditioned task planner, LoRA fine-tuned on synthetic data, that maps natural-language tasks and structured scene representations to variable-length sequences of parameterized actions for quadruped loco-manipulation in cluttered spaces with movable obstacles. Low-level learned skills execute the plans, and the decision space jointly spans skill, object, and geometric target selection. This extends LLM-based robot planning beyond low-dimensional command interfaces.

entry.title: Fu-TCM: a multimodal large language model that learns traditional Chinese medicine diagnostic reasoning

author.name: Jiahang Xie, Tong Jin, Lingfei Wu, Yaping You, Jie Huang, Yuanchang Jin, Weikang Gong, Wei Cheng, Jia You, Pan Sun, Jianfeng Feng, Hongcheng Guo

entry.summary: Presents Fu-TCM, a multimodal LLM for traditional Chinese medicine trained on roughly 7.12 million filtered examples from classical texts, textbooks, medical images, and clinical cases, then optimized with Bianzheng-Grounded Policy Optimization (BGPO), which explicitly targets syndrome differentiation reasoning. Models the four-examination diagnostic chain end to end. Notable for encoding a non-Western medical reasoning tradition in a domain model.

entry.title: Relevance-Guided Residual Calibration for Spectral Compression of Dense Retrieval Embeddings

author.name: Yongkang Li, Panagiotis Eustratiadis, Evangelos Kanoulas

entry.summary: RRC refines spectral (principal-subspace) compression of dense retrieval embeddings using relevance judgments: it estimates margin-based weights per retained direction, retains positive-weight directions, and adds power-law residuals to corpus-derived weighting. This closed-form method better accounts for individual directions' contributions to relevance, reducing storage and scoring cost with less quality loss. It targets the embedding-footprint problem in dense retrieval.

entry.title: Silhouette-Based Gaitomics for Frailty Assessment in Older Adults

author.name: Laura McDaniel, Ryan Roemmich, Crystal Szczesny, Peter Abadir, Rama Chellappa, Basudha Pal

entry.summary: The authors introduce silhouette-based gaitomics, deriving 90 shape, motion, and texture descriptors from walking silhouettes and gait energy images to build interpretable video-based frailty assessments in 66 older adults under the Fried Frailty Phenotype. Feature selection uses minimum redundancy maximum relevance with nested stratified cross-validation at the participant level.

entry.title: Beyond Region Memory: Local Point Tracking for Vocal Cord Localization in Video Laryngoscopy

author.name: Huayu Wang, Gyungmin Ko, Jung Heon Kim, Jia-Xian Jian, Dae Kon Kim, Dong Keon Lee, Hsiang-Wei Huang, Pau-Choo Chung, Linda Shapiro, Richard B. Utarnachitt, Jenq-Neng Hwang, Nathan J. White

entry.summary: This paper proposes Local Point Tracking for vocal-cord localization in emergency video laryngoscopy, combining a single-frame detector with SAM-supported point propagation and stateless mask refinement in a localize-then-snap pipeline. It handles challenges like tissue deformation, specular highlights, and instrument occlusion.

entry.title: MemoryFusion: Cross-Temporal Memory Learning for Multimodal Video Fusion

author.name: Meiqi Gong, Hao Zhang, Jiayi Ma

entry.summary: Presents MemoryFusion, a two-stage framework for multimodal video fusion combining short-term and long-term memory banks with progressive temporal refinement to exploit long-range temporal cues and reduce flickering artifacts. It addresses the underexplored use of distant frames in fusion pipelines.

entry.title: Segment Anything Model Based Context Guided Mamba Unet for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Chenchen Wang, You Zhou

entry.summary: SAMBA-UNet combines SAM's context knowledge with Mamba's hierarchical long-range feature learning in a UNet framework for medical image segmentation, aiming to add domain adaptability to SAM while preserving fine anatomical details that state space models can lose.

entry.title: Morphology-Aware Channel-Decoupled Mamba Network for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Chenchen Wang, You Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes MCDNet, a Mamba-based state-space network for multi-organ CT segmentation that splits feature channels into separate processing groups for differentiated structural modeling, combining adaptive local enhancement with long-range context. It targets the challenges of variable organ shape, low tissue contrast, and ambiguous boundaries in clinical image analysis.

entry.title: GC-LIF: Spiking Group-Equivariant Neural Network With Group-Coupled Membrane Dynamics

author.name: Nhan Trong Luu, Duong Trung Luu, Thang Cong Truong

entry.summary: GC-LIF provides a necessary and sufficient condition for a leaky integrate-and-fire neuron to preserve group equivariance despite its membrane recurrence, solving for parameter constraints in closed form and building group-equivariant spiking networks. This fills a real theoretical gap at the intersection of SNNs and equivariant CNNs. Relevant for energy-efficient, rotation-invariant vision on neuromorphic hardware.

entry.title: Proprioceptive Finger Force Estimation for Reliable Box Manipulation

author.name: Junha Cha, Chanwoo Kim, Kisang Park, Yeoncheol Jang, Doyoung Kim, Seungmin Kim, Kyungjae Lee, Sungjoon Choi

entry.summary: FEEL is an uncertainty-aware method that estimates per-finger external force magnitude from proprioceptive histories, combining a calibrated virtual-spring estimate with a Mixture Density Network residual, eliminating dedicated contact sensors at deployment. The estimates enable continuous per-finger force adaptation for damage-free box manipulation.

entry.title: Information-Driven Collaborative Autonomy for Heterogeneous UAV/UGV Teams

author.name: Joshua Yuriv Pilipovsky

entry.summary: A single-author paper formulating heterogeneous UAV/UGV team coordination for search with potentially hazardous unknown targets, using ergodic control to distribute sensing effort per spatial information density. It incorporates dynamic camera footprints, pose-dependent detection models, and Bayesian inference over angles-only measurements with data association marginalization. The framework targets principled exploration-exploitation balance in multi-robot search.

entry.title: Improving Fine-Grained Manipulation through Demonstration Expansion and Execution Design

author.name: Jingxu Gu, Dongze Lian

entry.summary: The paper introduces DEED, a framework for adapting pretrained vision-language-action policies to fine-grained manipulation tasks, demonstrated on the five MetaFine benchmark tasks. DEED expands demonstrations by generating multiple instruction variants from a single initial scene and rendering each trajectory under varied camera positions and lighting while preserving states and action targets, with a hierarchical sampling strategy balancing instructions, trajectories, and visual conditions during supervised adaptation. This matters because fine-grained manipulation remains a weak point for general VLA policies, and data-efficient adaptation methods address the high cost of robot demonstration collection.

entry.title: TERRA: Task-Oriented Edge AI for Regional Fire Detection with Identity-Free Reporting

author.name: Mohammad Kazemi, Julie A. McCann

entry.summary: TERRA is an edge-AI framework for distributed fire monitoring that combines task-oriented local inference with identity-free, region-tagged reporting and permutation-invariant regional aggregation. Devices report either quantized fire probabilities (TERRA-Score) or compact learned features (TERRA-Feature) rather than raw device-specific measurements, matching the actual regional detection objective.

entry.title: Conformal Predictive Distributions for Contextual Order Fulfillment Optimization

author.name: Tinghan Ye, Amira Hijazi, Pascal Van Hentenryck

entry.summary: The paper builds conformal predictive distributions for regression and classification and embeds them in a contextual optimization model for retail ship-to-home fulfillment decisions, solved via contextual sample-average approximation. It bounds the regret of each fulfillment decision in terms of forecast error, addressing delivery-time uncertainty across orders and fulfillment options.

entry.title: Robust Active Learning for More Efficient and Reliable Paths to Optimal Design

author.name: Hayriye Pehlivan Solak, Francesco Di Fiore, Jeroen Wackers, Riccardo Pellegrini, Andrea Serani, Matteo Diez, Laura Mainini

entry.summary: The authors introduce Multifidelity Cost-Aware Screening (MF-CAS), an active learning strategy that jointly selects both sampling location and model fidelity using decomposed uncertainty intervals and per-fidelity cost estimates. The method is validated on a constrained 14-dimensional hydrodynamic design optimization problem, showing efficient allocation of expensive high-fidelity simulations.

entry.title: TCC-RAG: Temporal Causal Chain-Guided RAG for Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering

author.name: Xinxun Zhang, Yuxiang Wang, Shanshan Feng, Jun Zhang, Tieyun Qian, Binhang Yuan, Kai Yin, Xiao Yan, Jiawei Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes TCC-RAG, which replaces semantic-only RAG for temporal knowledge graph QA with retrieval of concise causal chains that support multi-hop temporal reasoning, reducing redundant knowledge that traps LLMs in spurious reasoning chains. Addresses both insufficient causal structure and noise in standard retrieval. Targets a known weakness of LLMs on complex temporal questions.

entry.title: Verification Learning Theory: A Process Model of Checking and Retention in AI-Assisted Judgment

author.name: Christoph Trattner

entry.summary: Formalizes Verification Learning Theory (VLT), a process model of how AI-assisted claim-evaluation practice with feedback affects retained independent judgment ability. The theory predicts that perceived assistant fallibility can improve delayed unaided judgment through increased verification checking, even without observed errors.

entry.title: Prototype-Guided Dynamic Domain Modulation and a Large-Scale Multi-SKU Benchmark for Shampoo Bottle Surface Defect Detection

author.name: Yuehang Li, Xiao Wang, Qiang Chen, Yangyi Fan, Bo Jiang, Yaowei Wang, Jin Tang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Bottle-SKU, a large industrial benchmark of 13,119 images, 20,419 instance-level annotations, seven defect categories, and 48 bottle SKUs for surface defect detection under realistic product-variant variation. It also proposes a prototype-guided dynamic domain modulation method for SKU-aware detection.

entry.title: Retaining Repair Hypotheses for Cost-Aware Execution

author.name: Jae Hun Hwang, Hong-In Won

entry.summary: The paper studies a repair-to-execution interface that retains multiple compatible guard repairs of an executable model, weights them using diagnostic and execution observations, and uses the resulting predictions to choose routes, priced tests, or backups. On synthetic two-stage devices, an AI-weighted belief over repairs lowers no-test cost by about 2 percent versus committing to a single model-generated repair. It shows value in keeping uncertainty over repairs rather than collapsing early.

entry.title: Non-Zero Radius: The Missing Component of Neural Networks

author.name: Tiansi Dong, Mateja Jamnik, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: The paper argues that representing concepts as spheres with non-zero radii, rather than zero-radius vectors, can address the black-box nature and weak symbolic reasoning of conventional neural networks. It builds on a historical analysis from the McCulloch-Pitts neuron to modern LLMs to motivate sphere-based representation as a foundational change.

entry.title: Efficient Learning of Mechanism Designs and Compositionality

author.name: Jo\~{a}o Pedro Gandarela, Thiago Rios, Stefan Menzel, Andr\'{e} Freitas

entry.summary: Assur-KB represents planar mechanisms through irreducible modules, boundary interfaces, and solve dependencies, with theoretical results characterizing transfer through module interfaces and physical limits from missing interface information. Controlled experiments compare matched mechanism-curve pairs across training budgets, showing that exposing reusable constraint subassemblies improves prediction from limited data.

entry.title: The generative paradox: the Anti-Prompt paradigm for human capability

author.name: Margarita Trifonov Vadim E. Levit

entry.summary: This conceptual paper identifies the generative paradox: AI assistance boosts joint performance but can erode what humans can still understand, challenge, and repair when assistance disappears. It proposes developmental function allocation and an Anti-Prompt paradigm in which AI first creates conditions for a consequential human act rather than preempting it with immediate generation.

entry.title: FIRME: Registry-Anchored Memory Graphs for Evolving, Heterogeneous Investor Knowledge

author.name: Yunbai Zhang, Yunyi Gao, Han-Tai Shiao

entry.summary: FIRME is a registry-anchored memory graph that reconciles recurring investor observations expressed in different surface forms into persistent canonical relationships while retaining source, time, and context. Within periods it fuses investor-call discussions with cash-flow signals via a product-topic ontology; across periods it preserves canonical identities.

entry.title: Responsible Quantum Machine Learning for Medical Imaging: A Fairness Audit Across Sensitive Subgroups

author.name: Giovanni dos Santos Franco, Felipe Mahlow, Ellison Fernando Cardoso, Jos\'e Adenaldo Santos Bittencourt, Felipe Fanchini

entry.summary: The paper audits classical and quantum classifiers for medical imaging fairness on dermatological lesions and chest X-rays, testing differentiable Equalized Odds regularization, gradient reversal, and combinations. Using ResNet-18 embeddings with foundation model references, it explicitly assumes quantum machine learning is not inherently fair and measures subgroup disparities.

entry.title: Prompts and probabilities in the linguistic assessment of language models: Evidence from semantic focus-sensitivity

author.name: Robert Pasternak

entry.summary: This paper tests prompting versus token-probability methods for evaluating linguistic competence in a new domain: semantic focus-sensitivity, using textual focus markers like boldface and italics. Token probabilities perform universally above chance, while prompting mostly underperforms in smaller models but sometimes outperforms probabilities in larger ones.

entry.title: Self-training for cross-centre coronary vessel segmentation in X-ray angiography using pre-contrast frame subtraction

author.name: Danial Moafi, Aida Moafi, Mostafa Aryafar, Ashkan Sami, Maryam Aryafar

entry.summary: The study evaluates whether self-training with pseudo-labels — generated from an nnU-Net trained on the ARCADE dataset and extended using a contrast map obtained by subtracting pre-contrast frames — can improve coronary vessel segmentation on external-center X-ray angiography data without new manual annotation. It also addresses incomplete ARCADE labeling that only covers SYNTAX-score segments. This targets a well-known domain-shift problem in medical image segmentation cheaply.

entry.title: IMPACT: Inverter-Informed Multimodal Learning for Photovoltaic Generation Forecasting

author.name: Anushka Katiyar, Cong Feng, Jing Wang, Tristan Liu, Simon Julien, Zachary Jacobs

entry.summary: A physics-informed multimodal deep learning framework for probabilistic photovoltaic power forecasting over 10-110 minute horizons, combining plant-level temporal history, inverter-level spatial cloud dynamics via graph attention, solar geometry, and meteorological state through gated cross-attention. The decoder is anchored to a smart persistence baseline to learn horizon-dependent corrections.

entry.title: From extreme weather to agricultural consequences with agentic AI

author.name: Minghan Yu, Mengyu Dai, Yixin Wen, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: WxCrop is presented as the first agent that judges agricultural hazards from physically interpretable weather indices with causal analysis and combines weather and agricultural information to predict crop loss for past and forecast dates. It is demonstrated in Florida on hurricanes, freezes, and dry heat with loss models calibrated on insurance records.

entry.title: Interpretable neural equation learning for high-dimensional materials data

author.name: Philip Jacobson, Prasad Iyer, Remi Dingreville, Saaketh Desai

entry.summary: nn-EQL is an equation-learning framework for sparse, high-dimensional materials datasets that generates candidate equations via iterative training, pruning, and retraining with customizable neuron-level activation functions, ranked by a minimum-description-length-inspired score. It includes diagnostics for term-wise contributions, input-scaled sensitivities, and uncertainties, demonstrated on AI-Feynman benchmarks and materials problems.

entry.title: A Hybrid Physics-informed holomorphic neural networks Method

author.name: Zhijie Su, Qiaolin He, Zhiping Mao, Shiquan Zhang
