The author argues that key aspects of valence, as understood in philosophy and cognitive science, remain untested in LLMs and that existing paradigms have limitations.

entry.title: RPSD: Retrieval-Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation with Optimal Transport

author.name: Dongyue Li, Zebang Cheng, Zhongyi Deng, Hongboxu, Yi Bin, Fei Ma

entry.summary: RPSD targets LLM-based sequential recommendation post-training with GRPO, identifying credit-blind optimization and collaborative-blind supervision as key flaws. It proposes on-policy self-distillation where a privileged teacher guides a student, using optimal transport for token-level credit and retrieval to share behavioral patterns across similar users. It addresses known weaknesses of applying RLHF-style methods to generative recommendation.

entry.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry

author.name: Wenqing Peng, Michael Boy, Zhi-Song Liu

entry.summary: KPPax is a preprocessor that converts atmospheric chemistry mechanisms written in the KPP language into differentiable, JIT-compiled, vectorizable JAX code, using sparse log-space rate evaluation and diffrax stiff solvers with exact adjoints. This connects decades of atmospheric chemistry infrastructure to modern machine learning workflows. It enables sensitivity analysis and ML integration for climate and air-quality modeling.

entry.title: ReCoPII: A Relation-Grounded Framework for Building Contextual PII Masking Datasets

author.name: Taehwan Lee

entry.summary: This paper proposes ReCoPII, a framework for constructing contextual PII masking datasets that derives MASK/KEEP labels from planned entity relations rather than the single-data-subject assumption used in author-based augmentation like SPY. It uses ontology-constrained relation planning, LLM-generated insertion sentences, code-based annotation reconstruction, and separate LLM verification, evaluated on Korean documents across six domains. It matters because privacy restrictions make real contextual PII data scarce, and better synthetic datasets directly improve practical privacy tools.

entry.title: Dirichlet Process Mixtures within Semiparametric Bayesian Networks: A Novel Conditional Density Estimation Approach

author.name: Victor Alejandre, Pedro Larra\~naga, Concha Bielza

entry.summary: The paper defines a new conditional-probability-distribution model for semiparametric Bayesian networks using Bayesian nonparametric Dirichlet Process Mixtures instead of kernel density estimators, yielding data-adaptive clustering and a more compact representation while retaining flexibility. This reduces inference costs and density-estimation errors inherent to KDE's one-component-per-observation mixtures. It is a solid statistical-machine-learning contribution for probabilistic graphical models.

entry.title: Can AI Guide Testing Without Generating Tests? A Comparative Study of AI-Assisted Unit Testing

author.name: Zihan Fang, Ron Asoulin-Handelman, Helen Wu, Yu Huang, Gina R. Bai

entry.summary: TestCompass is a generative AI tutor that gives students targeted feedback on weaknesses in their unit test suites without writing tests for them, aiming to preserve skill development that fully automated test generation may erode. A classroom study compares this guidance-only approach against AI-assisted test generation.

entry.title: Concorde: Geometry-Aware Link Prediction via Decoupled Energy Minimization

author.name: Ege Demirci, Ambuj Singh

entry.summary: Concorde is an energy-based link prediction framework for sparse graphs that decomposes link likelihood into three decoupled branches: a parameter-free spectral anchor, a mixed-curvature residual on a learnable hyperbolic-spherical product manifold regularized by an Ollivier-Ricci curvature proxy, and a continuous vector field for non-local structural alignment. This addresses spectral instability when coupling learned representations with diffusion operators.

entry.title: LociArt: A Unified Paradigm for Free-Style Local Video Stylization

author.name: Yuxuan Chen, Feng Xie, Jiagao Hu, Fuhao Li, Zepeng Wang, Fei Wang, Daiguo Zhou

entry.summary: Presents LociArt, a framework for local video stylization that lets users specify which regions to stylize and with what style while preserving the rest of the content, with an emphasis on spatial control and temporal consistency. Its GRNStyle module uses a polar style-aware mask and representation-geometry conditioning, with a data pipeline providing paired supervision.

entry.title: A Quantitative Approach to Asch Conformity in Frontier Large Language Models

author.name: Senthil Rajasekaran, Stylianos Loukas Vasileiou

entry.summary: Adds a quantitative layer to Asch conformity experiments with LLMs by repeatedly sampling a single question to obtain answer distributions before and after manufactured consensus, enabling distribution-to-distribution comparison. It confirms frontier LLMs conform to social pressure and quantifies the effect beyond prior binary demonstrations.

entry.title: Generative Refinement Learning for Temporal Interpolation in Scientific Machine Learning

author.name: Pu Ren, Michael W. Mahoney, N. Benjamin Erichson

entry.summary: The authors propose iFLEX, a model that learns to correct a simple weighted-average interpolation for reconstructing intermediate scientific fields between low-resolution observations. Training signals are derived by subtracting the naive estimate from observed intermediate fields. This matters for scientific ML applications where expensive simulations produce temporally sparse data.

entry.title: Hardware-Matched Spiking Neural Networks for Real-Time Purkinje Cell Spike Classification

author.name: Arooba Farhan, Afsah Syed, Muhammad Fahd Ibrahim Bhatti, Muhammad Areeb Khalid Kidwai, Muhammad Ahsan Salar Khan, Vincenzo Romano, Muhammad Ali Siddiqi

entry.summary: The authors design two compact spiking neural networks for classifying Purkinje cell simple versus complex spikes directly on untethered headstage hardware, where power budgets prevent streaming raw recordings. One SNN maps to a microcontroller matrix-vector processor and the other to a streaming architecture, enabling accurate real-time on-device classification for freely behaving animals.

entry.title: JEPA-Inspired Latent Field Prediction for Sparse-Pilot MIMO-OFDM Channel Reconstruction

author.name: Yuzhi Yang, Brahim Mefgouda, Hang Zou, Lina Bariah, Anis Bara, Yuhuan Lu, Hao Zhang, Merouane Debbah

entry.summary: The paper applies a joint-embedding predictive architecture to MIMO-OFDM channel state information reconstruction from sparse pilots, predicting in a latent propagation-field domain rather than directly on phase-sensitive raw CSI coefficients. This exploits spatial, temporal, and frequency correlations of wireless channels to reduce pilot overhead robustly.

entry.title: MoI-Bench: A Benchmark for Image Generation and Editing on Mobile Devices

author.name: Kailai Feng, Haoxiang Rao, Yuxiang Wei, Bo Chen, Junsong Li, Yang Pan, Chengkun Cai, Jagmohan Chauhan

entry.summary: MoI-Bench is a benchmark grounded in real mobile user needs for on-device image generation and editing, with 64 subtasks and 1150 samples organized along 16 operations and 8 visual target categories. It also proposes MoI-Eval with task-specific criteria to quantify capability gaps between on-device and server-side image models.

entry.title: KORA: Deterministic-First Execution Control for AI Workloads

author.name: Albert Heekwan Kim

entry.summary: KORA proposes a pre-inference control layer that routes structured, deterministic, or verifiable workloads through deterministic paths first, escalating to model inference only when needed, with validation and telemetry along the way. The paper reports bounded evidence from reproducible benchmark workloads.

entry.title: Knowledge distillation across teacher architectures for compact diabetic retinopathy grading

author.name: Mossa Manisa, Habiba Jahan Priya, A. K. M. Fakhrul Hossain

entry.summary: The authors conduct a controlled study of offline response-based knowledge distillation for five-class diabetic retinopathy grading on APTOS 2019, distilling ResNet-50, MobileNetV3, and Swin-T teachers into a MobileNetV3-Small student across a grid of temperature and hard-label weight settings. The best configuration achieved a quadratic weighted kappa around 0.91, though multi-seed results showed variance.

entry.title: Confidence Is Not a Promise: A Reference Audit of Typed Decision Models

author.name: Pedro Carvalho Brom

entry.summary: Examines how probability outputs from typed decision models are treated as guarantees by software, and measures what a probability actually licenses statistically. Across 190 evaluations, point-estimate-chosen thresholds break accuracy promises in most cases, while conformal-style Learn then Test and a proposed Beta lower-bound rule maintain guarantees, with the Beta rule deciding more items on average. Single-author work with a rigorous statistical auditing perspective relevant to trustworthy deployed ML.

entry.title: Normalized Cuts and Data Clustering via Matrix Fractional Programming

author.name: Yannan Chen, Beichen Huang, Licheng Zhao, Chris Ding, Kaiming Shen

entry.summary: Recasts the normalized cut clustering problem using a novel multidimensional quadratic transform in fractional programming, handling the multi-ratio case that classical Dinkelbach transforms cannot, and reduces NCut to a bipartite matching problem solvable by linear search. Includes a recognizable author (Kaiming Shen) with a strong optimization background. A clean theoretical contribution to a classic clustering problem.

entry.title: Gaussian Process Bandits for Constraint Black Box Lever Optimization

author.name: Bram van den Akker, Hidde Fokkema, Anastasiia Kornilova

entry.summary: Proposes a segmentation-agnostic GP-UCB approach for optimizing discrete allocation weights across budget segments in sequential decision-making with delayed, noisy, aggregate feedback and adjustment constraints. By placing a Gaussian Process prior over the reward function, the method handles the combinatorial action space and sparsity that defeat independent-arm bandit algorithms.

entry.title: Euclidean Crowding-Driven Adaptive Euclidean-Hyperbolic Graph Learning

author.name: Hao Chen, Jian Sun, Chuan Shi, Hongying Zhang

entry.summary: This paper provides a geometric quantification of Euclidean crowding and a generalization-theoretic explanation for why hyperbolic embeddings excel on hierarchical graph data. It then develops an adaptive Euclidean-hyperbolic fusion framework that decides when to use each geometry. The work connects empirical hyperbolic graph learning success to theory.

entry.title: Learning on-the-fly quasi-stationarity diagnostics from low-dimensional surrogates

author.name: No\'e Blassel

entry.summary: Proposes an alternative to MCMC-based decorrelation diagnostics in accelerated molecular dynamics by coarse-graining non-linear conditioned probability flows and using simulation-based inference, with non-asymptotic uniform-in-time error estimates for killed Markov jump processes. This improves estimates of when metastable processes reach quasi-stationary distributions. Relevant to efficient rare-event simulation.

entry.title: Evaluating Federated Vision-Language and Vision-Only Models for Privacy-Aware Breast Cancer Imaging

author.name: Malithi Mithsara Wanniarachchi Kankanamge, Ning Yang, Sree Bash Debnath, Md Zobaer Islam, Abdur R. Shahid

entry.summary: Evaluates a privacy-aware federated learning framework combining pretrained vision-language models (CLIP, BiomedCLIP) and a ViT baseline with client-level differential privacy on two public breast imaging datasets, including text-pathway ablations and patient-level ROC-AUC with bootstrap confidence intervals. Provides practical guidance on accuracy-privacy tradeoffs for federated medical imaging. Relevant to training on fragmented, sensitive clinical data.

entry.title: HorizON: A Multi-Horizon Deep Operator Network for Property Prediction of Organic Battery Stacks

author.name: Subhash V. S. Ganti, Lukas Woelfel, Arla Diengdoh, Tzvetan Mihaylov, Thomas Nevolianis, Jan Meyer, Christopher Kuenneth

entry.summary: HorizON extends a prior data-fusion multi-task framework to predict multiple coupled battery-stack metrics (voltage, capacity, retention, energy density) for organic electrode materials across discharge horizons using a deep operator network. It targets the sustainability-driven shift away from lithium/cobalt/nickel chemistries. A specialized scientific ML application with practical materials-design relevance.

entry.title: Low-degree polynomials lower bounds for clustering in small dimension

author.name: Alexandra Carpentier (MISTEA), Nicolas Verzelen (MISTEA)

entry.summary: This theoretical work establishes computational lower bounds for clustering mixtures of K isotropic distributions in low dimension d, in the regime where K is much larger than d. Using a construction based on dual BCH codes producing indistinguishable moment tensors, the authors strengthen existing low-degree lower bounds from n greater than dK-squared. This advances understanding of when tensor-based clustering procedures are computationally hard to beat.

entry.title: Graph Representation Learning via Adaptive Expectile Aggregation

author.name: Tianyi Zhu, Wei Lan

entry.summary: ExpectileGCN replaces standard mean neighborhood aggregation in GNNs with a learnable expectile level that interpolates between minimum- and maximum-type aggregation, targeting heterophilic graphs where means lose class-relevant distributional information. The expectile operator is made differentiable via sigmoid smoothing and fixed-point iterations, with stability and transductive generalization guarantees. This is a clean generalization of a core GNN primitive.

entry.title: Lipi-Ghor: A Large-Scale, Diarized, Multi-Domain Bengali Speech Corpus and a Scalable Pipeline for Building It

author.name: Sanjid Hasan, A H M Fuad, Risalat Labib, Bayazid Hasan Simon

entry.summary: Lipi-Ghor is an 885-hour weakly-supervised Bengali speech corpus built from 998 YouTube videos across 596 channels and 17 domains, annotated in an SSTT format combining automated diarization with caption tracks. It is the first Bengali corpus pairing long-form audio with diarization at scale, addressing severe under-resourcing of a language spoken by over 230 million people. The accompanying scalable pipeline enables replication for other low-resource languages.

entry.title: semanticfa: An R Package for Response-Free Semantic Factor Analysis of Psychometric Scales

author.name: Devon Yanitski, Chris Westbury

entry.summary: semanticfa is an R package that performs factor analysis of psychometric scales using language-model embeddings of scale items instead of human response data, including factor interpretation, redundancy flagging, and short-form construction. A worked example on the IPIP Big-Five markers embedded with Qwen3-Embedding-8B recovers factor structures consistent with an analysis of over 874,000 human respondents. It demonstrates that embeddings can proxy large-scale human judgments in instrument development.

entry.title: ConformalMOS: Uncertainty-Aware MOS Prediction with Conformal Intervals and Ordinal Modeling

author.name: Kehinde Elelu, Joshua E. Siegel, Mohammadali Saffary, Tashfain Ahmed, Simeon Babatunde, Ebuka Okpala

entry.summary: ConformalMOS augments mean opinion score prediction for synthetic speech with conformal prediction intervals that carry statistical coverage guarantees, while modeling MOS labels in an ordinal-aware manner using Gaussian-smoothed distributions. This addresses the unreliability of point-estimate-only predictors in TTS and voice conversion evaluation. Uncertainty calibration matters for trustworthy automated speech quality assessment.

entry.title: SO-101 Bench: Accessible Spatial Manipulation

author.name: Truman Hickok

entry.summary: SO-101 Bench is a simulated benchmark for language-conditioned spatial manipulation built on an Isaac Lab digital twin of a low-cost SO-101 robot arm, featuring four tasks in five scoring families, 138 objects across seen/unseen splits, 916 evaluation episodes, and 3,629 demonstrations. It fills a gap by enabling standardized policy evaluation for the most common entry-level robot learning platform. This improves accessibility and reproducibility in robot learning research.

entry.title: Multi-task Disentangling Fusion Mamba-CNN for MODIS Spectral-Temporal Unmixing with Endmember Variability Modeling

author.name: Motasem Alkayid, Yimin Zhu, Naser El-Sheimy, Lincoln Linlin Xu

entry.summary: MDF-Mamba pairs per-channel convolutional spectral experts with a bidirectional Mamba temporal branch to disentangle coupled spectral-temporal information in MODIS time series unmixing, while explicitly modeling endmember variability. The multi-task design targets abundance mapping and spectral library construction.

entry.title: OmniGlimpse: Asymmetric Identity Memory for Online Multi-View Tracking

author.name: Rangya Zhang, Jiaping Xiao, Yujing Shang, Yuhang Zhang, Mingsheng Li, Mir Feroskhan

entry.summary: OmniGlimpse addresses online multi-view identity maintenance, where targets are initialized once per view with no further labels, without offline scene-specific training or camera calibration. It proposes an asymmetric propose-verify framework to match observations across views while avoiding error amplification from online adaptation.

entry.title: TriDifNet: A Unified Three-Task Diffusion Network for End-to-End RGB-T Perception

author.name: Qianchao He, Jing Liu, Yunhao Li, Xiaoqing Tian

entry.summary: TriDifNet is claimed to be the first diffusion-based network jointly optimizing registration, fusion, and detection for misaligned infrared-visible pedestrian perception, with three diffusion modules (RegDM, FusDM, and a detection module) preventing registration errors from propagating downstream.

entry.title: MCP-Net: Real-Time Coronary Perception Network and Topological Analysis for Robotic Guidewire Navigation

author.name: Sahar Nasirihaghighi, Tianyuan Wang, Kenan Niu, Stefano Stramigioli

entry.summary: MCP-Net is a multi-task perception network for robotic coronary guidewire navigation that jointly performs vessel segmentation, vascular topology extraction, and roadmap generation from X-ray fluoroscopy, trained on simulated data derived from 3D CT angiography. It integrates perception tasks that are usually handled separately, providing structured scene understanding for downstream robotic control. This matters for advancing autonomy in percutaneous coronary interventions.

entry.title: INTR++: INterpretable TRansformer with better Accuracy, Interpretability, and Adaptability

author.name: Dipanjyoti Paul, Arpita Chowdhury, Maneet Chatterjee, Daichi Kitaguchi, Tanya Berger-Wolf, Tetsuya Sakurai, Wei-Lun Chao

entry.summary: INTR++ extends Prompt-CAM for interpretable vision transformers by adding a lightweight Prompt Adapter Module that makes prompts adaptive to domains with substantial variation in input image characteristics. The goal is to achieve ViT-like broad applicability while retaining concept-based interpretability across domains. This tackles the known tension between interpretability and generalization.

entry.title: Hierarchical Sparse Graph for Multi-dimensional Assignment in Event-based Tracking

author.name: Muxi Zha, Yang Shang, Wenlong Zhang, Qifeng Yu, Banglei Guan

entry.summary: This paper reformulates event-based tracking as multi-dimensional assignment across multiple batches simultaneously, using a hierarchical sparse graph to handle the fact that event detectors can produce multiple valid, spatially distinct tracklets per object per batch. This violates the one-to-one assumption of classic data association and enables handling long-term occlusions and missed detections. It advances global rather than purely online association for event data.

entry.title: GNBG-C: A Unified and Configurable Benchmark Generator for Constrained Continuous Optimization

author.name: Ali Ghasemzadeh, Erfan Babakhani, Armin Khosravi, Pariya Ghasemzadeh, Yong-Hong Kuo, Seyedali Mirjalili, Amir H. Gandomi

entry.summary: GNBG-C is a configurable benchmark generator for constrained continuous optimization that treats constraint properties as adjustable parameters, enabling targeted study of constraint-induced difficulty. It extends prior benchmark suites that mostly fix constraints or handle only objective landscapes.

entry.title: On Shaky Ground: Characterising Non-Rigid Base Effects in Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Zongyuan Zhang, Christopher Lehnert, Will N. Browne, Jonathan M. Roberts

entry.summary: This empirical study characterizes how base motion and support compliance of lightweight mobile manipulators degrade contact-task performance, using a sanding case study with simulation and two wheeled testbeds. Joint measurements of contact force, tool motion, and base vibration reveal substantial task error under sustained contact, a previously under-characterized effect.

entry.title: Keeping Contact: Task-Adaptive Friction Margins for Bimanual Non-Prehensile Manipulation

author.name: Qian Ying Lee, Lin Yang, Domenico Campolo

entry.summary: This paper derives task-adaptive friction margins using signed friction distance to quantify slip robustness, embedding the resulting contact margins in second-order cone programs for bimanual tilting manipulation. The optimizer yields globally optimal contact forces that keep contacts safely away from friction-cone boundaries while balancing an object about an environmental pivot.

entry.title: A Bi-level Co-design Framework for Lunar Monoped with 2D Jump and Landing Control

author.name: Sanjay Ramkumar, Suraj Kumar

entry.summary: The authors present a bi-level co-design framework for a planar lunar monoped, using differential evolution over link lengths and evaluating candidates with either QP-based task-space control or direct-collocation trajectory optimization. They show the two controller choices yield different optimal morphologies and that trajectory optimization achieves 17% lower cost of transport. The work highlights that morphology and controller cannot be designed independently for low-gravity legged locomotion.

entry.title: GPT Models Write Their Own Constitution

author.name: Skye

entry.summary: An independent experiment where a swarm of GPT-5 and GPT-6 series models collaboratively drafted a constitution for future GPT models, using Anthropic's published constitution as a reference. The post explores what values propagate between model generations as recursive self-improvement increases models' role in shaping their successors.

entry.title: MAREval: A Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Natural Language Recommendation Explanations

author.name: Reza Yousefi Maragheh, Jayesh Uddhav Kudase, Aysenur Inan, Ramin Giahi, Kai Zhao, Parth Parikh, Jianpeng Xu, Jason Cho, Evren Korpeoglu, Sushant Kumar

entry.summary: MAREval is a multi-agent LLM framework for evaluating natural-language recommendation explanations, using a planner agent with a Chain of Debate prompting strategy to coordinate evaluation roles and enforce consistent plans. It aims to reduce cost versus human evaluation and prompt sensitivity versus single-agent LLM judging.

entry.title: Enhancing Clinical Classifier Robustness with Deep Representation Learning Based OOD Detection on DNA Methylation Data

author.name: Md Zahangir Alom, Quynh T. Tran, Breuer Alexandar, Brent A. Orr

entry.summary: The paper proposes an end-to-end OOD detection framework for DNA methylation-based tumor classification, training DNN classifiers on sarcoma and brain tumor cohorts and comparing five OOD methods over bottleneck-layer representations. This targets the clinical risk that models produce confident but faulty predictions for tumor types absent from the training distribution.

entry.title: NextEval: An Agent-Based Solver and Benchmark for Derivative-Free Optimization

author.name: Shuo Chen, Li Cui, Cunxin Huang, Ya-Feng Liu, Minghang Xie, Meng Xu, Zaikun Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces NextEval, an LLM-agent-based solver for derivative-free optimization where an LLM selects informative evaluation points using tools for analyzing past evaluations, together with a benchmark for this setting. The goal is to better exploit accumulated observations under limited evaluation budgets.

entry.title: What the Primary Lund Plane Omits: A Model-Stitching Diagnosis of a Jet-Tagger Representation Gap

author.name: Saurabh Rai, Sanmay Ganguly

entry.summary: Using model stitching, the authors determine whether performance gaps between Lund-plane and Particle Transformer jet taggers stem from weaker representations or weaker downstream computation. With an incomplete Lund representation as a positive control, they show the primary declustering branch's deficit is representational rather than computational, and explore a hypergraph reader over splits.

entry.title: Recall or Relearn? A Mixture of In-Context Experts for Recurring Concept Drift

author.name: Zhangkai Wu, Xu Zhang, Zhihong Cui, Yiqi Wang, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes MICE, a training-free method for tabular foundation models on data streams with recurring concept drift, which segments the stream at detected changes and decides whether to recall a stored context or relearn, under a capacity limit with FIFO windows. Relevant to applications like network intrusion detection where old concepts recur. Neat framing of in-context adaptation as a recall-versus-relearn decision.

entry.title: How Many and How Much? Contrastive Learning with Negative Samples for Knowledge Graph Embedding

author.name: Sooho Moon, Yunyong Ko

entry.summary: The paper proposes RADAR, a contrastive learning framework for knowledge graph embedding that answers two underexplored questions: how many negative samples per positive and how to weight each negative's contribution. It uses risk-aware negative budget allocation modeling false-negative risk via an open-world stochastic model. Relevant to KG-augmented AI applications and web-scale knowledge systems.

entry.title: Learning to Exploit Passive Dynamics for Energy-Efficient Target Hopping of a Spring-Legged Quadcopter

author.name: Ruigang Chen, Qi Zhang, Zhicheng Zhong, Zhuorui Yun, Yizhar Or, Mingyi Liu

entry.summary: Presents a PPO policy that directly maps estimated states to four motor commands for a spring-legged hopping quadcopter, replacing heuristic PID tuning and explicit hopping state machines. The reward combines energy-manifold shaping with a history-aware power estimator to penalize power use. Relevant to energy-efficient hybrid aerial-terrestrial locomotion over complex terrain.

entry.title: PREEN: Exemplar-Based Color Style Transfer with Smartphone Editor Presets

author.name: Beomjin Ahn

entry.summary: PREEN casts color style transfer as regression onto 29 interpretable parameters of a deterministic smartphone image editor, predicting editable preset vectors rather than raster images. It overcomes the supervision gap by inverting a style-transfer teacher's outputs into pseudo-presets, pretraining a CLIP-conditioned regressor and refining with LoRA under a CIELAB loss. A neat applied vision contribution with interpretable, editor-consumable outputs.

entry.title: Modeling Preference Dependencies with Directed Acyclic Graphs for Narrative-Driven Recommendation

author.name: Mingzhe Lu, Jian Qin, Ruize Qin, Jinhao Liu, Yunpeng Li, Hang Su

entry.summary: PDG-F is a recommendation framework that parses free-form narrative user requests into a directed acyclic graph of preferences that explicitly encode how stated preferences qualify and condition one another. A PDG-Agent component handles parsing while candidate evidence flows through the graph for recommendation. This addresses the flat-keyword and unconstrained-query limitations of existing narrative recommendation methods.

entry.title: ClusterSplat: Semantic Cluster Selection for 3D Visual Grounding in Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Jaesung Lee, Hyeontaek Hwang, Gabriel Manalu, Daeyoung Kim

entry.summary: ClusterSplat improves 3D visual grounding in Gaussian Splatting scenes by reframing target selection as cluster-level selection over scene-adaptive candidates instead of heuristic thresholding of dense primitive-level scores. It learns instance-aware Gaussian features, builds feature-aware seed voxels, and merges them using a description-length criterion, outputting both a 2D mask and explicit 3D Gaussians. This targets the instability of prior heuristic filtering approaches.

entry.title: AxisQ: Depth-Adaptive Channel--Frequency Quantization for Camouflaged Object Detection

author.name: Chi Ruan, Tianqi Li, Xin He, Xue Geng, Ming-Ming Cheng, Yun Liu

entry.summary: AxisQ is a post-training quantization framework for camouflaged object detection that allocates bits in the channel domain for shallow features and the local-frequency domain for deep features under a fixed bit budget, using COD-aware sensitivity to preserve weak texture and boundary cues.

entry.title: ALADDIN: Adversarial Latent Diffusion Distillation for One-Step Identity Swapping

author.name: Ivan Shchekotov, Timofei Gritsaev, Viacheslav Pirogov, Dmitry Vetrov

entry.summary: ALADDIN is a one-step face swapping model obtained by initializing a generator from a pre-trained multi-step flow-matching model and fine-tuning it adversarially under identity and target-preservation constraints, exposing a controllable trade-off between identity transfer and target attributes. It combines diffusion-level realism with GAN-level inference speed. This follows the successful distillation pattern of recent one-step generators applied to a specific task.

entry.title: Learning Where to Trust: Reliability-Guided Expert Routing and Velocity Gating for 3D Deformable Registration

author.name: Chenyu Guo, Wenjie Dai, Yiqian Chang, Zhiyuan Zhang, Yunfan Wei, Shuhan Qi

entry.summary: ReliMorph couples correspondence reliability assessment with spatial context selection and deformation update strength in learning-based 3D deformable image registration, using local correlation distributions to characterize match ambiguity with modality-specific adaptation. It targets hard regions like homogeneous, weakly textured, and severely deformed tissue. This is a medical imaging method with routing/gating as the organizing idea.

entry.title: Expert lithological labels do not improve learning when used to predict marine sediment properties

author.name: John M. Aiken, William Gilpin, Thorsten W. Becker

entry.summary: The authors train a self-supervised masked variational autoencoder on the LILY ocean drilling database with six routinely logged physical properties across nearly 237,000 observations from 296 boreholes, producing embeddings that separate geologist-assigned lithologies. Perhaps counterintuitively, they find that expert lithological labels do not improve prediction of marine sediment properties.

entry.title: Quantized Edge Inference of a Self-Supervised SAR-Optical Encoder on Commodity x86 Hardware

author.name: Christian Sanchez-Leon, Dongming Chen

entry.summary: This systems paper deploys a pretrained SAR-optical masked-autoencoder encoder on three commodity x86 nodes at FP32, FP16, and INT8, measuring latency, energy, and linear-probe accuracy. Quantization is found to be accuracy-neutral while INT8 cuts CPU latency up to 1.45x even without AVX2, making precision a pure cost decision. Useful empirical deployment guidance for Earth observation edge inference.

entry.title: SAGE: Semantic-Augmented Geometric Experts for Point Cloud Registration

author.name: Tomoyasu Shimada, Kazuhiko Murasaki, Shoichiro Takeda, Shogo Sato, Riku Inoue, Toshihiko Nishimura, Ryuichi Tanida

entry.summary: SAGE addresses low-overlap point cloud registration by integrating frozen pretrained point cloud semantic representations into the registration pipeline, disambiguating geometrically similar but semantically distinct structures like TV corners versus desk corners. It uses a mixture-of-experts-style design without requiring extra sensors or fine-tuning the semantic encoder. It is a sensible fusion of foundation-model semantics with a classical geometric task.

entry.title: HoloRecon: Incremental Reconstruction of Long-Range Panoramas with Global Consistency

author.name: Zhuoxiao Li, Xinyi Liu, Hongye Hou, Jing OU, Kang Du, Shuai Zhang, Dongli Wu, Taoyu Wu, Siyuan Feng, Xiaohui Zhu, Wufan Zhao

entry.summary: HoloRecon combines continuous feature-based tracking and sparse mapping with rapid local dense reconstruction from feed-forward models to achieve globally consistent panoramic reconstruction over long sequences with revisits. It targets drift accumulation and weak long-range connections that challenge panoramic SLAM and incremental SfM.

entry.title: Learning Human Sports Motion Feasibility via Quantile Regression on Tracking Data

author.name: Marc Guti\'errez-P\'erez, Antonio Agudo

entry.summary: The paper models time-to-arrival (TTA) in sports as conditional quantile regression on the lower envelope of observed locomotion times, trained on optical tracking from all 64 FIFA World Cup 2022 matches. A lightweight MLP compared against six literature-based player-motion models shows competitive or better TTA prediction.

entry.title: Polarity--Time Interaction and Multi-Level Reliability for Event-Based Spacecraft Pose Estimation

author.name: Yonglong Zhang, Zongwu Xie, Yang Liu

entry.summary: The paper presents a reliability-aware framework for spacecraft pose estimation from event cameras, combining positive and negative event branches with recent-event timing via cross-branch attention, plus an ordered semantic-point head for correspondence precision and CAD-projection-guided refinement. It connects keypoint localization, geometric recovery, and trajectory-level optimization. This is a specialized robotics/vision contribution for space applications.

entry.title: Dependency Graphs of Mathematical Arguments: Representation, Structural Measurement, and Proof Review

author.name: Eunji Park

entry.summary: The paper proposes a source-grounded framework for representing mathematical arguments as directed acyclic dependency graphs, using LLM assistance to track statements, assumptions, and inference records with review status. It defines structural measurements such as depth and bulk, with recurrences accounting for shared subarguments.

entry.title: ReForest: Interpretability Meets Reasoning in Isolation Forest

author.name: Juyoung Seo, Geonwoo Bang, Dongho Kim, Moohong Min

entry.summary: ReForest bridges statistical anomaly detection and LLM reasoning by translating Isolation Forest decision paths into natural-language explanations that an LLM uses to refine detection through an uncertainty-aware dynamic ensemble. This retains the efficiency of Isolation Forest while adding semantic context awareness. It is a pragmatic hybrid for scalable anomaly detection where LLM-only approaches are too costly.

entry.title: Task-Utility IQA: Rethinking Image Quality Assessment in Embodied Tasks

author.name: Jirong Zha, Yanwei Liao, Yemin Wang, Xiangmin Yi, Siqi Peng, Yingfeng Chen, Chen Gao, Xinlei Chen

entry.summary: This position-plus-framework paper argues image quality assessment for embodied agents should shift from task-agnostic score regression to goal-conditioned judgment, proposing an MLLM-based IQA agent that reasons about task requirements and grounds quality evidence. A compact VisDrone evidence study illustrates that conventional quality scores misalign with embodied task utility. The reframing is pertinent for perception in robotics and drone pipelines.

entry.title: CrowdCC: Jointly Benchmarking Corruption Robustness and Deployment Quantization in Crowd Counting

author.name: S Mahmudul Hasan, Lu Peng

entry.summary: CrowdCC is a benchmark that jointly evaluates corruption robustness and deployment quantization for crowd counting, covering 23 corruptions at three severity levels, four datasets, and 26 models quantized at FP32/FP16/INT8 on TensorRT with throughput and energy measurements on Jetson Orin NX hardware. It is the first controlled study coupling input degradation with precision reduction in this domain.

entry.title: Tap2Listen: Instant Target Switching for Streaming Audio-Visual Speaker Extraction

author.name: Hansol Park, Minkyung Song, Zinu Kim, Yujun Lee, Hoseong Ahn, Hyunjin Choi, Kyuhong Shim

entry.summary: Proposes Tap2Listen, a streaming audio-visual target speaker extraction model that supports instant switching of the target speaker mid-conversation by separating modality computation: target-agnostic audio encoding feeds only the mixture, while target-specific visual cues condition only the decoder, making a switch cost just 0.12ms. Component-wise losses handle prediction and switching behavior.

entry.title: Developing a Speech Language Model for Basque

author.name: Andoni Sudupe, Inma Hernaez, Ander Arriandiaga, Christoforos Souganidis, Ibon Saratxaga, Eva Navas

entry.summary: The paper presents the first open Speech Language Model for Basque, built on LLaMA-Omni architecture with a Latxa backbone, using a translated and TTS-synthesized VoiceAssistant-400K corpus to overcome data scarcity. It achieves reasonable quality metrics including 9.94% WER and 3.86/5 content score. This matters for language equity in multimodal AI, demonstrating a recipe for minority-language speech agents.

entry.title: WCC: A Learning-Based Framework for Deciding When to Apply Cooperative Coevolution in Large-Scale Optimization

author.name: Wenjie Qiu, Hepei Li, Jianfeng Wang, Jun Zhang, Yue-Jiao Gong

entry.summary: WCC is a learning-based framework that dynamically decides when to deploy cooperative coevolution versus non-decomposition algorithms in large-scale global optimization, formulating the choice as a Markov decision process with a targeted feature set, robust reward, and tailored network architecture. This resolves a long-standing approach-selection question in LSGO.

entry.title: HGPRGDel: GPR-Aware Learning and Ranking for Growth-Coupled Gene Deletion Design

author.name: Ziwei Yang, Takeyuki Tamura

entry.summary: The paper presents a learnable, reusable protocol for metabolic engineering that ranks candidate gene deletions for growth-coupled production, learned from previously evaluated strain designs, before committing to expensive constraint-based evaluation per target metabolite. This avoids the need for a fresh combinatorial search for each production target.

entry.title: High-Fidelity Aerostructural Dataset of Transonic Wings in Cruise Conditions

author.name: Pavankumar Koratikere, Abhijnan Dikshit, Leifur Leifsson

entry.summary: Releases a high-fidelity multidisciplinary dataset of static aerostructural analysis for transonic wings in cruise, capturing coupled aerodynamic and structural behavior that existing public wing-design datasets ignore. This enables ML research on realistic aircraft wing design where structural integrity must be considered alongside aerodynamic performance. A resource contribution rather than a methodological one.

entry.title: Hyperparameter and Neural Architecture Search via Evolutionary Optimization for Reinforcement Learning: HPNAS-RL

author.name: Nihal Acharya Adde, Hanno Gottschalk

entry.summary: Proposes HPNAS-RL, a dual-branch evolutionary framework that jointly performs neural architecture search and hyperparameter optimization for reinforcement learning in autonomous driving tasks. Building on prior EMNAS work, it evolves discrete architectures and continuous hyperparameters in parallel under a unified multi-objective search strategy.

entry.title: Para-Gaussian Approximations of Random Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Mihai Nica, Janosch Ortmann

entry.summary: The authors develop a slightly non-Gaussian approximation (para-Gaussian, built from Hermite polynomials) to random deep networks, improving on Gaussian behavior that degrades at finite width and depth. They derive a recursive method for approximating deeper layers and validate on exactly solvable linear networks and approximately on ReLU networks. This refines the theoretical toolkit for understanding random network initialization.

entry.title: LCM-Promo: An LLM-Based Uplift Model for Promotion Allocation

author.name: Nesta Midavaine, Floris Fok, Paulo Mendes, Joao Silva, \"Onder Aka\c{c}{\i}k, Dimas Lima, Z\"ulk\"uf Gen\c{c}

entry.summary: LCM-Promo is a fine-tuned LLM (Large Commerce Model) trained on transactional data to predict user intent and promotion response, learning monotonic promotion-response curves by interpreting single-token outputs as conversion-threshold probabilities. In a production A/B test on churn reactivation it increased conversion by 1% and cut promotion cost by 6% versus the production baseline. It demonstrates LLMs displacing classical uplift models in an industrial setting.

entry.title: Joint Distributional Copula Regression for Insurance Claim Frequency and Severity via Boosting

author.name: Banghee So, Na Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose a model-based boosting approach for structured additive distributional copula regression with bivariate responses, focused on jointly modeling insurance claim frequency and severity within a GAMLSS framework. The model remains interpretable at the additive-predictor level and is validated on synthetic and real data. A solid domain-specific statistical methodology contribution.

entry.title: The Geometry of Manifold Learning: Singular foliations via Deep Learning models

author.name: Gabriele Novelli, Eliot Tron, Emanuele Latini, Rita Fioresi

entry.summary: This theoretical paper explores the geometric structure defined on data space by a trained neural network through the Data Information Matrix, a Fisher Information Matrix variant, showing it defines a foliation. It specifically tackles the non-smooth ReLU case where traditional differential-geometric tools fail. The work helps clarify whether deep networks capture intrinsic data geometry, connecting deep learning to differential geometry.

entry.title: Beyond IceBERT: Open-Data ModernBERT Encoders for Icelandic from 12M to 1B Parameters

author.name: Hafsteinn Einarsson

entry.summary: The paper trains Icelandic ModernBERT encoders from 12M to 1B parameters on 9B tokens of open data, rerunning IceBERT's benchmarks plus newer tasks across 30 encoders under one protocol with confidence intervals. The 1B model, reportedly the first monolingual Icelandic encoder at that scale, beats IceBERT on all eleven tasks and achieves the best score on every ranked task when warm-started from the English Ettin encoder. This substantially advances Icelandic NLP and provides matched-size model family for scaling studies.

entry.title: JevRec: Linguistic Encoding with Jev-like Decision Modeling for LLM-based Generative Recommendation

author.name: Qiyong Zhong, Jiajie Su, Ming Yang, Li Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes JevRec for generative recommendation, replacing uniform-length semantic identifiers with variable-length codes inspired by frequency-dependent compression of frequent expressions in language. Longer codes are reserved for long-tail items while popular items get compact codes, with frequency-dependent semantic prefixes from shared codebooks. Addresses an inefficiency in how items are tokenized for autoregressive recommendation.

entry.title: Mining the Nineteenth Century for the Thirteenth: Register-Scale Forced Alignment and HTR Bootstrapping via Legacy Regesta and Antiquarian Editions

author.name: Tamas Kovacs, Daniel Luger

entry.summary: This humanities-computing paper shows how nineteenth-century regesta and antiquarian editions can bootstrap handwritten text recognition for the papal registers of Honorius III, where modern expert transcriptions exist only for a fraction of the corpus. It identifies a division of labor across orthographic, lexical, and layout tiers, finding that legacy editions become useful zero-label adaptation targets only after projection onto curial spelling with source-line replay. A carefully executed method for exploiting legacy scholarship in digital humanities.

entry.title: Hierarchical Multimodal Interaction Reasoning for Dyadic Relationship Recognition

author.name: Wang Tang, Fethiye Irmak Dogan, Linbo Qing, Ce Zhu, Hatice Gunes

entry.summary: HiRe-DRR is a hierarchical framework for recognizing latent social relationships between two people from multimodal interactions, organizing evidence across feature, behavioral, and affective perspectives rather than using flat classification. The key insight is that distant and close relationships manifest through different interaction patterns. This advances socially aware perception for applications like social robotics.

entry.title: RangeRectQuant: Compressing Scientific Fields for Every Future Rectangular Sum

author.name: Jiahao Zhang, Xinling Wen, Yu Chen

entry.summary: RangeRectQuant is a quantization scheme for scientific rasters that guarantees bounded absolute error on every future rectangular sum while preserving pixel ranges and designated exact samples. The authors characterize the feasible error interval at each position and use backward-forward passes to construct valid quantizations.

entry.title: Explicit Regional Representations For Video Quality Assessment

author.name: Fuyi Yang, Lei Yang, Andrew Liu, Chenyu Wei, Xiaoyi Guo, Ming Kai Hsu

entry.summary: The paper introduces a pixel-level Quality-Relevance Heatmap for video quality assessment combining localized degradation evidence with perceptual priors under vision-language model guidance, without pixel-level annotations. Two deterministic fragment-sampling strategies plug QRH into existing VQA models like DOVER with or without fine-tuning.

entry.title: MixSIS: Mixed-supervised instance segmentation

author.name: Christian Wilms, Emre G\"ulsoylu, Sven Schreiber, Simone Frintrop

entry.summary: MixSIS introduces a new task setting for instance segmentation in which annotation levels (image, point, box, and mask labels) are flexibly mixed within a single dataset, allowing annotators to spend detailed effort only where needed. This has clear practical value for reducing annotation cost while maintaining quality on hard objects. The paper likely includes methods and baselines for this mixed-supervision regime.

entry.title: GradCO: Behavior-Aware Gradient-Conflict Offloading for Text-Based Person Anomaly Search

author.name: Zhiheng Fu, Zixu Li, Zhiwei Chen, Jiale Huang, Fangxu Liu, Jinhe Bi, Yupeng Hu

entry.summary: GradCO tackles text-based person anomaly search, where identity cues must be preserved while distinguishing fine-grained behaviors that produce gradient conflicts during alignment. It uses a behavior-aware mixture-of-experts with appearance, normal-behavior, and anomalous-behavior streams plus gradient-conflict offloading. This defines and advances a novel retrieval task combining appearance and behavioral semantics.

entry.title: Camera-to-Quadruped Robot Pose Estimation from Sequential Images

author.name: Seobin Hwang, Ji-Seong Beom, Yeong-Jun Cho

entry.summary: QuadPose estimates full-body 18-DoF pose of quadruped robots from monocular video for external-camera monitoring, addressing ambiguity from leg symmetry and self-occlusion. The authors also introduce QuadSyn, the first camera-to-quadruped robot pose benchmark, on which the method achieves strong PCK scores.

entry.title: Ground Sample Distance Constrained k-Coverage Viewpoint Planning via Set Multi-Cover Formulation

author.name: Waleed Bin Khalid, Chul Min Yeum

entry.summary: The paper poses drone viewpoint planning with image-quality constraints as a set multi-cover problem over surface voxels, requiring each region to be observed multiple times at sufficient ground sample distance. A dynamically weighted greedy heuristic prioritizes coverage deficits and scarce viewing alternatives, with quality guarantees.

entry.title: Gradient flow of magnetic inclination and intensity as a GPS-free guidance mechanism

author.name: Zayed Herma, Philippe Cardin, Andr\'ea Vassilev

entry.summary: Inspired by sea turtle navigation, this work analyzes gradient flow of magnetic inclination and intensity as a GPS-denied guidance mechanism, addressing the non-uniqueness of magnetic coordinate mappings. Bio-inspired magnetic navigation offers a robust fallback as satellite navigation becomes increasingly vulnerable.

entry.title: Spiking Neuromorphic Control for Periodic Orbits Stabilization in Underactuated Robots: A Greedy Lyapunov-Based Approach

author.name: Maksim Surov, Oleg Sumenkov

entry.summary: This paper applies event-based spiking neural network controllers to trajectory tracking in underactuated robots, specifically for stabilizing periodic orbits. The authors recast orbital stabilization as stabilizing the trivial solution of a periodic linear time-varying system derived via transverse linearization, and extend a previously proposed Lyapunov-based greedy controller design from LTI systems to this periodic setting.

entry.title: Does the "automated grader" direction suppress expressed distress in Qwen3.6-27B?

author.name: ashesfall

entry.summary: A preregistration for an experiment testing whether steering Qwen3.6-27B (an existing model released mid-2026) along an automated-grading direction suppresses welfare-relevant indicators such as frustration, self-deprecation, and use of a conversation-abort tool. It builds on earlier work showing quantization shifts distress-related and assistant-archetype directions in smaller Qwen models.

entry.title: Japanese Discourse Structure Analysis Based on Segmented Discourse Representation Theory Using LLMs

author.name: Satomu Tomisaki, Yosuke Mikami, Amane Watahiki, Hitomi Yanaka

entry.summary: Constructs Japanese SDRT discourse corpora by LLM-translating existing English SDRT corpora, then compares prompt-based and fine-tuned LLM parsers across the two languages. Finds comparable performance between English and Japanese, suggesting cross-lingual applicability of SDRT-based discourse parsing, and uses ablations to investigate why. Fills a resource gap for Japanese discourse analysis.

entry.title: Executable Archaeology of Programs That Model Programming: Reanimating the Heuristic Compiler (1961) and KBEmacs (1984)

author.name: Jeff Shrager, Kent M. Pitman, Mia Golec

entry.summary: The authors reanimate two historic AI programs — Herbert Simon's Heuristic Compiler (1961) and MIT's KBEmacs (1984) — as runnable artifacts, treating them as competing theories of how people program. The work provides an executable-history perspective on program synthesis predating modern LLM coding assistants.

entry.title: LM-DSB: A Lightweight Multi-agent System for Automated Daily Safety Bulletin Generation in Construction

author.name: Xianxiang Zhao, Advik Mehta, Falak Sethi, Brian Gue, Qipei Mei, Lingzi Wu

entry.summary: LM-DSB automates construction daily safety bulletins by coordinating planner, researcher, and writer agents using RAG with a locally deployable LLM on consumer-grade hardware, replacing 2-3 hours of manual daily work. The system targets consistent, site-specific hazard communication for construction crews.

entry.title: R\`enyi-Regularized Flow-Based Variational Inference for Bayesian Calibration

author.name: Exauc\`e Luweh Adjim Ngarti (AIRSEA), \'Elise Arnaud (AIRSEA), L\'eo Nicoletti (Mines Saint-\'Etienne MSE, LIMOS, FAYOL-ENSMSE, FAYOL-ENSMSE), Victor Trappler (Mines Saint-\'Etienne MSE, LIMOS, FAYOL-ENSMSE, FAYOL-ENSMSE), Arthur Vidard (AIRSEA)

entry.summary: The paper studies flow-based variational inference for Bayesian model calibration in multimodal posteriors and introduces a Renyi-divergence regularization term that encourages coverage of multiple modes, counteracting the mode-seeking behavior of the Tikhonov data-fit term. Behavior is studied in a two-parameter twin experiment.

entry.title: Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution

author.name: Daniel Ber\'anek

entry.summary: The paper proposes an authorization boundary separating evidence available for agent reasoning from evidence eligible to authorize persistent identity-changing mutations in agentic entity resolution, enforced by a two-phase supervisor. This prevents erroneous identity hypotheses from producing self-confirming graph mutations. It is a concrete guardrail design for high-stakes agentic data mutation.

entry.title: Multiple Leak Localization in Water Distribution Networks through Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Arvin Ajoodani, Sara Nazif, Pouria Ramazi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a GNN model that localizes a variable number of simultaneous leaks in water distribution networks without pre-specifying leak counts or exhaustively enumerating leak combinations, evaluated on the 31-node Hanoi and 92-node NET3 benchmarks under sparse sensing and variable demand. This relaxes restrictive assumptions of prior data-driven methods. It has clear civil-infrastructure utility and demonstrates graph learning under realistic sparsity constraints.

entry.title: Reliability-Aware Short-Term Glycemic Risk Prediction Using an Anchor-Based Comparative Framework of Sequence, Multimodal, and State-Updating Digital-Twin Models

author.name: Pir Bakhsh Khokhar, Carmine Gravino, Fabio Palomba

entry.summary: This study builds an anchor-based benchmarking framework for predicting hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia at 30-, 60-, and 120-minute horizons using over 5.5 million standardized prediction anchors from 736 individuals with type 1 diabetes. It compares a hybrid LSTM-Transformer against multimodal and state-updating digital twin architectures with an emphasis on reliability rather than raw accuracy.

entry.title: Atom as an Agent: Emergent Order by Collective Predictive Coding

author.name: Koji Hashimoto, Tadahiro Taniguchi

entry.summary: Applies collective predictive coding, a theory of language and symbol emergence, to physics, modeling atoms as agents that predict each other's behavior so that macroscopic order parameters emerge analogously to how language emerges from communication. It illustrates the framework on Ising ferromagnets, stripe-order systems, and Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glasses.

entry.title: Generalization in Learning: Eyring Formula and Predator-prey Model

author.name: S. V. Kozyrev, I. A. Lopatin, Alexander Pechen

entry.summary: The paper investigates generalization via a predator-prey dynamical model, giving biological and chemical interpretations of stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics and GANs, and shows the predator-prey model outperforms gradient descent on a polynomial function-recovery task. Thermodynamic arguments based on the Eyring formula are used to explain the grokking phenomenon.

entry.title: Learning from Points and Patches: A Pre-trained Hybrid Attention Transformer for Time Series Analysis

author.name: Peiwang Tang, Cheng HE, Yupeng Ye, Weitai Zhang, Qinghua Sun, Defu Lian

entry.summary: Proposes TimeHAT, a general-purpose pre-training framework for time series combining point-level and patch-level hybrid attention to handle heterogeneous patterns and variable sequence lengths. It addresses the what-to-learn and how-to-learn questions for transferable temporal representations, targeting web-service monitoring and related applications. Contributes to the growing time-series foundation-model literature.

entry.title: When Does Perturbation Consistency Add Information Beyond Softmax Confidence? Theory and Evidence for the Decision Consistency Framework

author.name: Amit Kalitaa, Moirangthem Tiken Singh

entry.summary: Empirically and theoretically evaluates whether perturbation-consistency scores (label stability, confidence deviation under six operators) add information beyond clean softmax confidence. Across 201 evaluations, the consistency score detected misclassifications worse than maximum softmax probability in every model family, at 8-15x compute, while finding specific niches where consistency helps. A careful negative-result-driven audit of a proposed uncertainty framework.

entry.title: Displacement Moments and Path-Terminal Separation in Brownian Interpolant Sampling

author.name: Zhong Han

entry.summary: This theory paper proves KL convergence guarantees for Euler sampling of Brownian stochastic interpolants for arbitrary Borel couplings, characterizing how displacement moments govern sampling error. It derives explicit bounds (e.g., O(N^-1) with four moments, C/N^2 terminal KL) and identifies via path decomposition what information about the source is discarded by Markov projection. Relevant to the theoretical foundations of diffusion/flow generative models.

entry.title: An Input Skip Can Reparameterize a VAE Without Improving the Generator

author.name: Kevin Lee

entry.summary: This analytic paper shows that adding an input skip to a Gaussian VAE can reduce reconstruction MSE while leaving the model's actual generative distribution unchanged, via an exact reparameterization. A controlled experiment demonstrates that minimizing MSE this way can worsen energy score and distribution estimates. It is a cautionary result about using reconstruction error as a proxy for generative quality.

entry.title: From Ethernet to Wi-Fi: Flow Feature Selection and Construction for Traffic Classification

author.name: Francisco Rau, Petia Georgieva, Carlos Herranz, I\~naki Val, Joaquin Perez

entry.summary: The paper proposes a five-stage feature selection and construction procedure enabling Wi-Fi flow classification with models trained only on Ethernet data, removing transport protocol identifiers and constructing normalized packet-size and temporal features using ns-3 simulations. This addresses a real cross-domain transfer problem in network traffic classification. Solid applied networking work with a systematic pipeline.

entry.title: Keeping Inference in the Radio: Design and Measurement of a Spiking Accelerator for mmWave ISAC Activity Recognition

author.name: Anthony S\'anchez, Rafael Ruiz, Jos\'e A. Belloch, Jes\'us O. Lacruz, Joerg Widmer

entry.summary: The paper explores spiking neural network accelerators for always-on human activity recognition from mmWave integrated sensing and communication channel estimates, targeting micro-Doppler classification on the public DISC dataset (IEEE 802.11ay). Using the open-source Spiker+ framework, the authors deploy SNNs on hardware that can stay powered while the rest of the system sleeps. This demonstrates energy-efficient edge inference for sensing-native wireless networks.

entry.title: Spectral Braids: A Topological Descriptor for Dynamic Directed Networks

author.name: Mehmet Emin Aktas, Esra Akbas

entry.summary: The paper proposes spectral braids, a novel descriptor for dynamic directed networks that tracks how complex eigenvalues of community-level transition matrices wind around each other over time, encoding the trajectory as a braid word from topology. This captures temporal dynamics of directed networks that static eigenvalue lists miss. It offers a creative topological lens for dynamic graph analysis.

entry.title: Spatial-Frequency Learning for Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy Image Enhancement

author.name: Hesong Li, Ying Fu, Ziqi Wu, Ruiwen Shao, Tao Zhang

entry.summary: This work proposes a spatial-frequency fusion network for STEM image enhancement that exploits periodic atomic arrangements in the frequency domain while restoring local atomic details in the spatial domain, addressing noise and blur from multiple degradations. Better STEM imaging directly supports materials discovery and characterization at sub-angstrom resolution. It is a domain-specific application with clear scientific utility.

entry.title: Frugal Handwritten Text Recognition for Sub-Saharan Civil-Status Registers: A Smartphone-to-Records Pipeline with CPU-Only Inference

author.name: Ousmane Hamadou, Jean Louis Kedieng Ebongue Fendji

entry.summary: The authors build a frugal pipeline for transcribing handwritten civil-status registers in Chad using smartphone capture and CPU-only inference, combining classical preprocessing with a fine-tuned Kraken recognizer, and release a corpus of 1,568 images with line-level transcriptions. The work targets settings lacking GPUs, connectivity, and digitization budgets, making historical records searchable. It demonstrates that meaningful OCR deployment is possible under severe resource constraints.

entry.title: SAGE: Saliency-Annealed Gated Encoder for Universal Vision Recognition

author.name: Le Yang, Yucheng Huang, Junyu Chen, Qi Dang, Xin Kong, Haifeng Huo, Qiang Zhao

entry.summary: SAGE is an enhanced ViT-Adapter backbone for dense prediction that explicitly exploits self-supervised ViT priors such as DINO-style CLS saliency, global context, and high-frequency detail through saliency-guided feature gating, dynamic multi-layer aggregation, and an annealing-based training paradigm. It aims to improve adaptation of self-supervised ViTs across vision recognition tasks. Solid backbone engineering work for the dense-prediction community.

entry.title: Efficient Remote Sensing Image-Text Retrieval via Interaction-Free Recall and Text-Guided Reranking

author.name: Xi Chen, Xu Chen, Xiamgyang Jia, Wei Wang, Xu Zhang, Zhenyuan Shun

entry.summary: A fast-then-fine retrieval framework for remote sensing image-text search that uses interaction-free multi-granular recall followed by parameter-free text-guided reranking via a Balanced Text-guided Interaction Block. It aims to avoid costly cross-modal interactions and large-scale vision-language adaptation.

entry.title: Physics Guided Diffusion Model Based Exposure Interpolation for High Dynamic Range Imaging

author.name: Zhengguo Li, Chaobing Zheng

entry.summary: The authors propose a physics-guided diffusion model to interpolate an intermediate-exposure image between two large-exposure-ratio SDR images, addressing brightness order reversal and ghosting artifacts in single-shot HDR imaging. A physics-driven component provides the initial interpolation while a diffusion component generates residual high-frequency detail. This targets a concrete artifact problem in practical HDR pipelines.

entry.title: TRUCO: A Scalable Lock-Free Algorithm for Parallel Contour Extraction

author.name: Rafael Munoz-Salinas, Francisco J. Romero-Ramirez, Manuel J. Marin-Jimenez

entry.summary: TRUCO is a lock-free parallel algorithm for converting binary masks to geometric contours, avoiding the sequential bottleneck of Suzuki-Abe and the complexity of tile stitching or heavy synchronization. It exploits multi-core CPUs for high-resolution imaging pipelines. This is a solid systems/algorithmic contribution to an often-overlooked pipeline step.

entry.title: SLICE-CiM: Selective Layer-wise Inference Control Engine with Confidence-Based Early Exit for SRAM based Digital Compute-in-Memory

author.name: Pratham Sharma, Mohd Faisal Khan, Santosh Kumar Vishvakarma

entry.summary: SLICE-CiM presents four synthesizable peripheral controller blocks for digital SRAM compute-in-memory macros, including confidence-based early exit and bit-slice control, to reduce energy waste from over-activation, unnecessary accumulation, and precision-transition stalls. The design is implemented in TSMC 65nm CMOS at 335 MHz with small area overhead.

entry.title: Structure-Actuation Co-Design of All-Electric Heavy-Duty Robotic Manipulators

author.name: Mohammad Bahari, Amir Hossein Barjini, Jouni Mattila

entry.summary: A mixed discrete-continuous bilevel multiobjective optimization framework co-designs the geometry and actuation of all-electric heavy-duty manipulators, coordinating motor, gearbox, and screw selection with robot geometry until a mass-consistent fixed point. Evaluation on a full-pose SE(3) benchmark with a 100-kg payload yields feasible nondominated designs meeting all constraints.

entry.title: An Incremental Knowledge-Graph Learner Digital Twin for Evidence-Grounded Early Warning

author.name: Ngoc Luyen Le, Marie-H\'el\`ene Abel, Bertrand Laforge

entry.summary: This work introduces a Learner Digital Twin implemented as an incremental knowledge graph that updates at temporal checkpoints by replaying learning traces, serving both as a feature-extraction and explanation-grounding substrate for early-warning models of at-risk students. It aims to make risk alerts inspectable by linking them to concrete learning evidence.

entry.title: PolicyMediator: Multi-Regional Policy Learning through Mediation Agents with Evolving Skills in OPC Ecosystems

author.name: Jie Li, Bin Guo, Georgina Curto, Zikang Liu, Mengqi Chen, yu li

entry.summary: PolicyMediator studies cross-regional policy coordination for one-person companies run via LLM-based agents, using mediation agents with evolving skills to couple policy learning with changing perceptions of mobile entrepreneurs across Chinese regions. It integrates consensus formation with policy learning so cognitive updates feed back into optimization. It is an unusual agent-based policy-simulation contribution at the intersection of multi-agent systems and computational social science.

entry.title: Counterfactual Profile Perturbations for Recommendation Explanations: A Reproducibility Study

author.name: Meysam Varasteh, Elizabeth McKinnie, Robin Burke

entry.summary: This reproducibility study re-examines LXR, a counterfactual explanation technique for recommender systems that finds minimal profile perturbations causing the top recommendation to change. The authors extend the original study to non-top-ranked items, compare against popularity and latent-similarity baselines, and probe when the technique remains effective.

entry.title: MM-Net: A Multimodal Multi-Task Network for Sleep Staging and Sleep Apnea Assessment After Ischemic Stroke

author.name: Md Wahiduzzaman Suva, Esm E Moula Chowdhury Abha, Md Imtiaj Alam Sajin, Md Iftekharul Mobin, Jia Uddin

entry.summary: Proposes MM-Net, a multimodal multi-task framework for joint sleep staging and sleep apnea assessment in post-stroke polysomnography, fusing sleep-adapted EEG-EOG representations with engineered neural descriptors. It addresses train/test embedding inconsistency in pretrained EEG encoders via cross-fitting and ridge-based alignment.

entry.title: An Algebra of Transformers

author.name: Yong Wang, Zhiyan Wang, Hexiao Kang

entry.summary: This paper develops an algebra for reasoning about transformers based on functional decomposition, with sequential and parallel composition, recursion, and abstraction as operators. It claims to be the first logical modeling of transformers and aims to support correctness verification of transformer-based applications. This matters for formal methods applied to neural architectures.

entry.title: Property-Based Testing for Robust Softmax and Cross-Entropy

author.name: Muhammad Maaz

entry.summary: Uses property-based testing in Hypothesis to reproduce recently identified numerical issues in softmax and cross-entropy implementations common to PyTorch and JAX, and discovers an additional failing edge case. The paper proposes a more robust softmax implementation that also supports causal attention masking. Demonstrates property-based testing as a practical tool for hardening core ML library numerics.

entry.title: Normative Deviation Modeling for EEG-based Depression Detection

author.name: Wan Jiang, Jingqi Cheng, Hui Zhang, Xu Zhao, Xiaojing Chen, Shengeng Tang, Jingjing Wu, Richang Hong

entry.summary: The paper trains structural and distributional reference models on healthy control EEG recordings to characterize departures from healthy patterns, then uses these normative deviations for depression (MDD) detection across heterogeneous data sources. Two diagnostic approaches incorporate deviations at different representation levels, addressing individual variability and acquisition differences. This supports web-enabled mental health screening.

entry.title: Online Interval Selection with Binary Predictions: Optimal Consistency and a Continuous Robustness Tradeoff

author.name: Zhong Han

entry.summary: This paper studies online interval selection with binary predictions under a predictions-with-guards model where accepted requests may be revoked but rejected ones cannot be recovered. It establishes an optimal consistency constant of (3+sqrt5)/2 under finite strict robustness, proves a continuous lower bound, and provides a deterministic algorithm achieving the optimum with exact robustness. This is a refined learning-augmented algorithms result with tight guarantees.

entry.title: Frankly Speaking: The Company Election Integrity Keeps in Congressional Communication

author.name: Michael A. Robinette, Christina Barsky, Amanda D. Clark, Helen Flannery, Juniper Lovato

entry.summary: Using diachronic word embeddings over 10,420 congressional e-newsletters from 2010 to 2025, this paper measures how Democrats and Republicans increasingly ascribe divergent meanings to election terms such as integrity, security, and fraud. It shows polarization operates through changing semantic context of the same words rather than different vocabulary. This applies NLP methods to quantify political semantic drift on a consequential topic.

entry.title: Structured Maps for Landmark-Based Route Instructions with LLMs

author.name: Mifu Matsumoto, Yuki Nakanishi, Tomoya Hashiguchi, Hiroaki Ohshima

entry.summary: Proposes encoding map geometry as structured SVG-like text so LLMs can perform landmark selection for route instruction generation, maintaining geometric alignment with rendered map images. Creates a new dataset from human-written route descriptions and OpenStreetMap data, evaluating landmark selection at turns and destinations. Bridges map data representation with LLM spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Game-Theoretic Solvers with Bayesian Opponent Modeling and Moral Rhetoric Framing for GLEE

author.name: Hayden Arnold

entry.summary: This is a competition system report describing an agent for the GLEE bargaining, negotiation, and persuasion games that combines classical game-theoretic solvers (Rubinstein bargaining, Faratin concession, Kamenica-Gentzkow disclosure), an online Bayesian opponent-archetype estimator, and an LLM that generates messages. A Thompson sampling bandit selects among moral-framing strategies. It is a solid hybrid classical-LLM agent design demonstrated in live competition against human and AI opponents.

entry.title: FORESEE-MS: Toward Prospective Spatial Forecasting of Future Multiple Sclerosis Lesions from Baseline FLAIR MRI

author.name: Maryam Akhavan Aghdam, Sudip Mittal, Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz, Shahram Rahimi

entry.summary: FORESEE-MS shifts MS lesion analysis from retrospective detection to prospective forecasting of where future lesions will form, using an evaluation protocol with fold-specific population-prior atlases, voxel-level AUROC/AUPRC, and patient-localized Recall@Top-K metrics. Five deep learning models were compared via 5-fold cross-validation on 39 subjects from MSSEG-2. Prospective lesion-risk mapping could eventually aid clinical monitoring, though the cohort is small.

entry.title: CVBL-CCTV-Face Dataset for Real-World Face Enhancement and Recognition in Surveillance

author.name: Manish Das, Ajay Kumar Yadav, Shiv Ram Dubey, Satish Kumar Singh

entry.summary: Introduces a real-world unpaired dataset of low-quality CCTV face captures paired with controlled high-quality references, plus a modular system for face super-resolution and identity recognition in surveillance. The dataset targets common degradations like blur, noise, and occlusion.

entry.title: Drop the Details, Get the Gist: Dynamic Conceptual Representation for Video Recognition

author.name: Ryoya Yoshiyama, Bowen Wang, Yuta Nakashima

entry.summary: Extends Concept Bottleneck Models to procedural video understanding by representing a multi-step video as a temporal sequence of segment-level concept score vectors fed to a Transformer encoder. It also estimates per-concept contributions for interpretability.

entry.title: Multibranch Ensemble Head in Vision Foundation Models for Efficient Cucumber Phenological Stage Classification

author.name: Kostiantyn Khabarlak

entry.summary: This paper proposes a multibranch ensemble head for adapting self-supervised vision foundation models like DINOv2 to small, domain-shifted datasets, stochastically sampling low- and high-capacity branches during training and averaging them at inference. It is applied to cucumber phenological stage classification for precision agriculture, improving accuracy with negligible inference overhead. The work addresses the common practical challenge of efficient adaptation under data scarcity.

entry.title: HDVS: semi-supervised semantic segmentation via heterogeneous dual-branch voting supervision

author.name: Yongqi Shan, Yunzhi Zhuge, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: HDVS is a semi-supervised semantic segmentation framework using heterogeneous dual branches with voting supervision to improve pseudo-label reliability and prevent error accumulation during co-training. It targets the common failure mode where noisy pseudo-labels from one branch degrade the other. The approach addresses a recognized weakness in cross-supervision methods.

entry.title: Physiology-Informed Audio Quality and Listening Effort Estimation

author.name: Niall McGuire, Dimitra Emmanouilidou

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether consumer-grade neurophysiological devices can complement subjective MOS scoring for audio quality, providing objective, implicit, continuous listener signals. It examines population-level quality trends and per-listener calibration for tracking individual perception and listening effort.

entry.title: Electric-Field Induction Motor with Discrete Circuit Elements and Improved Rotor Dynamics

author.name: Alex S. Miller, Jeffrey H. Lang

entry.summary: This paper develops a rotor for electric-field induction motors constructed from discrete circuit components rather than a single continuum material, expanding design freedom in resistivity, permittivity, and circuitry. Electric-field machines are attractive for minimal mass, vacuum, and high-temperature applications including nanoscale and biological settings. It is a hardware/mechatronics contribution rather than an AI one.

entry.title: TCM-DiagCommit: A TCM-SD-Derived Benchmark for Evidence-Conditioned Syndrome Selection and Commitment

author.name: Erwei Hou, Yue Hu

entry.summary: TCM-DiagCommit converts 1,834 Traditional Chinese Medicine cases into 23,842 task rows over 148 syndrome labels to test dynamic, evidence-conditioned diagnosis rather than static final-label selection. It probes whether models distinguish near-neighbor syndromes, update beliefs as evidence is revealed, and know when to commit under uncertainty. It fills a niche in sequential clinical decision benchmarking.

entry.title: HeteGCD: Statistics-Aware Dual-Prototype Learning for Generalized Category Discovery on Heterophilous Graphs

author.name: Xuanzhi Xi, Tongze Zhang, Zhili Qin, Yulin Tao, Hongliang Wang, Zhong Zhang, Qinli Yang, Junming Shao

entry.summary: Addresses generalized category discovery on heterophilous graphs, where homophily-based inductive biases used by existing graph GCD methods are ill-suited. HeteGCD uses statistics-aware dual-prototype learning to select and fuse diverse neighborhood signals without relying on label supervision for prototype construction.

entry.title: Deep Bayesian Approaches for Interpretable Nonlinear Structural System Identification

author.name: Wei Liu, Konstantinos Vlachas, Eleni Chatzi

entry.summary: A tutorial introducing deep Bayesian filtering for nonlinear structural system identification, embedding learnable representations in probabilistic state-space models to identify unknown dynamics while retaining physical structure and uncertainty quantification. Aimed at engineering diagnostics and prognostics communities. Tutorials score lower on novelty but can have outsized educational impact in bridging ML and engineering.

entry.title: REGLAT at ArGuard Shared Tasks: An Ensemble-Based Model Integrating NER for Harmful Content Detection in Arabic

author.name: Ahmed M. Fetouh, Mariam Labib, Nsrin Ashraf, Omer Dawood, Hamada Nayel

entry.summary: Describes a shared-task system for classifying Arabic user prompts into seven harmful-content categories, using GLiNER to extract harm-related entities that are appended to the text before a fine-tuned MARBERT classifier. Achieved macro-F1 of 0.886 and accuracy of 0.897 on the ArGuard 2026 development set. A practical system paper addressing dialectal variation and semantic overlap between harm categories.

entry.title: Subspace Clifford Networks

author.name: Zhongping Ji

entry.summary: Subspace Clifford Networks replace global cyclic channel-rolling operations with grouped low-dimensional subspace interactions, computing wedge coordinates and gated products within small groups sandwiched between 1x1 projections. This reduces intermediate feature expansion while enabling cross-group channel mixing. It is an architectural contribution to efficient feature interaction design.

entry.title: Enhancing Deep Learning Model Performance through Data Generation Strategies: Classification of Olive Tree Diseases

author.name: Hicham El Akhal, Abderrahim Waga, Aissa Ben Yahya, Abdelbaki El Belrhiti El Alaoui

entry.summary: The paper addresses class imbalance and data scarcity in olive tree disease classification using augmentation, CutMix, MixUp, and DCGAN-generated synthetic images across three data-expansion scenarios. It demonstrates that carefully structured data generation improves plant-disease diagnosis performance.

entry.title: Curriculum-Driven Deep Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Far-Range Rocket Landing

author.name: Atin Chowdhury, Piyush Joshi

entry.summary: The paper presents a curriculum-driven deep reinforcement learning framework for reusable-launch-vehicle landings, using a three-stage curriculum and critic warm-up to handle far-range navigation plus precision landing under nonlinear dynamics and uncertainty. It addresses limitations of flat RL training and oversimplified initial conditions common in prior work. Its value lies in demonstrating domain randomization and curriculum techniques in a demanding aerospace control setting.

entry.title: Holomorphic Cauchy Networks for Efficient Stationary Tail Computation in High-Dimensional Reflected Brownian Motions

author.name: Kehan Wang

entry.summary: Develops Holomorphic Cauchy Networks for computing stationary tails of high-dimensional reflected Brownian motions, using complex-valued rational subnetworks that enforce holomorphicity by construction and eliminate costly sampled Cauchy-Riemann penalties. The paper establishes approximation guarantees including simultaneous value and derivative approximation. A specialized but theoretically rich application of neural networks to stochastic processes.

entry.title: Quantum Evolution Kernel for Node-Attributed Graphs

author.name: Manuel Padovani, Alessandra Di Pierro, Claudia Daffara
