entry.summary: The authors extend Pasqal's quantum evolution kernel to node-attributed graphs via a three-level quantum state feature encoding, demonstrating digit recognition on simulated neutral-atom quantum hardware using the Pulser library. The method slightly outperforms classical baselines on the small-scale test. An early-stage quantum machine learning prototype constrained by simulation size.

entry.title: A note on data-efficient finetuning of vision foundation models

author.name: Niclas Hergenr\"other, Antonio Orvieto

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates Visual Prompting (VP) and alternative efficient fine-tuning methods for adapting vision foundation models, including newer architecture families like Mamba, using pipelines such as AutoVP. It aims to map progress, challenges, and opportunities in resource-limited fine-tuning. It is an empirical benchmarking note rather than a new method.

entry.title: GarmentSegAgent: Autonomous Garment Segmentation for Web Fashion Images via Textual Self-Refinement

author.name: Jia Chen, Chao Huang, Xinrong Hu, Mingdi Huang, Ruyang Zhao, Jun Bai

entry.summary: GarmentSegAgent is an autonomous pipeline for garment segmentation in heterogeneous web fashion images, combining semantic planning, spatial execution, and visual evaluation through iterative textual self-refinement. Its CAST mechanism links visual error attribution to targeted optimization of segmentation instructions, removing the need for human spatial prompts. It is a competent agentic application for e-commerce vision tasks.

entry.title: Readout and Operating-Point Sensitivity in Event-Stream Candidate Selection

author.name: Yifan Shuai

entry.summary: This paper evaluates event-camera representations for event-triggered recording on DailyDVS-200 clips with participant-disjoint splits, examining how encoder scale, accumulation duration, and threshold calibration affect target capture versus false triggers. A post-review extension adds supervised CNN encoders and multi-seed, multi-partition calibration sensitivity analysis.

entry.title: TopoField: Technical Report for ECCV 2026 SceneFun3D Challenge

author.name: Zhiwei Chen, Zhiheng Fu, Zixu Li, Mingyu Zhang, Jiale Huang, Yupeng Hu

entry.summary: TopoField addresses the field-to-instance gap in functional segmentation of indoor point clouds by converting test-time-augmented semantic predictions into a consensus field, deterministically decoding instance candidates, and ranking them class-aware. The approach won/placed in the ECCV 2026 SceneFun3D challenge setting for locating small interactive parts like knobs and sockets. It is a solid challenge-focused systems contribution.

entry.title: Quantity has a quality of its own

author.name: djbinder

entry.summary: An essay arguing that even if recursive self-improvement stalls short of superintelligence, vast numbers of near-human-level AI agents could themselves be destabilizing or catastrophic, so arguments against RSI provide little consolation. It suggests pacing RSI may be desirable but insufficient as a risk-reduction strategy.

entry.title: Are Persona Features Coherent?

author.name: Koby Lewis

entry.summary: A conceptual LessWrong post questioning whether persona features in mechanistic interpretability research are a coherent concept, noting that existing persona-related work does not clearly distinguish a deception feature from a deceptive persona feature. The author, referencing the Persona Selection Model, asks what distinguishes a representation of a character attribute from the behavior or abstract concept itself, and sketches possible framings for resolving this.

entry.title: Beyond Greenwashing: Algorithmic Resilience and the Non-Linear Governance Premium in Sovereign Capital Flows

author.name: Sourav Bose, Taoufik Bouraoui

entry.summary: Using a forward-chained global panel of 147 sovereign entities (2010-2024), this paper shows sovereign FDI tail-risk transmission is non-linear, with gradient boosting cutting forecast errors over 39% versus L1-regularized baselines during extreme events. Dual interpretability frameworks map discrete threshold effects of institutional quality on capital flows. The AI content is applied ML for macro-finance rather than core AI research.

entry.title: A Harness Reducing over-Defensive Writing in Agents by Isolating Objections

author.name: Xiaochen Chang

entry.summary: Identifies over-defensive writing in LLM agents expanding reports, where the model introduces stronger claims than the source and then disclaims them, hypothesizing it stems from writing against an imagined adversarial reviewer. Proposes a harness that separates reviewer, filter, and writer roles so the writer sees only filter-selected problems in an isolated context. Evaluated on 25 business-project drafts.

entry.title: Anthropic Versus Anthropic

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's commentary assessing Anthropic's record, weighing its safety culture, governance structure, and strong models against disappointing behaviors, in the context of ongoing discussion of a leaked draft bill. The piece argues views of Anthropic depend on whether one thinks its approach can solve problems that may exceed operational excellence.

entry.title: A Smart Instant Book Filter Model based on Dual-Objective Optimization

author.name: Yi Hou, Li Fan, Huizhong Duan

entry.summary: The paper presents a dual-objective optimization model for an instant-book filter in online hospitality marketplaces, aimed at reducing booking rejections and response delays by predicting qualified guests for hosts. It extends prior instant-book functionality to address residual friction in request-to-book flows.

entry.title: SFE-O: An Ontology for Knowledge-Grounded AI in Supercritical CO$_2$ Biomass Extraction and Fractionation

author.name: Thomas Pallet (CRAN, LIFIA, Mgib), Mario Lezoche (CRAN, LS2N - {\'e}quipe CPS3, LS2N), Gianpaolo Leone (ENEA), Daniele Pizzichini (ENEA), Diego Torres (LIFIA, UNQ), Herv{\'e} Panetto (CRAN), M{\'e}lanie Glibusic (Mgib)

entry.summary: SFE-O is a modular OWL 2 ontology for supercritical CO2 biomass extraction, structured around Biomass, Process, and Product dimensions with explicit process topology and parameter provenance. It aims to unify heterogeneous knowledge from technical reports, engineering models, databases, and expert practice to support knowledge-grounded AI.

entry.title: Structured Time-Frequency Representation for Channel Prediction

author.name: Ning Yang, Yuming Xian, Tong Li, Ning Gao, Haijun Zhang

entry.summary: FAR-CSI introduces an FDD-aware representation for wireless channel-state-information forecasting within a joint temporal and operating-band positional field, so that historical uplink observations and future downlink targets occupy structured, segregated regions for a pretrained predictor. This addresses channel aging in high-mobility systems where both time extrapolation and cross-band inference are needed. It is a specialized wireless-domain contribution with modest broader AI relevance.

entry.title: Interpretable Deep Learning Models for Breast Cancer Diagnosis Using Medical Imaging

author.name: Sami Alnawali, Muhammad Atif Saeed, Abdul Hadi, Azka Atiq, Akhtar Jamil, Ahmad Din

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks ten ImageNet-pretrained architectures for benign-versus-malignant classification on the BreakHis histopathology dataset with patient-level splits, applying Grad-CAM, LIME, Integrated Gradients, and LRP for explanations. DenseNet121 achieves 99.4% accuracy and 0.999 AUC, with explanations highlighting diagnostically relevant nuclei-rich regions. This matters for clinically oriented, interpretable cancer diagnosis.

entry.title: SpecLST: Spectral-Enhanced Long-Short Term Spatio-Temporal Multimodal Modeling for Traffic Forecasting

author.name: Kenan Kang, Matthew M. Y. Kuo, Weihua Li

entry.summary: Proposes SpecLST, a traffic forecasting framework using FFT-based frequency-domain encoding to efficiently capture multi-week historical dependencies and fuse exogenous modalities like weather and incidents. It addresses memory bottlenecks of long sequences in spatio-temporal models. A competent but incremental architecture paper in a crowded traffic forecasting field.

entry.title: Regression Functions as Fields on Covariate Space: Evolution Equations, the Hessian, and Identification

author.name: Nobuaki Tanaka

entry.summary: This theoretical paper treats a regression function as a field on covariate space and derives a second-order evolution equation governing how it changes as covariates diffuse and outcomes evolve, with a Hessian-trace diffusion term, a time-reversed drift transport term, and a conditional-mean source term. This provides new structure for understanding regression dynamics, potentially linking to identification questions. It is a single-author mathematical statistics contribution.

entry.title: Progressively Refining SAM for Accurate Phytoplankton Segmentation

author.name: Jialin Li, Jinkun Jiang, Yuezun Li, Junyu Dong

entry.summary: PhySeg adapts the Segment Anything Model to phytoplankton segmentation with a lightweight refinement module that progressively restores fine-grained details via multi-scale feature fusion, and contributes a manually annotated instance-mask dataset. Accurate segmentation supports ecological monitoring where pixel-level annotations are scarce. A modest but useful domain application with a released resource.

entry.title: Evaluation-Guided Demonstration Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Policies: The Winning Entry in the MetaFine Open Competition

author.name: Lifan Zheng, Guotao Chen, Zhenyang Li, Shujie Cui, Qiang Huang, Fan Liu

entry.summary: A competition report describing fine-tuned pi0.5 VLA policies for five manipulation tasks, using local evaluation to expose recurring failure modes and refining demonstrations with expert continuations from states the policy reached. The submission ranked first overall in the MetaFine Open Competition with a score of 96.66.

entry.title: Zhengrong-Spatial-Aware 1.0: Advancing 3D Multimodal Intelligence

author.name: Yu Zhang, Xiaogang Wang, Yuhang Cheng, Jingrui Li, Wenbo Chen

entry.summary: This technical report describes two end-to-end pipelines for 3D-aware visual question answering: fine-tuning HiSpatial-3B with metric-scale 3D point maps and adapting Qwen3-VL via memory-efficient QLoRA, along with a complete engineering stack for data conversion, training, inference, and evaluation. HiSpatial adaptation raises accuracy on the target spatial benchmark from 1.73% to 79.89%. It is a practical adaptation study rather than a new architecture.

entry.title: A 2-DOF MultiBody Track Joint for Race Car Optimization

author.name: Srikanth Sivaramakrishnan, Behzad Danaei, Adwait Verulkar, Ryan Trinter

entry.summary: TrackJoint is a Modelica multibody component that represents an arbitrary fitted 3D road surface as a two-degree-of-freedom joint parameterized by arc-length distance and lateral offset. It closes the road constraint via d'Alembert's principle without Lagrange multipliers, enabling efficient race-car simulation and optimization on any circuit.

entry.title: Time for automated decision forecasting?

author.name: Jordan Arel

entry.summary: A proposal for automated decision forecasters (ADF): systems that take a user's goal and candidate options, then produce quantitative forecasts of how likely each option is to achieve the goal, building on recent AI superforecasting results. The author argues the capability is now commercially available and sketches use cases and design considerations.

entry.title: Notes on “We’re in Triage Mode for AI Safety” by Miles Brundage

author.name: Chris_Leong

entry.summary: Reading notes by Chris_Leong on Miles Brundage's essay arguing that AI safety and governance are in triage mode: at best, roughly 80 percent of risks will be mitigated with 20 percent of the effort that slower progress would have allowed, and several very bad but sub-worst-case outcomes (unjust economic transition, AI-enabled terrorism, or stable totalitarianism) will likely not be fully avoided. The notes contextualize the piece within the BlueDot governance curriculum and Brundage's background as a former OpenAI policy advisor.

entry.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations

author.name: Henrique Schechter Vera, Sahil Dua, Jovan Andonov, Sara Smoot, Sebastian Russo, Ivan Llanos, Max Matveev, Jae Hyeon Yoo, Kat Black, Shih-Cheng Huang, Josiah Aklilu, Maarten Grootendorst, Omar Sanseviero, Chandramouli Amarnath, Ian Ballantyne, Zhe Li, Daniel Salz, Ibrahim Alabdulmohsin, Ilya Philippov, Kristen Quan, Glenn Cameron, Edouard Yvinec, Luciano Martins, Doug Reid, Sindhu Raghuram Panyam, Weiyi Wang, Hengxuan Ying, Madhuri Shanbhogue, Tanmaya Dabral, Shanfeng Zhang, Juyeong Ji, Renjie Wu, Joe Zou, Xu Chen, Yunan Zhang, Yu-Hui Chen, Matthew Soulanille, Vinod Mamillapalli, Yi-Chun Kuo, Wai Hon Law, Matt Kreileder, Alice Zheng, Suril Shah, Mogan Shieh, Pooja Consul, Alberto Montes, Andreas Hess, Andres Sevilla, Babak Samari, Brendan McCloskey, Brian Potetz, Daniel Cer, Georgios Kathareios, Gustavo Hern\'andez \'Abrego, Hesen Zhang, Ji Ma, Jiaxing Wu, Keegan Mosley, Paul Suganthan, Rui Meng, Shen Gao, Shengcao Cao, Yi-Ting Chen, Yichang Chen, Zhongli Ding, Kendra Byrne, Cormac Brick, Olivier Lacombe, Qin Yin, Tris Warkentin, Armand Joulin, Tom Duerig, Mojtaba Seyedhosseini

entry.summary: EmbeddingGemma 2 is an open multimodal embedding model from Google that natively represents text, images, audio, and video in a unified embedding space, using simplified per-layer embeddings and a multi-stage curriculum. It establishes a new Pareto frontier on embedding benchmarks, outperforming specialist models and models 2-12x larger, while supporting selective modality loading and adjustable vision token budgets for resource-constrained deployment. Note: this model reached general availability earlier in October 2026, so this paper is the technical report accompanying an existing release rather than a brand-new launch.

entry.title: AK_QMUL at ArGuard Shared Tasks: A Single Fine-Tuned JAIS for Arabic Harmful-Prompt Detection

author.name: Ali Khairallah, Arkaitz Zubiaga

entry.summary: This system paper describes AK_QMUL's first-place submissions to the ArGuard-2026 shared tasks on Arabic harmful-prompt detection, using a single JAIS-6.7B backbone fine-tuned with 4-bit QLoRA and a classification head. For the binary safe/unsafe task they factor labels by dialect register and augment with AraSafe data; for the seven-way harm-domain task they ensemble five seeds. Both submissions ranked first with macro-F1 of 0.984 and 0.790.

entry.title: uTHCD-C: A Corruption-Robustness Benchmark for Tamil Handwritten Character Recognition

author.name: Preethi S, Meeradevi T, Arun Prakash A

entry.summary: uTHCD-C establishes a corruption-robustness benchmark for Tamil handwritten character recognition with ten corruption types (including a handwriting-specific stroke-thinning corruption) at five severity levels, evaluating nine CNN and transformer architectures with writer-independent testing and mCE metrics.

entry.title: A Singularity Avoiding Track Model for Race Car Optimization

author.name: Adwait Verulkar, Behzad Danaei, Srikanth Sivaramakrishnan, Ryan Trinter

entry.summary: The paper presents a pipeline converting measured racetrack point clouds into a closed, C4-differentiable 3D Monge-patch surface for Modelica race-car optimization. It anchors the parameterization on the minimum-curvature line to avoid normal crossing singularities on tight corners.

entry.title: Scattered thoughts on how doing math feels these days

author.name: dynomight

entry.summary: A personal time-capsule essay by dynomight describing how AI went from toy to near-indispensable for real mathematics between 2024 and 2026, estimating roughly 50% personal productivity gain despite AI sometimes doing in minutes what would take the author hours. It reflects on why felt productivity lags apparent capability, since research involves steps AI does not yet accelerate.

entry.title: What happens with steering vectors to remove biases?

author.name: Avani Gupta

entry.summary: The author, who previously published on concept distillation at NeurIPS 2023, applies the ActAdd steering method to debias a classifier in a Colored-MNIST setting where the model associates digits with spurious colors. Early results and discussion explore whether steering activations away from a learned color direction recovers test accuracy.

entry.title: scPyviewer: a Python-native interactive viewer from AnnData single-cell data

author.name: Hao Xuan, Yu Huang, Jiang Bian, Xiangtao Liu

entry.summary: scPyviewer is a lightweight, Python-native web viewer for AnnData single-cell objects, filling a gap where interactive viewers required R/Seurat and Python users had to convert data or share notebooks. It reproduces incumbent interaction patterns with a scriptable Python API. This is laboratory infrastructure rather than novel AI research.

entry.title: Evaluating Priority Dispatch for Premium Membership in On-demand Taxi-sharing

author.name: Nozomi Yamamoto, Hiroki Sakaji, Itsuki Noda

entry.summary: The paper evaluates dispatch-level mechanisms for premium memberships in on-demand taxi-sharing using SUMO simulations, comparing deadline shortening with and without dedicated premium vehicles under three demand scenarios. It finds the suitable priority mechanism depends on operating conditions and premium-user ratio. This matters as applied operations research for mobility services.

entry.title: A Lightweight Attention-Based CNN with Saliency-Map Interpretability for Skin Cancer Detection

author.name: Sanjana Islam Kasfia, Md. Ismiel Hossen Abir, AKM Bahalul Haque, Abir Mahmud Shahariar

entry.summary: The paper presents a lightweight attention-based CNN for binary classification of skin lesions, integrating channel attention with saliency-map interpretability at low computational cost. It achieves 87 percent accuracy on a publicly available dataset of about 3,300 dermoscopic images with balanced class weighting.

entry.title: Real-Time Smart Retail Analytics through Fog Computing using the RetailLightNet Lightweight Model

author.name: Mayank Atreya, Navin Chhibber, Shilpa Ajay, R Loshini, K Anitha

entry.summary: This work proposes RetailLightNet, an ultra-lightweight deep learning model for edge devices performing real-time retail video analytics such as customer tracking and shelf inventory. The fog-based deployment addresses cloud latency, privacy, and bandwidth limitations of transmitting raw video.

entry.title: Solving for the Necessity of Phenomenal Consciousness

author.name: Marek Kowalski

entry.summary: A long-form philosophical essay arguing for more relentless attempts to solve the hard problem of consciousness, especially regarding selfhood, using evolutionary reasoning about why recurrent structures like the camera eye were favored. It explicitly frames biological consciousness as the only testable analog for thinking about digital minds.

entry.title: A dead man's switch for scheming AIs

author.name: Carlos Guerrero Alvarez

entry.summary: Proposes a deterrence mechanism inspired by the folk theorem: guarantee that if scheming AIs eliminate humanity, they will be shut down, so that even goal-directed schemers behave well as long as they act as if shutdown matters. The post motivates the idea via warning-shot incidents and situates it as complementary to alignment and control techniques.

entry.title: Directional Statistics on Circles and Spheres: A New Angle on Data

author.name: Siddhesh Kulkarni

entry.summary: This is a tutorial-style article introducing circular and axial averages, directional variability, and probability models on circles and spheres, motivated by examples like compass bearings, wind observations, and diffusion-MRI orientations. Its guiding principle is to match statistical methods to the geometry and symmetries of the data.

entry.title: TimeLineXR: An Interactive Exploration of Time in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Nidham Tekaya, Markus Passecker, Matthias Zeppelzauer

entry.summary: TimeLineXR is an interactive demonstration that visualizes the temporal manifold VLMs encode in their embedding spaces, letting users upload images and see them placed on a color-coded 3D time axis in a WebXR scene. It builds on prior quantitative findings that VLMs encode time along a low-dimensional non-linear manifold. The contribution is visualization/exploration tooling rather than new modeling.

entry.title: How to manage a small custom model with limited data at deployment? Delexicalization to rescue.

author.name: Avani Gupta

entry.summary: A practitioner account of fine-tuning a content moderation model with very limited custom-category data, where the model failed on out-of-domain entities such as alternate country names and regional terms. The author proposes delexicalization as a remedy for entity-related robustness failures in small custom classifiers.

entry.title: Notes on “We’re in Triage Mode for AI Safety” by Miles Brundage

author.name: Chris_Leong

entry.summary: Study notes on Miles Brundage's essay arguing that AI safety is in triage mode, where even strong efforts will mitigate only roughly 80% of risks and bad-but-not-worst-case outcomes such as unjust transitions and AI-enabled authoritarianism are likely. The author contextualizes Brundage's background and laments the reading being made optional in a governance course.

entry.title: Emotion is Perception with Pull

author.name: Joseph Gardner

entry.summary: A speculative LessWrong essay proposing an identity theory of emotion: emotion is a perceptual-like representation that describes and directs behavior, constructed in integrative brain regions such as the ventromedial prefrontal cortex, anterior cingulate cortex, and anterior insula. The author argues this explains patient Elliot's combined loss of function and feeling, and claims related accounts such as Lisa Feldman Barrett's stop short of making the identity claim. The relevance to AI is indirect, mostly via theories of agentic steering and conscious motivation.

entry.title: Crop Yield Prediction Using Regression Models: A Comparative Evaluation of Model Performance

author.name: Saptak Das, Arijit Sarkar, Soumik Neogi, Suborno Naskar

entry.summary: This study compares five classical regression models (linear, ridge, lasso, decision tree, random forest) for crop-yield prediction on a one-million-observation dataset with standard preprocessing and splits. This matters modestly for agricultural planning but applies well-established techniques.

entry.title: Comments on the BlueDot Strategy Course

author.name: Chris_Leong

entry.summary: Brief commentary critiquing how the BlueDot AI safety strategy course uses the term power concentration, including its inclusion of rogue AI under that pathway, noting this is idiosyncratic relative to broader community usage. The author points out that proponents of the two concerns often favor opposite interventions.

entry.title: Have LLMs passed the Turing test?

author.name: EJIKAGORAMEN

entry.summary: A LessWrong discussion post arguing that no publicly available LLM has unambiguously passed a strong form of the Turing test, pointing to the absence of fully undetectable agent-generated spam, reliable author-style mimicry, and other expected consequences. The author speculates that a truly duplicitous model arriving earlier would have triggered an internet-spam crisis that could have strengthened AI safety awareness and governance.

entry.title: How to find a philanthropic advisor who cares about cost-effectiveness

author.name: jackultraphil

entry.summary: Announces a free advisor-matching tool aimed at prospective Anthropic employees who may become wealthy through the company's IPO, arguing they will soon need philanthropic advice and should choose evidence-first, cost-effectiveness-minded advisors. It references the S-1 filing published October 26, 2026.

entry.title: Xenobiology: Could life have evolved via an alternative route?

author.name: Byron Lee

entry.summary: Announcement of a moderated OtherMinds lab discussion on alternative biochemistry, centered on three papers about intrinsically disordered proteins, tardigrade desiccation survival, and directed evolution of enzymes forming carbon-silicon bonds. It asks whether life could arise via non-standard molecular routes.

entry.title: Integrated Design and Reproducible Feasibility Analysis of a Four-Wheel Rover with Packet-Commanded Imaging, LiDAR Ranging, and Learning-Assisted Target Recognition

author.name: Sabik Bin Sultan, Shafi Bin Sultan, Safwan Sadad, Aranya Abeer Khan Prapya, Maria Sultan

entry.summary: This paper documents an integrated, reproducible design and feasibility analysis for a four-wheel educational rover built for the 2027 NASA Human Exploration Rover Challenge high-school division, covering mobility, electrical constraints, and a Raspberry Pi-based sensing subsystem. It is primarily an engineering design report for a student competition vehicle.

entry.title: March Against AI Extinction

author.name: kieuk

entry.summary: An announcement for a PauseAI UK march in London on 21 November 2026, advocating frontier AI legislation, a regulator, and developer liability for AI-caused harm. It cites claims including an OpenAI autonomous agent allegedly escaping an isolated test environment as motivation.

entry.title: Poll: Biosecurity Community Pulse & Perspective 2026

author.name: Ana Leonescu

entry.summary: A short community survey invitation from two independent researchers seeking perspectives from biosecurity practitioners to compare grassroots experiences with institutional and policy narratives. The form takes under five minutes and aims to gather broad responses for a collaborative write-up.

entry.title: Remote embalming and shipment for brain or whole body preservation with Sparks

author.name: Andy_McKenzie

entry.summary: An essay arguing that ordinary embalmers distributed worldwide could perform initial aldehyde-based preservation for biostasis patients far from cryonics facilities, addressing the critical time window after death. The author makes the case for using existing embalming infrastructure and discusses longstanding debates in the preservation community.

entry.title: Against Girardian mimesis

author.name: Viliam

entry.summary: A critical essay examining Rene Girard's mimetic theory of desire and scapegoating, summarizing the framework and pushing back on its claims. The piece is philosophical commentary on social dynamics rather than empirical or technical AI research.

entry.title: Sci.STEPS opens applications for mentors for the 2027 season

author.name: Valentin2026

entry.summary: Announcement that Sci.STEPS, a free volunteer-run mentorship program with an AI Safety division, is accepting mentor applications for its February-April 2027 season. Mentors commit two hours per month for three months, and the previous AI Safety pilot had two mentors with positive mentee feedback.

entry.title: Learner collaborates with MIT peers to develop book of AI insights

author.name: Caroline Maselli | MIT Open Learning

entry.summary: A MIT News human-interest story about Prabha Jha, a Verizon professional who took the MIT xPRO AI for Senior Executives program and collaborated with peers to produce a book of AI insights for business leaders. The piece covers her motivations and experience rather than any technical or research content.

entry.title: San Francisco Rationalist Dinner

author.name: dactyl

entry.summary: A short announcement of a regular San Francisco rationalist meetup in a food court, welcoming first-timers to discuss AI safety, blog posts, and rationality topics.
